# @motifx-community/ui

> UI components for MotifJS (@motifx/core) on the MotifJS design system. Version 0.1.0-beta.2: a preview, its API may still change before 1.0.

Built on MotifJS (`@motifx/core`): a component is an object, made in JSX or with `new`, whose every prop takes a value or a function (`Bind<T>`); `x-model` binds a value two-way. The look is the design system’s (`@motifx-community/design-system`): five design languages (`data-identity`), light and dark themes, density.

## Start

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, set up Vite, styles, design languages, the kit’s languages

# Getting started

> `@motifx-community/ui` is a **preview** (`beta`): it is complete enough to build with, and its API may still change
> before 1.0. Install it with the `beta` tag; `@motifx/core` and its compiler with `next`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @motifx/core@next @motifx-community/ui@beta @motifx-community/design-system@beta @motifx-community/data@beta @motifx-community/i18n@beta
npm i -D @motifx/compiler@next vite typescript
```

`exceljs` (the grid's Excel export, `@motifx-community/ui/excel`) and `jspdf` (`@motifx-community/ui/pdf`) are optional: install
them only when you import those entries.

## Set up Vite and TypeScript

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import compiler from '@motifx/compiler';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [compiler()],
  resolve: { extensions: ['.tsx', '.ts', '.jsx', '.js'], dedupe: ['@motifx/core'] },
  // The kit's styles use :dir(), :has() and relative colours: build CSS for the browsers it supports.
  build: { cssTarget: ['chrome120', 'edge120', 'firefox128', 'safari18'] },
});
```

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json (the keys that matter)
{ "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "preserve", "target": "ES2021", "module": "esnext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "useDefineForClassFields": true, "strict": true } }
```

## Styles, design languages, themes

```ts
// main.tsx
import '@motifx-community/ui/styles.css'; // the design system first, then the kit
import { Application } from '@motifx/core';
import { App } from './App';

Application.CreateBuilder().build().run('#app', new App());
```

The look comes from the design system. Choose a design language and a theme on `<html>` (or on any element, for that
part of the page):

```html
<html data-identity="material" data-theme="dark" data-density="compact">
```

- `data-identity`: `tactile` (the default, without the attribute), `lounge`, `material`, `fluent`, `lilac`.
- `data-theme`: `light`, `dark`, `high-contrast`; without it the system's preference.
- `data-density`: `compact`; without it the regular one.

Restyle by overriding design-system tokens (`--mx-*`) after the kit's stylesheet, e.g. `:root { --mx-color-accent-solid: #8764b8; }`.

## The kit's language

The texts the components write themselves (buttons, messages, screen-reader names) and their numbers and dates follow
`uiLocale`. English and Turkish ship with the kit; `uiLocale.use('tr')` loads the Turkish pack and every component
draws again, live.

```ts
import { uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
await uiLocale.use('tr');
uiLocale.add('de', { ok: 'OK', cancel: 'Abbrechen' /* … */ });
```

With `@motifx-community/i18n` for the app's own texts, `connectI18n(i18n)` keeps the kit on the app's language.

## How the components work

- A component is an object: write it in JSX (`<Button text="Save" />`) or make it with `new Button({ text: 'Save' })`, add it
  anywhere (`this.controls.add(button)`), change it later (`button.text = 'Saved'`).
- Every prop and property takes a value or a function (`Bind<T>`): `disabled={() => this.model.busy}` follows the state.
- `x-model` binds a value two-way: `<TextBox label="Name" x-model={() => this.form.name} />`.
- Events are `onX` props or properties that take a listener: `onValueChanged={(e) => …}`, `grid.onRowClick((e) => …)`;
  `e.byUser` tells a user's change from one made by code.
- A component added to another is its child and goes with it when it is disposed; add components with `controls.add`,
  never by putting their element into the page yourself.
- Your data is used as given: items, rows and values are not wrapped or copied.

```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export class App extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
  state = reactive({ name: '', saved: false });

  view() {
    return (
      <Stack gap="md">
        <TextBox label="&Name" x-model={() => this.state.name} required />
        <Button text="&Save" tone="accent" disabled={() => !this.state.name} onclick={() => (this.state.saved = true)} />
      </Stack>
    );
  }
}
```

Each component's page in `docs/` lists its props, properties, methods, events, keyboard, accessibility and design
tokens, with examples.

# @motifx-community/ui

> Get started · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Components for MotifJS that work the way desktop UI does — created when needed, shown anywhere, closed and disposed like windows — drawn from the MotifJS design system's tokens.

## Install

```tsx
npm i @motifx/core @motifx-community/ui

import { Button, Control, FocusContainer, addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## How the components work

- Every component is an object. Write it in JSX and bind it to state, or create it with `new` and add it wherever and whenever you need it — the developer using it decides, both ways are complete.

- Lifetime follows ownership: a component dies with the one it belongs to.

- Keyboard, focus and ARIA are part of every component, not extras.

## What ships today

The components are being written one at a time; Button is the first. Under them is the base they all build on: focus and the keyboard, and the shared parts a menu or a drop-down opens on.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`Button`](button.md) | Solid, outline and ghost in three tones and sizes, pressable; icon, `&` access key, toggle, busy; a menu or any content, from the whole button or with `split` from an arrow next to it. |
| `Popup`, `MenuList` | The shared parts: a surface above the page that follows its anchor and closes on Escape or a press outside, and a keyboard-driven list of commands. |
| [`Control`](control.md) | The base of every control: `text`, `enabled`, `visible`, `tabStop` and focus, the same from JSX and from code. |
| [`FocusContainer`, `addShortcut`](keyboard.md) | Tab order, the active control of a container, `&` access keys, shortcuts, and focus that never falls to the page when a control goes away. |

## Design system

The look comes from `@motifx-community/design-system`: its tokens, three themes, density, fonts and user-preference overrides. `styles.css` imports it first, then this kit's own layer (`mx.components`) adds the [component tokens](tokens.md) and the components. Nothing here is a color or a size of its own.

- Themes: light, dark and high contrast, switched with `data-theme`; the OS preference is the default. Every text/background pair is checked in the design system's build: WCAG AA, AAA in high contrast.

- Density: `data-density="compact"` shrinks every control, bar and title bar.

- RTL through logical properties.

```tsx
<html data-theme="dark" data-density="compact">

/* your accent, after styles.css: a design-system override restyles every component */
:root {
  --mx-color-accent-solid: #8764b8;
  --mx-color-accent-solid-hover: #9373c0;
  --mx-color-accent-solid-pressed: #7e5aaf;
  --mx-color-accent-fg: #5c2e91;
}
```

An order screen built with the kit, the way a MotifJS app is built: the state and the operations live in a model (`OrderModel`), the page binds to it. The customer list is a data source of 5,000 rows that answers like a server.

# Design tokens

> Get started · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Five layers. The first four — primitives, the design language's own scales, semantic tokens per theme, density — come from `@motifx-community/design-system` and are listed here for reference. The fifth, the component tokens, is this kit's own: a knob per component, each referencing a design-system token, written in `@layer mx.components`. Every design language gives every one of them its own value.

## Component ({componentDocs.length})

Source: `tokens/schema/*.json` (names and types) and `tokens/languages/<language>/*.json` (the values; listed here: Tactile's). Override one after `styles.css` to restyle every instance of that component; override the design-system token it references to restyle everything.

| Token | CSS variable | References | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access-key.underline-style` | `--mx-access-key-underline-style` | `` | `solid` |
| `access-key.underline-color` | `--mx-access-key-underline-color` | `` | `currentcolor` |
| `access-key.underline-thickness` | `--mx-access-key-underline-thickness` | `` | `auto` |
| `access-key.underline-offset` | `--mx-access-key-underline-offset` | `` | `auto` |
| `access-key.key.shown.text-decoration` | `--mx-access-key-key-shown-text-decoration` | `` | `underline` |
| `accordion.font-size.sm` | `--mx-accordion-font-size-sm` | `font.size.caption` | `0.75rem` |
| `accordion.font-size.md` | `--mx-accordion-font-size-md` | `font.size.body` | `0.875rem` |
| `accordion.font-size.lg` | `--mx-accordion-font-size-lg` | `font.size.body-large` | `1.125rem` |
| `accordion.line-height.sm` | `--mx-accordion-line-height-sm` | `font.line.caption` | `1rem` |
| `accordion.line-height.md` | `--mx-accordion-line-height-md` | `font.line.body` | `1.25rem` |
| `accordion.line-height.lg` | `--mx-accordion-line-height-lg` | `font.line.body-large` | `1.5rem` |
| `accordion.height.sm` | `--mx-accordion-height-sm` | `control.height.sm` | `1.5rem` |
| `accordion.height.md` | `--mx-accordion-height-md` | `control.height.md` | `2rem` |
| `accordion.height.lg` | `--mx-accordion-height-lg` | `control.height.lg` | `2.5rem` |
| `accordion.padding.sm` | `--mx-accordion-padding-sm` | `control.padding.sm` | `0.5rem` |
| `accordion.padding.md` | `--mx-accordion-padding-md` | `control.padding.md` | `0.6875rem` |

## Identity ({identity.length})

What a design language brings of its own: corner radii, shadows, type and motion. The names are the same in every language; `data-identity` picks whose values apply. Tactile, shown here, is the default.

| Token | Type | CSS variable | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius.none` | dimension | `--mx-radius-none` | `0px` |
| `radius.xs` | dimension | `--mx-radius-xs` | `0.25rem` |
| `radius.sm` | dimension | `--mx-radius-sm` | `0.25rem` |
| `radius.md` | dimension | `--mx-radius-md` | `0.375rem` |
| `radius.lg` | dimension | `--mx-radius-lg` | `0.625rem` |

| `space.4` | dimension | `--mx-space-4` | `1rem` |
| `space.5` | dimension | `--mx-space-5` | `1.25rem` |
| `space.6` | dimension | `--mx-space-6` | `1.5rem` |
| `space.8` | dimension | `--mx-space-8` | `2rem` |
| `space.10` | dimension | `--mx-space-10` | `2.5rem` |
| `space.12` | dimension | `--mx-space-12` | `3rem` |
| `space.16` | dimension | `--mx-space-16` | `4rem` |
| `icon.size.sm` | dimension | `--mx-icon-size-sm` | `0.75rem` |
| `icon.size.md` | dimension | `--mx-icon-size-md` | `1rem` |
| `icon.size.lg` | dimension | `--mx-icon-size-lg` | `1.25rem` |
| `border.width.1` | dimension | `--mx-border-width-1` | `1px` |
| `border.width.2` | dimension | `--mx-border-width-2` | `2px` |
| `opacity.disabled` | number | `--mx-opacity-disabled` | `0.5` |
| `z.dropdown` | number | `--mx-z-dropdown` | `1000` |
| `z.sticky` | number | `--mx-z-sticky` | `1100` |
| `z.window` | number | `--mx-z-window` | `1200` |
| `z.overlay` | number | `--mx-z-overlay` | `1300` |
| `z.toast` | number | `--mx-z-toast` | `1400` |

## Using token names in TS

```tsx
import { cssVar } from '@motifx-community/ui/tokens';

cssVar('color.accent.solid');  // 'var(--mx-color-accent-solid)' — a design-system token
// component tokens join as components bring them; names are typo-checked,
// and apps that need only the design system import cssVar from there
```

# Control

> Foundations · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

The base of every control in the package. It gives each one the same `text`, `enabled`, `visible` and `tabStop`, and the same focus methods, whether the control is written in JSX and bound to state or created with `new` and changed from code.

## Import

```tsx
import { Control, type ControlProps } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

Every component of the package ([Button](button.md), …) extends it; extend it for your own controls.

## From JSX and from code

Both ways are complete; the developer using the control decides.

```tsx
// JSX, bound to state
<Badge text="Unread" enabled={() => !this.state.busy} />

// code: create, add anywhere, change later
const unread = new Badge({ text: 'Unread' });
this.toolbar.controls.add(unread);
unread.enabled = false;
unread.text = 'Unread mail';
unread.text = () => `Unread (${this.mail.count})`; // a function is followed
```

`Badge` is the control written in [Writing a control](#own).

```tsx
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Buttons created with `new`, added to a container, and their text changed from code on a click. */
export default function AddFromCode() {
  let added = 0;
  let target: Stack | null = null;

  const addFromCode = () => {
    const b = new Button({ text: `Button ${++added}` });
    b.motif.on('click', () => (b.text = `${b.text} ✓`));
    target?.controls.add(b);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Add a button from code" onclick={addFromCode} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" ref={(c: Stack) => (target = c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## How a property gets its value

- A prop is a value or a function. A function of a reactive object (`enabled={() => !state.busy}`) keeps the property in step with it; this is how MotifJS keeps a prop live.

- Your data is used as you give it: the control never makes it reactive, never copies or changes it. Over plain data the function is read again when you call `reState()` on the control or on anything it sits in; you choose which kind of data to give.

- With `x-model` the model always shows the control's state: a change by the user, by your code (`ctrl.value = …`, `select()`, `show()`) or by a rule you gave (`decimals`, a mask, `min` / `max`) is written back to it.

- A property set from code takes the same: a function (`ctrl.enabled = () => !state.busy`) is bound in place of what was there and followed; a value (`ctrl.enabled = false`) drops what was bound, and from then on the code owns it.

- Every property is reactive to read: `{() => ctrl.text}` in JSX or a `bindings.watch` follows it, whichever way it changed.

- `x-wait` and `x-display` stay one-way: they show and hide from state, and nothing is written back. If the state must change when the control goes away, do it in `onDisposed`.

## Enabled

Disabling a control disables everything inside it — other controls and plain elements alike, as a disabled `<fieldset>` does for form fields — and enabling it puts every element back exactly as it was. An element that was disabled on its own stays disabled; content added while the control is disabled is disabled too; a change the app makes in the meantime (a bound `disabled`) is what gets restored. Disabled containers nest: an element stays disabled while any of them, or its own value, says so.

| What | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `Native controls` | `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `fieldset`, `optgroup`, `option` get `disabled`: the browser blocks them and announces the state. |
| `Other focusable elements` | Links, `[tabindex]`, `contenteditable`, `summary`, `iframe` get `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. |
| `Pointer input` | `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `click`, `dblclick`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu` are swallowed inside the disabled control, before any handler. |
| `The control itself` | Gets `data-disabled` for styling. |
| `Windows inside` | A `<dialog>` window opened inside a disabled control is not disabled: owned windows stay usable. |

If focus was inside, it moves to the next usable element in the same window (or the one before it) instead of falling to `<body>`.

```tsx
import { Button, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A panel disabled and enabled from code: everything inside follows, and the inner button keeps its own `enabled`. */
export default function EnabledPanel() {
  let panel: Panel | null = null;
  let inner: Button | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Toggle panel enabled" onclick={() => (panel!.enabled = !panel!.enabled)} />
      <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" class="ctl-panel" ref={(p: Panel) => (panel = p)}>
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <label>
            Name <input name="panel-name" />
          </label>
          <Button text="Inner button" ref={(b: Button) => (inner = b)} />
          <a href="#enabled">A link</a>
        </Stack>
      </Panel>
      <output>{() => (inner ? `Inner button: enabled ${inner.enabled}, isEnabled ${inner.isEnabled}` : '')}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Visible and TabStop

`visible` uses core `hide()` / `show()`: a hidden control leaves the page and comes back in place, with its state. If focus was inside, it moves on first. `tabStop = false` only skips the control on Tab.

## Focus

```tsx
if (!nameBox.focus()) saveButton.focus();
nameBox.canFocus;      // enabled, on the page, focusable
panel.focusWithin;   // focus is somewhere inside
```

Focus never falls to `<body>` because of a control: disabling, hiding, removing or disposing the focused part moves focus to the next usable element. Focus rings show only for keyboard use (`:focus-visible`). Tab order, access keys and shortcuts: [Keyboard and focus](keyboard.md).

## FocusContainer

A control that remembers which control inside it is active and is a scope for Tab; the package's windows, tab pages and document views will be ones. The outermost container of a page or window also runs the `tabIndex` order (see [Keyboard and focus](keyboard.md)).

```tsx
class CustomerEditor extends FocusContainer<HTMLDivElement> { … }

editor.activeControl;           // the control holding focus inside, reactive
editor.activeControl = nameBox; // focuses it
editor.restoreFocus();          // back to where focus was when it was last active
```

| Member | Type | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeControl` | `Control \| null` | read/write, reactive | The control inside that has (or last had) focus, as `document.activeElement` is for the page; a nested container counts as one. Setting it focuses that control. |
| `restoreFocus()` | `boolean` | method | Focus back to where it was the last time the container was active, else its active control, else the first in Tab order. |
| `cyclesTab` | `boolean` | protected getter | `true` keeps Tab inside the container. `false` by default; a modal window returns `true`. |

## Writing a control

Extend `Control`, set the root element, and render `text` (and your own properties) with `observeProperty`: no effect is created, the callback runs on every change.

```tsx
interface BadgeProps extends ControlProps {
  count?: Bind<number>;
}

class Badge extends Control<HTMLSpanElement, BadgeProps> {
  static override elementTag = 'span';

  constructor(props?: IBaseProp<BadgeProps>) {
    super(props);
    if (this.props.count !== undefined) this.bindProperty('count', this.props.count);
  }

  get count(): number { return this.getProperty<number>('count') ?? 0; }
  set count(value: number) { this.setProperty('count', value); }

  override onConfigured() {
    this.class.add('my-badge');
    this.observeProperty<string>('text', (t) => this.element.setAttribute('aria-label', t));
    this.observeProperty<number>('count', (n) => (this.element.textContent = String(n ?? 0)));
  }
}
```

| Member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `static elementTag` | The root element. `div` unless the subclass sets another (`button` for a button). |
| `focusElement` | Getter: the element that takes focus; the root by default. Composite controls override it. It runs from the constructor, so derive it from `this.element`. |
| `observeProperty(name, apply)` | Renders a property without an effect: `apply` runs now and on every change, from a getter prop or from code. |
| `getProperty(name) / setProperty(name, value)` | The storage behind the shared properties, for your own: tracked read, and set-from-code (which replaces a bound getter). |
| `bindProperty(name, prop)` | Binds one of your own props: a getter is read now and followed by a binding of the control (so `reState()` reads it again), a value is stored once. Call it from your constructor. |
| `applyProperty(name, value) / peekProperty(name)` | Render your own properties without an effect: override `applyProperty` (call `super`); read the current value untracked with `peekProperty`. Can run from the constructor: touch only `this.element`. |
| `setAccessKey(key)` | Declares the access key parsed from `&Text` (`parseAccessKey`): written to `aria-keyshortcuts` as `Alt+K`, which is how Alt+K finds the control. |

## Performance

The base adds no listeners per control and pays only for what is used.

| Case | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| `A property nobody set, bound or read` | Nothing: no storage, no DOM write, no binding. |
| `A plain value (`enabled={false}`, `new Badge({ text })`)` | Stored and written to the DOM once. |
| `A getter (`enabled={() => !state.busy}`)` | One binding for that property, stopped when the control is disposed or another value or function is set. |
| `Reading a property` | A small change counter, created the first time someone reads it. |
| `Setting from code` | A direct DOM write; readers are notified through the counter. |
| ``enabled = false`` | One pass over the control's subtree, plus one shared observer while anything is disabled (it disappears when nothing is). |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The control's text. Where it shows is up to the control: a button's caption, a form's title. |
| `enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` disables the control and everything inside it. See "Enabled". |
| `disabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The HTML-style inverse of `enabled`, for habit: `disabled={() => state.busy}`. Ignored when `enabled` is given. |
| `visible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` hides the control with core `hide()`; `true` shows it again with `show()`. |
| `tabStop` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` takes the control out of the Tab order; a click or `focus()` still focuses it. |
| `tabIndex` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | Order among the controls of the same container: Tab visits them in ascending order, ties in document order. Leave it unset where you can: document order is also the reading order of screen readers. See Keyboard and focus. |

### Properties

| Property | Type | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | read/write, reactive | Set from code with a value or a function, like the prop (see "How a property gets its value"). |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | This control's own value, as set or bound (like the HTML `disabled` attribute). |
| `isEnabled` | `boolean` | read-only, reactive | Whether it can be used now: enabled itself and in every control it sits in (like CSS `:enabled`). Windows shown inside do not inherit it. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | This control's own value; a hidden parent does not change it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | `!enabled`. |
| `tabIndex` | `number` | read/write, reactive | Position in the Tab order of its container. |
| `tabStop` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | Writes `tabindex="-1"` on the focus element while `false`, and puts back the element's own `tabindex` afterwards. |
| `parentControl` | `Control \| null` | read-only | The nearest ancestor that is a `Control`, not crossing a window. |
| `canFocus` | `boolean` | read-only | Enabled, on the page and focusable right now. |
| `focused` | `boolean` | read-only | Its focus element has focus. A DOM query, not reactive. |
| `focusWithin` | `boolean` | read-only | Focus is on it or anything inside it. A DOM query, not reactive. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focus()` | `boolean` | Focuses the control; `false` when it cannot take focus (`canFocus`). |
| `onAccessKey()` | `boolean` | What its access key (`&Save` → Alt+S, Control+Option+S on Apple platforms) does: focus; a button also clicks. Override it in your control. |
| `addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | A shortcut active while focus is inside this control, removed when it is disposed. See Keyboard and focus. |

## Not yet

- Arrow keys inside composite controls (one Tab stop, arrows inside): with the first composite control.

# Keyboard and focus

> Foundations · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

The rules every control follows: Tab order, the active control of a container, focus that never falls to `<body>`, `&File` access keys and app-wide shortcuts.

## The rules

| Rule | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab navigation` | Every control is a Tab stop unless `tabStop = false`; `tabIndex` orders the controls of a container. |
| `Active control` | Containers (`FocusContainer`) track `activeControl` and put focus back with `restoreFocus()` when they become active again. |
| `Composite controls` | One Tab stop, arrow keys inside (roving tabindex or `aria-activedescendant`): with the first composite control. |
| `Focus never on <body>` | Disabling, hiding, removing or disposing the focused part of a control moves focus to the next usable element. |
| `Focus ring` | Only for keyboard use (`:focus-visible`), the design system's double ring. |
| `Access keys` | `&Save` in a control text: Alt+S. Underlined while Alt is held. |
| `Shortcuts` | `addShortcut('Ctrl+S', …)` app-wide, or scoped to a control. |

## Tab order

Give controls a `tabIndex` and the outermost container of the page or window visits them in ascending order at each level of the control tree; equal indexes (and plain elements, index 0) go in document order. Until a control inside sets a `tabIndex`, Tab is left to the browser. A modal window keeps Tab inside itself; one radio button per group is a stop, as in browsers.

```tsx
import { Button, FocusContainer, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A container of your own: it runs the Tab order of its controls and remembers the active one. */
class CustomerEditor extends FocusContainer<HTMLDivElement> {}

/** Tab visits the buttons by `tabIndex`; the container reports its `activeControl` and puts focus back with `restoreFocus()`. */
export default function TabOrder() {
  let editor: CustomerEditor | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <CustomerEditor ref={(c: CustomerEditor) => (editor = c)}>
        <Panel variant="outline" padding="md">
          <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button text="Third" tabIndex={3} />
            <Button text="First" tabIndex={1} />
            <Button text="Second" tabIndex={2} />
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
      </CustomerEditor>
      <span>
        activeControl: <output class="active-name">{() => editor?.activeControl?.text ?? '—'}</output>
      </span>
      <Button text="restoreFocus()" onclick={() => editor?.restoreFocus()} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Active control

A `FocusContainer` knows which control inside holds focus (`activeControl`, reactive) and puts focus back there with `restoreFocus()`: a window coming to the front, a tab page coming back.

## Access keys

```tsx
<Button text="&Save" onclick={save} />    // Alt+S
<Button text="Save &as…" onclick={saveAs} /> // Alt+A
<Button text="Tom && Jerry" />             // a literal &
<input aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+N" />        // plain elements too
```

| Topic | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `Marker` | `&` before a letter: `&Save`, `Save &as…`. `&&` is a literal ampersand. Only the first marker counts. |
| `Keys` | Alt + the key; on Apple platforms Control + Option + the key, because Option alone types characters there (browsers use the same keys for HTML `accesskey`). |
| `What it does` | The key activates the control: a button is focused and clicked (as HTML `accesskey` does), another control is focused (`onAccessKey()`). |
| `Several with the same key` | Each press moves focus to the next one, activating none. |
| `Where` | The modal window while one is open, else the window holding focus, else the page outside windows. Disabled and hidden controls are skipped. |
| `AltGr` | Ignored: AltGr (Ctrl+Alt on Windows) types characters such as `@` on a Turkish keyboard. |
| `Underline` | Shown while Alt is held (Control + Option on Apple platforms). Tapping Alt (press and release) keeps it shown until Alt is tapped again, another key is pressed or the pointer is used; while the page has access keys, that tap is kept from the browser, which would otherwise move keyboard focus to its menu bar. `data-mx-access-keys="always"` on `<html>` shows it all the time. |
| `Accessibility` | The accessible name is the plain text; the control gets `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+S"` (`"Control+Alt+S"` on Apple platforms). |
| `Plain elements` | Any element with `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+N"` takes part: a button-like one is clicked, an input focused, a `<label>` focuses its field. |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** `&` in a button text: Alt+S saves, Alt+O opens, Alt+P exports. */
export default function AccessKeys() {
  const s = reactive({ saves: 0, opens: 0, exports: 0 });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="&Save" onclick={() => s.saves++} />
      <Button text="&Open" onclick={() => s.opens++} />
      <Button text="Ex&port" onclick={() => s.exports++} />
      <span>
        Saved <output class="saves">{() => s.saves}</output> · opened <output class="opens">{() => s.opens}</output> · exported{' '}
        <output>{() => s.exports}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

Browsers keep a few Alt combinations for their own menus, and they differ per browser and language; test the keys you choose.

## Shortcuts

```tsx
import { addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const remove = addShortcut('Mod+S', () => model.save()); // app-wide
grid.addShortcut('Delete', () => grid.deleteSelected()); // while focus is in the grid
addShortcut('F2', () => rename(), { scope: tree });
```

### Chords

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl / Control` | The Ctrl key. |
| `Alt / Option` | The Alt key (Option on a Mac). |
| `Shift` | The Shift key. |
| `Meta / Cmd / Win` | The Windows key, Cmd on a Mac. |
| `Mod` | Cmd on Apple platforms, Ctrl elsewhere: `Mod+S` saves everywhere. |
| `keys` | A character (`S`, `1`, `/`), or a `KeyboardEvent.key` name: `Enter`, `Escape` (`Esc`), `Delete` (`Del`), `F2`, `ArrowUp` (`Up`), `Space`, `Plus`… Case does not matter; `Ctrl++` is Ctrl and plus. |

### Which shortcut runs

| Rule | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `Most specific first` | Shortcuts scoped to the controls holding focus run first, the innermost one first; app-wide ones last. A handler that returns `false` passes the key on. |
| `Modal windows` | While a modal window is open, only shortcuts scoped inside it run; app-wide ones are silent. |
| `Windows` | App-wide shortcuts without Ctrl, Alt or Meta (Delete, Escape, a letter) do not run while focus is in a window: those keys belong to the window. Chords with a modifier and F-keys still do. |
| `Text fields` | A chord without Ctrl, Alt or Meta leaves text fields alone (Delete deletes text) unless `inEditable: true`. F-keys and chords with a modifier work everywhere. |
| `Disabled scope` | A shortcut scoped to a disabled control does not run. |
| `Handled` | The key gets `preventDefault()` and stops there. Shortcuts run before access keys: an explicit chord wins over an implicit key. |

```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An app-wide shortcut, Mod+K, registered for as long as this component lives. */
export default class Shortcut extends Component {
  private readonly s = reactive({ palette: 0 });

  override onConfigured(): void {
    this.motif.setDisposable(addShortcut('Mod+K', () => void this.s.palette++));
  }

  override view() {
    return (
      <span>
        This page registers <kbd>Mod+K</kbd> (Ctrl+K, Cmd+K on a Mac). Pressed <output class="palette">{() => this.s.palette}</output> times.
      </span>
    );
  }
}
```

## Focus never on &lt;body&gt;

When the focused part of a control is disabled, hidden, removed (a list row, a branch) or disposed, focus moves to the next usable element from that spot in the same window, else the one before it. A click on an empty spot still clears focus as usual, and route changes are left to the router.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Removing the row that holds focus moves focus to the next row, not to `<body>`. */
export default function FocusGuard() {
  const s = reactive({ items: [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }, { id: 4 }] });
  return (
    <>
      {s.items.map((item) => (
        <Stack key={item.id} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <span>Row {item.id}</span>
          <Button text={`Remove row ${item.id}`} onclick={() => s.items.splice(s.items.indexOf(item), 1)} />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## API reference

| Member | Returns / kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | Registers a shortcut; returns the remover. `options.scope`: a component; `options.inEditable`: also in text fields. |
| `control.addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | The same, scoped to the control and removed when it is disposed. |
| `parseAccessKey(text)` | `{ text, key, index }` | Parses `&Text` for your own controls; render with the `mx-access-key` class and call `setAccessKey(key)`. |
| `tabIndex` | prop / property | Order inside the container; default 0. |
| `activeControl / restoreFocus()` | FocusContainer | See the Control page. |

Controls: see `Control` for `tabStop`, `tabIndex`, `focus()`, `onAccessKey()` and `FocusContainer`.
