# Tooltip

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A short description shown next to an element: after the pointer rests on it, when it gets keyboard focus, or from code. It can be hovered, Escape hides it, and one is open at a time on the page.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tooltip, addTooltip, type TooltipShowOn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

In JSX a tooltip is placed anywhere and pointed at its `target`; where it sits does not matter. From code, `new Tooltip({ target, text })` needs nothing else: it puts itself into the page when it first shows, and goes when its target component does.

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A tooltip from JSX pointed at its target, and one created with `new` and opened from code. */
export default function FromCode() {
  let save: Button | null = null;
  let target: Button | null = null;
  let tip: Tooltip | null = null;
  let opened = 0;

  const openFromCode = () => {
    if (!target) return;
    if (!tip) {
      tip = new Tooltip({ target });
      tip.placement = 'end';
    }
    tip.text = `Made from code, opened ${++opened} time(s)`;
    tip.open();
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (save = b)} text="Save" tone="accent" />
      <Tooltip target={() => save} text="Save the file (Ctrl+S)" />
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (target = b)} text="Target" variant="outline" />
      <Button text="Open a tooltip from code" variant="outline" onclick={openFromCode} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Icon-only buttons

A button with only an icon needs its own name (`aria-label`); the tooltip shows it to sighted users and adds the shortcut as a description. Moving from one button to the next shows the next tooltip at once.

```tsx
import { Button, Stack, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const BoldIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M4.5 2.5h4.25a2.75 2.75 0 0 1 0 5.5H4.5zM4.5 8h5a2.75 2.75 0 0 1 0 5.5h-5z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linejoin="round" />
  </svg>
);

const ItalicIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M7 2.5h5M4 13.5h5M9.5 2.5l-3 11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  </svg>
);

const LinkIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M6.5 9.5l3-3M7 4.5l1-1a2.83 2.83 0 0 1 4 4l-1 1M9 11.5l-1 1a2.83 2.83 0 0 1-4-4l1-1" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  </svg>
);

/** Icon-only buttons named with aria-label; the tooltips show the name and the shortcut. */
export default function IconButtons() {
  let bold: Button | null = null;
  let italic: Button | null = null;
  let link: Button | null = null;
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="toolbar" aria-label="Text style">
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (bold = b)} icon={() => <BoldIcon />} variant="ghost" aria-label="Bold" />
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (italic = b)} icon={() => <ItalicIcon />} variant="ghost" aria-label="Italic" />
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (link = b)} icon={() => <LinkIcon />} variant="ghost" aria-label="Link" />
      <Tooltip target={() => bold} text="Bold (Ctrl+B)" />
      <Tooltip target={() => italic} text="Italic (Ctrl+I)" />
      <Tooltip target={() => link} text="Insert a link (Ctrl+K)" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## On a field

On a TextBox the whole field shows it on hover, and its input is described by it while it shows, also on keyboard focus.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { TextBox, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A tooltip on a TextBox: the field shows it on hover, its input is described by it. */
export default function OnField() {
  const s = reactive({ email: '' });
  let email: TextBox | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <TextBox ref={(b: TextBox) => (email = b)} label="Email" type="email" x-model={() => s.email} />
      <Tooltip target={() => email} text="We send the receipt here." placement="end" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Placement

`top` by default. It opens on the other side when there is no room, and `start` / `end` follow the reading direction (try the RTL switch at the top).

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, Tooltip, type PopupPlacement } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLACEMENTS: PopupPlacement[] = ['top', 'bottom', 'start', 'end', 'top-start', 'bottom-end'];

/** The side the tooltip opens on, picked from the buttons. */
export default function Placement() {
  const s = reactive({ placement: 'top' as PopupPlacement });
  let target: Button | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Placement">
        {PLACEMENTS.map((placement) => (
          <Button
            key={placement}
            text={placement}
            size="sm"
            variant={() => (s.placement === placement ? 'solid' : 'ghost')}
            aria-pressed={() => s.placement === placement}
            onclick={() => (s.placement = placement)}
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button ref={(b: Button) => (target = b)} text="Hover or focus me" variant="outline" />
        <Tooltip target={() => target} text={() => `Opens at ${s.placement}`} placement={() => s.placement} />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Delay

The pointer rests `delay` milliseconds on the target before it shows (500 by default); `hideDelay` keeps it a moment after the pointer leaves. Right after one closed, the next shows at once (`Tooltip.skipDelay`).

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const DELAYS = [0, 500, 1500];

/** Three tooltips that wait a different time before they show. */
export default function Delay() {
  const targets: Button[] = [];
  return (
    <>
      {DELAYS.map((delay, i) => (
        <span key={delay}>
          <Button ref={(b: Button) => (targets[i] = b)} text={`delay ${delay}`} variant="outline" />
          <Tooltip target={() => targets[i]} text={`Shown after ${delay} ms`} delay={delay} />
        </span>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Rich content

JSX children or `content` (any component) come after the text. Keep it short and never put buttons or links in it: a tooltip cannot take focus.

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A tooltip with markup after its text, given as JSX children. */
export default function RichContent() {
  let target: Button | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (target = b)} text="Rich tooltip" variant="outline" />
      <Tooltip target={() => target}>
        <strong>Bold</strong> makes the selection stand out. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>
      </Tooltip>
    </>
  );
}
```

## When it shows

`showOn` picks what shows it: `hover-focus` (default), `focus` (keyboard focus only) or `manual` (only `open()` / `opened`). `enabled` turns a tooltip off.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Tooltip } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A tooltip opened only from code, and one shown on keyboard focus while a toggle allows it. */
export default function ShowOn() {
  const s = reactive({ on: true });
  let help: Button | null = null;
  let tip: Tooltip | null = null;
  let keyboardOnly: Button | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (help = b)} text="Help" variant="outline" />
      <Tooltip ref={(t: Tooltip) => (tip = t)} target={() => help} text="Shown from code" showOn="manual" placement="bottom" />
      <Button text={() => (tip?.opened ? 'Hide it' : 'Show it')} onclick={() => tip && (tip.opened = !tip.opened)} />
      <Button text={() => (s.on ? 'Tooltips on' : 'Tooltips off')} toggle x-model={() => s.on} variant="ghost" />
      <Button ref={(b: Button) => (keyboardOnly = b)} text="Keyboard only" variant="outline" />
      <Tooltip target={() => keyboardOnly} text="Shown on keyboard focus, while the toggle is on" enabled={() => s.on} showOn="focus" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Many elements

`addTooltip(target, text)` gives an element a tooltip that is made only when it is first needed; every tooltip on the page shares one set of document listeners, so hundreds of them cost next to nothing. It returns the function that removes it.

```tsx
import { addTooltip, Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SEATS = ['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6'].flatMap((row) =>
  ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'].map((letter) => ({
    id: `${row}${letter}`,
    note: `Row ${row}, seat ${letter}: ${letter === 'A' || letter === 'D' ? 'window' : 'aisle'}${row === '1' ? ', extra legroom' : ''}`,
  })),
);

/** A tooltip on each of 24 seats, made only when first needed, and one that is removed from code. */
export default function ManyElements() {
  let removeGuideTip = () => {};
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Seats">
        {SEATS.map((seat) => (
          <Button
            key={seat.id}
            ref={(b: Button) => {
              addTooltip(b, seat.note);
            }}
            text={seat.id}
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button
          ref={(b: Button) => (removeGuideTip = addTooltip(b, { text: 'Opens the guide', placement: 'end' }))}
          text="Guide"
          variant="outline"
        />
        <Button text="Remove the guide's tooltip" variant="ghost" onclick={() => removeGuideTip()} />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab (focus on the target)` | Shows it at once; leaving the target hides it. |
| `Escape` | Hides it; focus stays where it is. Only the tooltip closes, not the window around it. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Role` | `role="tooltip"`, one element per tooltip. |
| `Description` | While it is shown the target (its focusable part, e.g. the input of a TextBox) has `aria-describedby` pointing to it, next to its own descriptions. |
| `Focus` | It never takes focus and holds nothing interactive. For buttons or links next to an element, open a drop-down (Button `dropDown`). |
| `WCAG 1.4.13` | Dismissible (Escape), hoverable (the pointer can move onto it) and persistent (it stays until the pointer or focus leaves). |
| `Pointer only?` | Never: whatever it says must also be reachable without it. An icon-only button still needs its own name (`aria-label`). |
| `Touch` | A touch does not show it; give touch users the information another way. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-tooltip` | The tooltip. `data-side` tells the side it opened on (`top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`). |
| `.mx-tooltip__text` | The text. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `tooltip.offset, tooltip.enter-offset` | The gap to its target, and how far it comes in from it. |
| `tooltip.surface` | Unit: the tooltip with its box (`max-width`: the widest it gets before it wraps; `rich`: with content of its own). |
| `tooltip.arrow, tooltip.text` | Units: an arrow towards the target a design may show, and the text. |
| `tooltip.text-align` | How its text lines up. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `Bind<Element \| ComponentBase \| null>` | — | What it describes. A function is fine for a component that comes later in the view (`() => this.save`). |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What it says. |
| `content` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | — | Any content after the text, made the first time it shows. JSX children work too. Nothing interactive. |
| `placement` | `Bind<PopupPlacement>` | `'top'` | `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`, each with `-start` / `-end`. It opens on the other side when there is no room; start and end follow the reading direction. |
| `delay` | `Bind<number>` | `500` | Milliseconds the pointer rests on the target before it shows. Keyboard focus shows it at once. |
| `hideDelay` | `Bind<number>` | `150` | Milliseconds it stays after the pointer leaves, so the pointer can move onto it. |
| `showOn` | `Bind<TooltipShowOn>` | `'hover-focus'` | `hover-focus`, `focus` (keyboard focus only), `manual` (only `open()`). |
| `enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false`: it never shows, and closes if it is open. |
| `onOpened, onClosed` | `() => void` | — | See Events. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write, reactive | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `opened` | read/write, reactive | Whether it is shown; setting it opens or closes it. |
| `Tooltip.skipDelay` | static, read/write | Milliseconds after a tooltip closes during which the next one shows at once (default `300`; `0` turns it off). |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open()` | `boolean` | Shows it now, whatever `showOn` says; `false` without a target on the page, or when disabled. |
| `close()` | `void` | Hides it. |
| `place()` | `void` | Lines it up with its target again, e.g. after the target moved. |
| `addTooltip(target, text \| options)` | `() => void` | A tooltip for one element, made on first use; returns the function that removes it. For a component it goes with the component. |

### Events

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `onOpened` | It was shown. |
| `onClosed` | It was hidden. |


---

# Popover

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Content next to the element it belongs to: a title, a close button, a form, a card. It opens on a press or while the pointer rests on its target, follows it, and points at it with an arrow where the design language has one.

## Import

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

The JSX children are the content; `target` names the element or component it opens next to. From code, `content` gives the content and `open()`, `close()` and `toggle()` move it; `value` and `x-model` say whether it is open.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Popover, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A popover with a title, a close button and a small form; one made from code for a plain element. */
export default function Basic() {
    const s = reactive({ open: false, name: 'Ada', saved: '' });
    let button!: Button;
    let link!: HTMLElement;
    const coded = new Popover({ title: 'From code', content: new Button({ text: 'OK', variant: 'outline', onclick: () => coded.close() }) });

    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button ref={(b: Button) => (button = b)} text="Rename" variant="outline" />
            <Popover target={() => button} title="New name" showClose x-model={() => s.open}>
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <TextBox label="Name" x-model={() => s.name} />
                    <Button text="Save" tone="accent" onclick={() => ((s.saved = s.name), (s.open = false))} />
                </Stack>
            </Popover>
            <output class="po-saved">{() => (s.saved ? `Saved: ${s.saved}` : s.open ? 'Open' : 'Closed')}</output>
            <a
                href="#from-code"
                class="po-link"
                ref={(c: { element: HTMLElement }) => (link = c.element)}
                onclick={(e: Event) => {
                    e.preventDefault();
                    coded.target = link;
                    coded.toggle();
                }}
            >
                A popover from code
            </a>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## While the pointer rests

`showOn: 'hover'` opens it after `delay` while the pointer rests on the target, and when the target has keyboard focus; the pointer may move onto the popover. It closes `hideDelay` after the pointer leaves both.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Popover, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A card that opens while the pointer rests on a name, or when the name has keyboard focus. */
export default function Hover() {
    let name!: HTMLElement;
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <span>
                Reviewed by{' '}
                <a href="#ada" class="po-person" ref={(c: { element: HTMLElement }) => (name = c.element)} onclick={(e: Event) => e.preventDefault()}>
                    Ada Lovelace
                </a>
            </span>
            <Popover target={() => name} showOn="hover" placement="top" label="Ada Lovelace">
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" align="center">
                    <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" size="lg" />
                    <Stack>
                        <strong>Ada Lovelace</strong>
                        <span>Analytical Engine, Programs</span>
                    </Stack>
                </Stack>
            </Popover>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Placements, the arrow and a width

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, Popover, Stack, type PopupPlacement } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLACEMENTS: PopupPlacement[] = ['top-start', 'top', 'top-end', 'start', 'end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom', 'bottom-end'];

/** Every placement; the arrow where the language draws one, and a width of its own. */
export default function Placements() {
    const s = reactive({ arrow: true, placement: 'bottom' as PopupPlacement });
    let button!: Button;
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                {PLACEMENTS.map(placement => (
                    <Button key={placement} text={placement} variant={() => (s.placement === placement ? 'solid' : 'outline')} size="sm" onclick={() => (s.placement = placement)} />
                ))}
                <CheckBox label="Arrow" x-model={() => s.arrow} />
            </Stack>
            <div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; padding: 3rem 0">
                <Button ref={(b: Button) => (button = b)} text="Open" />
            </div>
            <Popover target={() => button} placement={() => s.placement} arrow={() => s.arrow} width="16rem" label="Placement">
                <p>{() => `Placed at ${s.placement}; it moves to the other side when there is no room.`}</p>
            </Popover>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keeping it open

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Popover, Stack, TextArea } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A press outside does not close it, and onClosing keeps it open while there is unsaved text; Escape and the button close it. */
export default function Events() {
    const s = reactive({ note: '', told: '' });
    let button!: Button;
    let pop!: Popover;
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button ref={(b: Button) => (button = b)} text="Add a note" variant="outline" />
            <Popover
                ref={(p: Popover) => (pop = p)}
                target={() => button}
                title="Note"
                closeOnOutside={false}
                onClosing={e => {
                    if (e.reason === 'escape' && s.note.trim() !== '') {
                        e.cancel = true;
                        s.told = 'Save or clear the note first.';
                    }
                }}
                onClosed={reason => (s.told = `Closed: ${String(reason)}`)}
            >
                <Stack gap="sm">
                    <TextArea label="Text" x-model={() => s.note} rows={3} />
                    <Button text="Save" tone="accent" onclick={() => ((s.note = ''), pop.close())} />
                </Stack>
            </Popover>
            <output class="po-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Behaviour

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Opening` | By a press on the target, by the pointer resting on it (`hover`), or from code. It appears in the browser’s top layer, next to the target, and follows it while the page scrolls. |
| `Focus` | Opened by a press or from code, focus moves to the first focusable part inside, else to the popover; it goes back to the target when the popover closes. Opened by hover, focus stays where it is. |
| `Closing` | Escape, a press outside it and its target, focus leaving both (Tab out), the close button, the target pressed again, or the pointer leaving both (`hover`). `onClosing` may keep it open. |
| `Placement` | `placement` names the side and the alignment, as for the kit’s popups; without room on that side it opens on the other. |
| `Where it lives` | Made from code, it goes into the nearest container of its target that can hold it, so it stays in the target’s window and landmark. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Role` | `dialog`, named by its title, else by `label`: give it one. |
| `Target` | `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`; `aria-haspopup="dialog"` when a press opens it. |
| `Keyboard` | Tab moves through the content and out (which closes it); Escape closes and returns focus. A `hover` popover opens on keyboard focus too. |
| `Arrow` | Decorative. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-popover` | The popover. `data-side` (`top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`), `data-arrow`. |
| `.mx-popover__arrow` | The arrow. |
| `.mx-popover__header, .mx-popover__title, .mx-popover__close` | The header, its title and the close button. |
| `.mx-popover__body` | The content. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `popover.surface, .arrow, .header, .title, .body` | Units: the surface (`focus`), the arrow (`display`, `size`, its fill and frame), the header, the title and the body. |
| `popover.close` | Place: the close button’s look (`variant`). |
| `popover.offset, .enter-offset, .header-gap` | The gap to the target, how far it comes in as it appears, the space between title and close button. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `Bind<Element \| ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | The element or component it opens next to. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A title in the header. The same property as `text`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers call it when it has no title. |
| `content` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | Content from code, after the JSX children. |
| `showOn` | `Bind<PopoverShowOn>` | `'click'` | `click`: a press on the target toggles it; `hover`: the pointer resting on the target, or keyboard focus on it; `manual`: only code. |
| `placement` | `Bind<PopupPlacement>` | `'bottom'` | The side and the alignment; it opens on the other side when there is no room. |
| `arrow` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | An arrow towards the target, where the design language draws one. |
| `showClose` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A close button in the header. |
| `width` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | `null` | A width of its own (a CSS length, or pixels). |
| `closeOnOutside` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A press outside it and its target closes it. |
| `delay, hideDelay` | `Bind<number>` | `300`, `200` | Milliseconds the pointer rests on the target before it opens, and it stays after the pointer leaves both (`showOn: 'hover'`). |
| `value` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Open or not; `x-model` binds it two-way. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onOpened` | event | It opened. |
| `onClosing` | event | About to close (`reason`); `cancel = true` keeps it open. |
| `onClosed` | event | It closed, with the reason: `escape`, `outside`, `focus`, `toggle`, `hover`, `close-button`, `code`. |
| `open(), close(reason?), toggle()` | `boolean` / `void` | From code; `open()` is `false` without a target on the page or when disabled. |
| `place()` | `void` | Lines it up with its target again, after its content changed size. |
| `isOpen` | read-only | Whether it is open now. |
| `closeButton, body` | read-only | The close button (the kit’s) and the part that holds the content. |


---

# LoadPanel

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A “loading” layer over a container or the whole page: a shade, a pane with the kit’s spinner and a message, a Cancel button when the work can be stopped. Nothing under it can be used meanwhile, and focus comes back afterwards.

## Import

```tsx
import { LoadPanel } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Over a container

`target` names the component or element it covers; `value` (or `x-model`) shows and hides it, `show()` and `hide()` from code. `delay` keeps quick work from flashing it.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Panel, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A load panel over a panel while its orders load: bound with x-model, shown after a short delay. */
export default function Container() {
    const s = reactive({ loading: false, result: '' });
    let panel!: Panel;

    // Stands in for a call to the server.
    const load = () => {
        s.loading = true;
        s.result = '';
        setTimeout(() => {
            s.loading = false;
            s.result = 'Orders loaded.';
        }, 1800);
    };

    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Panel class="lp-panel" variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-block-size: 10rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (panel = c)}>
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <TextBox label="Customer" value="Ada" />
                    <Button text="Load orders" tone="accent" onclick={load} />
                </Stack>
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => panel} message="Loading orders" delay={200} x-model={() => s.loading} />
            <output class="lp-result">{() => s.result}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Over the page, with Cancel

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Over the whole page, with a Cancel button: the work stops when it is pressed (or on Escape). */
export default function Page() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    const panel = new LoadPanel({
        message: 'Building the report…',
        cancelable: true,
        onCancel: () => {
            if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
            timer = null;
            s.told = 'Cancelled.';
        }
    });
    const start = () => {
        s.told = '';
        panel.show();
        timer = setTimeout(() => {
            timer = null;
            panel.hide();
            s.told = 'The report is ready.';
        }, 4000);
    };
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button text="Build the report" variant="outline" onclick={start} />
            <span onConfig={c => c.controls.add(panel)} />
            <output class="lp-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Shade, pane and indicator

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Without the shade, without the pane, without the indicator; a press on the shade may hide it. */
export default function Options() {
    const s = reactive({ clear: false, bare: false, words: false });
    let clear!: Panel;
    let bare!: Panel;
    let words!: Panel;
    const flash = (key: 'clear' | 'bare' | 'words') => {
        s[key] = true;
        setTimeout(() => (s[key] = false), 2500);
    };
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (clear = c)}>
                <Button text="No shade" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('clear')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => clear} shade={false} x-model={() => s.clear} closeOnOutside />
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (bare = c)}>
                <Button text="No pane" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('bare')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => bare} showPane={false} x-model={() => s.bare} />
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (words = c)}>
                <Button text="Words only" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('words')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => words} showIndicator={false} message="Please wait" x-model={() => s.words} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Behaviour

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Over a container` | It goes inside the container, over everything in it; the container is `aria-busy` and what is under the panel is inert: nothing there can be pressed or focused. |
| `Over the page` | Without a `target`, it covers the viewport and the rest of the page is inert. |
| `Focus` | Focus that was under it waits on the panel (on the Cancel button when there is one) and goes back where it was when the panel hides. |
| `Delay` | Quick work shows nothing: it comes after `delay`, and a hide before that cancels it. |
| `Spinner.cover` | The kit’s spinner covers a container from code in one call (`Spinner.cover`); the load panel is the component with the pane, the message, the delay and the button. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Pane` | A `status` region: the message is read when the panel appears, and again when it changes. |
| `Indicator` | Decorative; the message says what is going on. |
| `Under it` | `inert` and `aria-busy`, so readers skip it and nothing there takes a press or focus. |
| `Cancel` | The kit’s button, named in the kit language; Escape presses it. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-load-panel` | The layer. `data-shade`, `data-pane`, `data-page`. |
| `.mx-load-panel__pane` | The pane. |
| `.mx-load-panel__indicator, .mx-load-panel__message, .mx-load-panel__cancel` | The spinner, the message and the button. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `load-panel.shade, .pane, .message` | Units: the layer (`shaded`), the pane (`shown`), the message. |
| `load-panel.cancel` | Place: the Cancel button’s look (`variant`). |
| `load-panel.padding, .gap` | The least space to the edge of what it covers; the space between the indicator, the message and the button. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| HTMLElement \| null>` | `null` | What it covers: a component or an element; `null` covers the whole page. |
| `message` | `Bind<string>` | the kit’s “Loading…” | The message under the indicator. The same property as `text`. |
| `value` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Shown or not; `x-model` binds it two-way. |
| `delay` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | Milliseconds before it shows; a hide before that shows nothing. |
| `shade` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Dims what it covers. |
| `showPane` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The box behind the indicator and the message. |
| `showIndicator` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The turning indicator (the kit’s spinner). |
| `cancelable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A Cancel button in the pane; Escape presses it too. |
| `cancelText` | `Bind<string>` | the kit’s “Cancel” | The button’s text. |
| `closeOnOutside` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A press on the shade hides it. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onShown, onHidden` | event | It came on the screen (after its delay); it went. |
| `onCancel` | event | The Cancel button was pressed, or Escape; the panel hides after. |
| `show(), hide(), cancel()` | `boolean` / `void` | From code; `show()` is `false` while it is shown or waiting for its delay. |
| `isShown` | read-only | Whether it is on the screen now. |
| `spinner, cancelButton` | read-only | The kit’s spinner and button in the pane. |


---

# Toast

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Short notifications at an edge of the window: four tones, an action such as Undo, a time of their own or none, six positions and a limit on how many show at once. Called from code; a region of your own can sit in JSX.

## Import

```tsx
import { toast, Toast, Toaster, type ToastTone, type ToastPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From code and from JSX

`toast.show()` and its tone shortcuts return the `Toast`, an object you can `close()`, `update()` or await. They use `Toaster.default`, made in `document.body` the first time; an app can put a `Toaster` of its own where it wants it in JSX and make it the default.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast, type Toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Toasts shown from code: the Toast that comes back can be closed and awaited. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ reason: '' });

  const exportFile = () => {
    const t = toast.show({ title: 'Export', text: 'Preparing the file…', duration: 0 });
    setTimeout(() => t.close(), 2000);
  };

  const watch = async () => {
    s.reason = 'waiting…';
    const t: Toast = toast.show({ text: 'Close me any way you like.', duration: 3000, action: { text: 'Done' } });
    s.reason = `closed by: ${await t.closed}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Show a toast" tone="accent" onclick={() => toast.success('Your changes are saved.', { title: 'Saved' })} />
      <Button text="Export" variant="outline" onclick={exportFile} />
      <Button text="Watch how it closes" variant="outline" onclick={watch} />
      <output class="toast-reason">{() => s.reason}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Tones

`tone` sets the glyph, its color, and how a screen reader reads the toast: politely for `info` and `success`, at once for `caution` and `danger`.

```tsx
import { Button, toast, type ToastTone } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: { tone: ToastTone; text: string }[] = [
  { tone: 'info', text: 'A new version is ready.' },
  { tone: 'success', text: 'Your changes are saved.' },
  { tone: 'caution', text: 'Your session ends in 5 minutes.' },
  { tone: 'danger', text: 'The server did not answer.' },
];

/** A toast in each of the four tones. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <>
      {TONES.map(({ tone, text }) => (
        <Button key={tone} text={tone} variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.show({ tone, text })} />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Action and Undo

`action` adds a button; it runs `click`, then closes the toast. Make the undone thing come back, rather than asking first.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Archiving a mail at once, with an Undo button in the toast that brings it back. */
export default function Undo() {
  const s = reactive({ mails: ['Invoice #1042', 'Team lunch on Friday', 'Your order shipped'] });

  const archive = () => {
    const mail = s.mails.shift();
    if (!mail) return;
    toast.info(`“${mail}” archived.`, { action: { text: 'Undo', click: () => s.mails.unshift(mail) } });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <p class="toast-mails">{() => (s.mails.length ? `Inbox: ${s.mails.join(' · ')}` : 'The inbox is empty.')}</p>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Archive the first" variant="outline" enabled={() => s.mails.length > 0} onclick={archive} />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Duration and update

`duration` is 5 seconds by default; `0` keeps the toast until it is closed. Every option takes a function too, and `update()` changes a shown toast and starts its time again.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toast with a live text that stays until the upload ends, then turns into a success; one that stays. */
export default function DurationAndUpdate() {
  const s = reactive({ progress: 0, uploading: false });

  const upload = () => {
    if (s.uploading) return;
    s.uploading = true;
    s.progress = 0;
    const t = toast.show({ title: 'report.pdf', text: () => `Uploading… ${s.progress}%`, duration: 0, closeButton: false });
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      s.progress = Math.min(100, s.progress + 10);
      if (s.progress < 100) return;
      clearInterval(timer);
      s.uploading = false;
      t.update({ text: 'Uploaded.', tone: 'success', duration: 4000, closeButton: true });
    }, 300);
    void t.closed.then(() => clearInterval(timer));
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Upload a file" variant="outline" enabled={() => !s.uploading} onclick={upload} />
      <Button text="A toast that stays" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.caution('This one stays until you close it.', { duration: 0 })} />
      <Button text="Close all" variant="ghost" onclick={() => toast.closeAll()} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Positions

Six positions; start and end follow the reading direction. The newest toast is nearest the edge. A toast's `position` beats its toaster's.

```tsx
import { Button, toast, type ToastPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const POSITIONS: ToastPosition[] = ['top-start', 'top', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom', 'bottom-end'];

/** A toast at each of the six positions. */
export default function Positions() {
  return (
    <>
      {POSITIONS.map((position) => (
        <Button key={position} text={position} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.info(`At ${position}.`, { position })} />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## A toaster of your own, and max

A `Toaster` is the region the toasts show in. `max` limits how many show at once at one position; the rest wait and come in as others close. This one sits right here in the page, so Tab reaches its toasts after these buttons.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, Toaster } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toaster placed in the page, showing at most `max` toasts at once. */
export default function OwnToaster() {
  const s = reactive({ max: 2, count: 0 });
  let uploads: Toaster | null = null;

  const addFive = () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) uploads?.success(`photo-${++s.count}.jpg is uploaded.`, { duration: 3000 });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Toaster ref={(t: Toaster) => (uploads = t)} position="top-start" max={() => s.max} text="Demo notifications" />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Max">
        {[1, 2, 3].map((max) => (
          <Button
            key={max}
            text={`max ${max}`}
            size="sm"
            variant={() => (s.max === max ? 'solid' : 'ghost')}
            aria-pressed={() => s.max === max}
            onclick={() => (s.max = max)}
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Button text="Add five" variant="outline" onclick={addFive} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `F8 (`hotkey`)` | From anywhere on the page: to the newest toast. In a toast: back to where focus was. |
| `Tab` | Through the toasts and their buttons. The default toaster is the last thing in the page, so Tab reaches it after the page content. |
| `Escape` | With focus in a toast: closes it. Focus goes to the next toast, or back to where it came from. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Region` | `<section role="region">` named "Notifications" (`uiLocale`), with `aria-keyshortcuts` for the hotkey. |
| `Read out` | Info and success toasts are read politely (`role="status"`), caution and danger at once (`role="alert"`). `update()` reads it again; a live `text` function does not, so a progress number is not read on every change. |
| `Focus` | A toast never takes focus. Each toast is a group named by its title and text, and a Tab stop of its own, so one without buttons can be reached too. |
| `Time` | Timers stop while the pointer or focus is on the toasts and while the page is hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). Use `duration: 0` for anything the user must act on. |
| `Motion` | It slides in and fades out with the motion tokens; with reduced motion it just appears. |

## Localization

The name of the region and of the close button come from `uiLocale.strings` (`notifications`, `close`) and follow a change at once.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Switches the names of the region and the close button. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ lang: 'en' });

  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <Button text="Show a toast" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.info(s.lang === 'en' ? 'Hello.' : 'Merhaba.')} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-toaster` | The region. |
| `.mx-toaster__stack` | A stack at one position. `data-position`. |
| `.mx-toast` | A toast. `data-tone`, `data-state` (`entering`, `shown`, `leaving`). |
| `.mx-toast__icon, .mx-toast__body, .mx-toast__title, .mx-toast__text` | Its parts. |
| `.mx-toast__action, .mx-toast__close` | Its buttons (Buttons, `sm`). |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `toast.width` | The width of a toast (never wider than the window). |
| `toast.inset, toast.slide, toast.slide-inline` | The distance to the window edge; how far it slides in from its edge (at a corner, also from its side). |
| `toast.buttons-align` | Where the action and close buttons sit across the toast. |
| `toast.stack, toast.surface` | Units: the space between toasts; the toast with its box per tone (`success`, `caution`, `danger`) and under the keys (`focus`). |
| `toast.stripe, toast.timer` | Units a design may show: a stripe along the start edge, and a line that runs out with the time the toast stays; per tone. |
| `toast.icon, toast.plate, toast.mark` | Units: the tone glyph and a plate behind it, per tone; the tone’s own mark. |
| `toast.title, toast.message, toast.action-room, toast.close-room` | Units: the title, the message and the room around the buttons (their look is the `action` and `close` places’). |

## API reference

### Toast options and props

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The message. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A bold line above it. |
| `tone` | `Bind<ToastTone>` | `'info'` | `info`, `success`, `caution`, `danger`: the glyph, its color, and how a screen reader reads it. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | the tone glyph | An icon of your own; `null` for none. |
| `duration` | `Bind<number>` | `5000` | Milliseconds it stays; `0` keeps it until it is closed. |
| `action` | `Bind<ToastAction \| null>` | — | `{ text, click }`: a button in the toast, such as Undo. It runs `click(toast)`, then closes the toast. |
| `closeButton` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A close button, named from `uiLocale`. |
| `position` | `Bind<ToastPosition>` | the toaster's | Where it stacks: `top-start`, `top`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom`, `bottom-end`. |
| `onClosed` | `(reason) => void` | — | See the events. |

### toast and Toast

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toast.show(options \| Toast)` | `Toast` | Shows a toast on `Toaster.default`. |
| `toast.info / success / caution / danger(text, options?)` | `Toast` | The same with the tone set. |
| `toast.closeAll()` | `void` | Closes every toast of `Toaster.default`. |
| `t.close(reason?)` | `void` | Closes it; a closed toast is disposed. |
| `t.update(options)` | `void` | Changes any of the options, starts its time again and reads it out again. |
| `t.closed` | `Promise<ToastCloseReason>` | Settles when it closes: `timeout`, `button`, `escape`, `action` or `code`. |
| `t.onClosed(fn)` | event | The same as an event. |
| `t.text, t.tone, …` | read/write, reactive | Every option is a property too, taking a value or a function. |

### Toaster props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `Bind<ToastPosition>` | `'bottom-end'` | Where its toasts stack unless a toast says otherwise. |
| `max` | `Bind<number>` | `3` | How many show at once at one position; the rest wait their turn. |
| `hotkey` | `Bind<string>` | `'F8'` | Moves focus to the newest toast, and back again; `''` for none. |
| `pauseOnHover` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Timers stop while the pointer is over the toasts. They always stop while focus is in them or the page is hidden. |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `uiLocale` notifications | The name of the region. |

### Toaster members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Toaster.default` | static, read/write | The toaster `toast` uses: made in `document.body` on first use, or the one you assign. |
| `show, info, success, caution, danger, closeAll` | methods | As on `toast`, for this toaster. |
| `focusNewest()` | `boolean` | Moves focus to the newest toast. |
| `toasts` | read-only | The toasts on the screen, then the waiting ones. |
| `paused` | read-only | Whether the timers are stopped now. |

`enabled`, `visible` and the other shared properties of every control work on both.

# Badge

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A short text, a count or a dot: in a line of text, or on a corner of a button, an avatar or an icon. A count over its maximum shows “99+”, a count of zero hides.

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

Every prop takes a value or a function. Created with `new`, the same properties are set from code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Badge, Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A badge from JSX follows its functions; one made with `new` takes the same properties from code. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ unread: 4 });
  const coded = new Badge({ text: 'Beta', tone: 'info', variant: 'subtle' });

  return (
    <>
      <span>
        Inbox <Badge count={() => s.unread} label={() => `${s.unread} unread`} />
      </span>
      <Button text="Add one" variant="outline" onclick={() => s.unread++} />
      <Button text="Read all" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.unread = 0)} />
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)}>Search </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Tones and looks

```tsx
import { Badge, Stack, type BadgeTone, type BadgeVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: BadgeTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const VARIANTS: BadgeVariant[] = ['solid', 'subtle', 'outline'];

/** Every tone in each look. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Badge key={tone} text={tone} tone={tone} variant={variant} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Counts and dots

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Badge, NumberBox, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A count up to `max` and `max+` beyond it; at 0 it hides unless `showZero`; a dot says only that there is something. */
export default function Counts() {
  const s = reactive({ count: 120, max: 99, showZero: false });

  return (
    <>
      <NumberBox label="Count" min={0} x-model={() => s.count} />
      <NumberBox label="Max" min={1} x-model={() => s.max} />
      <Switch label="Show zero" x-model={() => s.showZero} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" align="center">
        <Badge count={() => s.count} max={() => s.max} showZero={() => s.showZero} />
        <Badge count={() => s.count} max={() => s.max} showZero={() => s.showZero} variant="subtle" />
        <Badge count={() => s.count} dot label="Something new" />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## On a corner

`position` puts the badge on a corner of what it is in. `Badge.attach` does it from code, on any component.

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Stack, type BadgePosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const CORNERS: BadgePosition[] = ['top-end', 'top-start', 'bottom-end', 'bottom-start'];

/** On a corner of what it is in: `position` inside a button, or `Badge.attach` on any component (here a `<span>`). */
export default function OnCorner() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="xl">
      {CORNERS.map((corner) => (
        <Button key={corner} text={corner} variant="outline">
          <Badge count={7} position={corner} />
        </Button>
      ))}
      <span ref={(bell) => Badge.attach(bell, { dot: true, tone: 'danger', label: 'New notifications' })}>Notifications</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Badge, Stack, type ControlSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: ControlSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];

/** A badge and a dot in each size. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
          <Badge text={size} size={size} />
          <Badge count={42} size={size} variant="subtle" />
          <Badge dot size={size} />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Text` | Read where it stands, as part of what it is in. |
| `label` | With a label the badge is an image with that name (`role="img"`), so a count can say what it counts. |
| `Dot` | Without a label a dot is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`): give it one when it says something. |
| `Colour` | The tone is never the only way something is said: pair a tone with a text or a label. |

## Localization

A count is written in the kit language (`uiLocale`), again when it changes: “1,234” in English, “1.234” in Turkish.

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-badge` | The badge. `data-tone`, `data-variant`, `data-size`, `data-position`, `data-dot`, `data-empty`. |
| `.mx-badge-anchor` | What a badge on a corner sits on (`position: relative`). |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `badge.badge` | Unit: the badge, at rest (solid, standard), in each look and tone (`accent` … `danger`, `subtle-*`, `outline-*`) and as a `dot`. |
| `badge.height.*, badge.dot-size.*, badge.font-size.*, badge.padding.*` | The badge and the dot per size. |
| `badge.offset` | How far a badge on a corner sits in from it. |
| `badge.tone, badge.variant` | The tone and look a badge takes when none is given. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A short text; shown while there is no `count`. |
| `count` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | A count, written in the kit language; over `max` it shows `max+`. |
| `max` | `Bind<number>` | `99` | The highest count written as it is. |
| `showZero` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A count of 0 shows; without it the badge hides at 0. |
| `dot` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A dot only: there is something, without saying what. |
| `tone` | `Bind<BadgeTone>` | the language’s | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution`, `danger`. Material marks counts in `danger`, the other languages in `accent`. |
| `variant` | `Bind<BadgeVariant>` | the language’s (`solid`) | `solid`, `subtle`, `outline`. |
| `size` | `Bind<ControlSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `position` | `Bind<BadgePosition \| null>` | `null` | `top-end`, `top-start`, `bottom-end`, `bottom-start`: on that corner of what it is in, which becomes its anchor. `start` and `end` follow the writing direction. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers say (“3 unread messages”); without it they read the text. |
| `visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | The shared properties of every control. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `shownText` | read-only | What it shows now: the count as written (`99+`), else the text; `''` for a dot. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Badge.attach(target, props?)` | `Badge` | Puts a badge on a corner of a component (`top-end` unless `props` says otherwise). It becomes one of its children and goes with it. |

# Avatar and AvatarGroup

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Someone’s picture, or their initials, or a person icon, with their presence on its corner. A group stacks or spreads them and counts the ones it does not show.

## Import

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

Every prop takes a value or a function. Created with `new`, the same properties are set from code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Avatar, Button, Stack, type AvatarStatus } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper'];
const STATUSES: AvatarStatus[] = ['online', 'away', 'busy', 'offline'];

/** An avatar from JSX follows its functions; one made with `new` takes the same properties from code. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ person: 0, status: 0 });
  const coded = new Avatar({ name: 'Edsger Dijkstra', tone: 'success', shape: 'square' });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Avatar name={() => PEOPLE[s.person]} status={() => STATUSES[s.status]} />
      <Button text="Next person" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.person = (s.person + 1) % PEOPLE.length)} />
      <Button text="Next presence" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.status = (s.status + 1) % STATUSES.length)} />
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Picture, initials, icon

The picture shows once it has loaded; until then, and when it cannot load, the initials show. Without a name the person icon does.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

// A picture of our own, so the example needs no network: a sunset as an SVG.
const PICTURE = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64"><defs><linearGradient id="sky" x2="0" y2="1">' +
    '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#3b5bdb"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#f08c00"/></linearGradient></defs>' +
    '<rect width="64" height="64" fill="url(#sky)"/><circle cx="32" cy="40" r="12" fill="#ffd43b"/>' +
    '<path d="M0 46h64v18H0z" fill="#2b8a3e"/></svg>',
)}`;

/** A picture; initials when there is none or it cannot load; a person icon without a name. */
export default function Content() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src={PICTURE} />
      <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
      <Avatar name="Alan Turing" src="does-not-exist.png" />
      <Avatar initials="QA" label="Quality team" />
      <Avatar />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Tones and shapes

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack, type AvatarShape, type AvatarTone } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: AvatarTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const SHAPES: AvatarShape[] = ['circle', 'square'];
const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Linus Torvalds'];

/** Every tone in each shape; `auto` takes a tone from the name, the same for the same name. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {SHAPES.map((shape) => (
        <Stack key={shape} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Avatar key={tone} name={tone} tone={tone} shape={shape} label={`${tone}, ${shape}`} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        {PEOPLE.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} tone="auto" />
        ))}
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes and presence

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack, type AvatarSize, type AvatarStatus } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: AvatarSize[] = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'];
const STATUSES: AvatarStatus[] = ['online', 'away', 'busy', 'offline'];

/** Each size, with each presence. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {STATUSES.map((status) => (
        <Stack key={status} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {SIZES.map((size) => (
            <Avatar key={size} name="Grace Hopper" size={size} status={status} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Groups

`max` shows that many and counts the rest in a `+N`; `total` counts those not given as well. The group sets the size of all its avatars.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TEAM = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov'];

/** Stacked with the rest counted, side by side, and a total larger than the avatars given. */
export default function Groups() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <AvatarGroup max={3} label="Team">
        {TEAM.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
      <AvatarGroup layout="spread" size="sm" label="Team">
        {TEAM.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
      <AvatarGroup size="lg" total={42} label="Followers">
        {TEAM.slice(0, 3).map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | With a name or a label the avatar is an image with that name (`role="img"`); the presence is said after it (“Ada Lovelace, Away”). |
| `No name` | An avatar with nothing to say (no name, no label, no presence) is hidden from screen readers. |
| `Picture` | The picture has an empty `alt`: the avatar itself carries the name. |
| `Group` | `role="group"` with its label; the `+N` says how many are not shown (“8 more people”). |
| `Colour` | The presence is not said by colour alone: it is in the name screen readers hear, and Fluent draws a mark in the dot. |

## Localization

Initials are written in the capitals of the kit language (`uiLocale`): “ilgin” is “İ” in Turkish. The presence and the `+N` texts are kit texts (`presenceOnline` … `presenceOffline`, `avatarPresence`, `moreItems`, `avatarGroupMore`) and change with it.

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-avatar` | The avatar. `data-size`, `data-shape`, `data-tone`. |
| `.mx-avatar__image` | The picture. `data-pending` until it loads. |
| `.mx-avatar__initials, .mx-avatar__icon` | The initials, and the person icon shown without them. |
| `.mx-avatar__status` | The presence dot. `data-status`. |
| `.mx-avatar-group` | The group. `data-size`, `data-layout`; an avatar it does not show has `data-beyond`. |
| `.mx-avatar-group__more` | The `+N` avatar. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `avatar.avatar` | Unit: the avatar at rest (the standard tone) and in each tone. |
| `avatar.icon, avatar.status, avatar.status-icon` | Units: the person icon; the presence dot (its ring, per presence); a mark inside the dot, per presence. |
| `avatar.size.*, avatar.font-size.*, avatar.icon-size.*, avatar.status-size.*, avatar.square-radius.*` | The avatar, its initials, its icon, its dot and its square corners, per size. |
| `avatar.tone, avatar.shape` | The tone and shape an avatar takes when none is given. |
| `avatar-group.stacked` | Unit: the ring that parts a stacked avatar from the one it covers. |
| `avatar-group.overlap.*, avatar-group.gap.*, avatar-group.layout` | How far stacked avatars go under each other, the space between spread ones, and the layout taken when none is given. |

## API reference

### Avatar props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | The picture. Until it loads, or when it cannot, the initials (else the person icon) show. |
| `name` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Whose avatar it is: the initials are made from it, and screen readers say it. |
| `initials` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Initials of your own instead of the ones made from `name`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers say instead of the name. |
| `size` | `Bind<AvatarSize>` | `'md'` | `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. In a group, the group’s. |
| `shape` | `Bind<AvatarShape>` | the language’s (`circle`) | `circle`, `square` (with the language’s corners for its size). |
| `tone` | `Bind<AvatarTone>` | the language’s | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution`, `danger`, or `auto`: one taken from the name, the same for the same name everywhere. Material and Lilac take `accent`, the others `standard`. |
| `status` | `Bind<AvatarStatus \| null>` | `null` | `online`, `away`, `busy`, `offline`: a presence dot on the lower end corner. |
| `visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | The shared properties of every control. |

### Avatar properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `shownInitials` | read-only | The initials it shows: the ones given, else the ones made from the name. |
| `showsPicture` | read-only | Whether the picture is what shows now (it loaded). |

### AvatarGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `Bind<AvatarSize>` | `'md'` | The size of every avatar in it. |
| `layout` | `Bind<AvatarGroupLayout>` | the language’s (`stack`) | `stack`: each over the one before it; `spread`: side by side. |
| `max` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | The most avatars shown; the others are counted in a `+N` after them. |
| `total` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | How many there are in all, when only some are given; the rest are counted in the `+N`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers call the group (“Members”). |

### AvatarGroup properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `avatars` | read-only | The elements of the avatars given, in order, from JSX lists too (the `+N` is not one of them). |
| `hiddenCount` | read-only | How many are counted in the `+N`; 0 when it does not show. |

### Functions

| Function | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `initialsOf(name, locale)` | `string` | The initials an avatar makes of a name: the first letters of its first and last words, in the capitals of the language. |

# Chip and ChipGroup

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A short text with an icon or an avatar before it: a filter to turn on, a choice among a few, or something picked that can be removed. A group selects one or several and moves between them with the arrow keys.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chip, ChipGroup } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

Every prop takes a value or a function. Created with `new`, the same properties are set from code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Chip, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A chip from JSX follows its functions; one made with `new` takes the same properties from code. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ vegan: false });
  const coded = new Chip({ text: 'Spicy', selectable: true });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Chip text="Vegan" selectable selected={() => s.vegan} onSelectedChanged={(e) => (s.vegan = e.selected)} />
      <span>{() => (s.vegan ? 'Vegan only' : 'Everything')}</span>
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Looks and states

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ChipVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const VARIANTS: ChipVariant[] = ['filled', 'outline'];

// A small star of our own, so the example needs no icon set.
const star = () => {
  const svg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg');
  svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 16 16');
  svg.innerHTML = '<path d="M8 1.5l1.9 4.1 4.4.5-3.3 3 .9 4.4L8 11.3l-3.9 2.2.9-4.4-3.3-3 4.4-.5z" fill="currentColor"/>';
  return svg;
};

/** Each look: at rest, selected, with an icon, with an avatar, removable, disabled. */
export default function Looks() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <Chip text="Rest" variant={variant} clickable />
          <Chip text="Selected" variant={variant} selectable selected />
          <Chip text="Icon" variant={variant} icon={star()} clickable />
          <Chip text="Ada Lovelace" variant={variant} avatar={{ name: 'Ada Lovelace' }} removable />
          <Chip text="Removable" variant={variant} removable />
          <Chip text="Disabled" variant={variant} selectable disabled />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Tones

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ChipTone, type ChipVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: ChipTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const VARIANTS: ChipVariant[] = ['filled', 'outline'];

/** Every tone in each look. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Chip key={tone} text={tone} tone={tone} variant={variant} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ControlSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: ControlSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];

/** Each size, plain, with an avatar and removable. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <Chip text={size} size={size} selectable />
          <Chip text="Grace Hopper" size={size} avatar={{ name: 'Grace Hopper' }} removable />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Choosing in a group

`selection` makes the chips choices; `value` holds their values and `onValueChanged` tells a change.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Chip, ChipGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const DIETS = ['Vegan', 'Vegetarian', 'Gluten free', 'Dairy free'];
const SIZES = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large'];

/** Several chosen (filters, bound with `x-model`) and one chosen (`value` and `onValueChanged`); the value is the chips' values. */
export default function Groups() {
  const s = reactive({ diets: ['Vegan'] as unknown, size: 'Medium' as unknown });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <ChipGroup selection="multiple" label="Diet" x-model={() => s.diets}>
        {DIETS.map((diet) => (
          <Chip key={diet} text={diet} />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <span>{() => `Diet: ${(s.diets as string[]).join(', ') || 'any'}`}</span>
      <ChipGroup selection="single" label="Size" value={() => s.size} onValueChanged={(e) => (s.size = e.value)}>
        {SIZES.map((size) => (
          <Chip key={size} text={size} />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <span>{() => `Size: ${s.size ?? 'none'}`}</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Removing

A removable chip only asks: `onRemove` is where your list loses the item, and the group follows the list.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Chip, ChipGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra'];

/** Removing is yours to do: `onRemove` takes the person out of the list, and the group follows the list. */
export default function Removing() {
  const s = reactive({ people: PEOPLE.map((name) => ({ name })) });

  return (
    <Stack>
      <ChipGroup label="Invited">
        {s.people.map((person) => (
          <Chip
            key={person.name}
            text={person.name}
            avatar={{ name: person.name }}
            removable
            onRemove={() => s.people.splice(s.people.indexOf(person), 1)}
          />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <Button text="Invite everyone again" variant="outline" onclick={() => s.people.splice(0, s.people.length, ...PEOPLE.map((name) => ({ name })))} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter, Space` | Presses the chip: turns a selectable one on or off, selects one in a group. |
| `Delete, Backspace` | Asks to remove a removable chip. |
| `Arrow keys, Home, End` | In a group: move between the chips. Tab stops once on the group, at the chip focused last. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Selectable` | A button with `aria-pressed`. |
| `In a group that selects` | The group is a `listbox` (`aria-multiselectable` for several), each chip an `option` with `aria-selected`. |
| `Remove` | The remove button is named “Remove Ada” in the kit language; the keyboard reaches it through Delete on the chip. |
| `Disabled` | Out of the Tab order and marked `aria-disabled`. |

## Localization

The remove button’s name is the kit text `removeItem` (“Remove {text}”) and changes with the kit language (`uiLocale`).

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-chip` | The chip. `data-size`, `data-variant`, `data-selected`, `data-pressable`, `data-removable`, `data-lead`, `data-check`, `data-disabled`. |
| `.mx-chip__check, .mx-chip__icon, .mx-chip__avatar` | What stands before the text. |
| `.mx-chip__text, .mx-chip__remove` | The text, and the remove button. |
| `.mx-chip-group` | The group. `data-wrap`. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `chip.chip` | Unit: the chip, filled at rest, then `outline`, each tone filled and outlined (`accent` … `danger`, `outline-*`), `selected`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `disabled`. |
| `chip.icon, chip.remove` | Units: the icon or check mark; the remove button (`hover`, `pressed`). |
| `chip.height.*, chip.font-size.*, chip.padding.*, chip.icon-inset.*, chip.gap.*` | The chip, its text and its spaces, per size. |
| `chip.icon-size.*, chip.avatar-size.*, chip.remove-size.*` | What stands before and after the text, per size. An avatar and the remove button sit as far in from the edge as from the top and bottom. |
| `chip.variant, chip.check` | The look a chip takes when none is given; whether a selected chip shows a check mark (Material). |
| `chip-group.gap` | The space between chips. |

## API reference

### Chip props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text. |
| `value` | `Bind<unknown>` | its text | What it stands for in a group’s value. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | `null` | An icon before the text: an image address, an element or a component. |
| `avatar` | `Bind<AvatarProps \| null>` | `null` | An avatar before the text (its props; the chip sets its size). |
| `selectable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Pressed, it turns on and off (a filter). In a group that selects, the group decides. |
| `selected` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Whether it is on. |
| `clickable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | It can be pressed like a button (`onclick`). |
| `removable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A remove button after the text; it and Delete / Backspace raise `onRemove`. |
| `variant` | `Bind<ChipVariant>` | the language’s | `filled`, `outline`. Material draws chips outlined, the other languages filled. |
| `tone` | `Bind<ChipTone>` | `'standard'` | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution`, `danger`; a selected chip shows the selection instead. |
| `size` | `Bind<ControlSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `enabled, visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | The shared properties of every control. |

### Chip events

| Event | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onRemove` | `ChipRemoveEventArgs` | The user asked to remove it (`byKeyboard`); removing it is yours to do. |
| `onSelectedChanged` | `ChipSelectedChangedEventArgs` | It was turned on or off (`selected`), by the user or by code (`byUser`). |

### Chip properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `avatarControl` | read-only | The avatar before the text, when it has one. |

### Chip methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove()` | `void` | Asks for it to be removed, as its remove button does (raises `onRemove`). |

### ChipGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selection` | `Bind<ChipGroupSelection>` | `'none'` | `none`, `single`, `multiple`. |
| `value` | `Bind<unknown>` | `null` / `[]` | The selected chip’s value (`single`), or an array of the selected ones’ values (`multiple`). A change gives a new array. Two-way with `x-model`. |
| `wrap` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` keeps the chips on one line that scrolls. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers call the group (“Diet”). |

### ChipGroup events, properties and methods

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueChanged` | event | The value changed (`value`), by the user or by code (`byUser`). |
| `chips` | read-only | The chips in it, in order, from JSX lists too. |
| `isSelected(value)` | `boolean` | Whether the chip of `value` is selected. |

# Card

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A surface holding one thing: a picture, a header with an avatar and titles, content and a row of actions. Parts with nothing in them are left out.

## Import

```tsx
import { Card } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

Every prop takes a value or a function. Created with `new`, the same properties are set from code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A card from JSX follows its functions; one made with `new` takes the same properties from code. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ following: false });
  const coded = new Card({ title: 'Made in code', subtitle: 'new Card({ … })', variant: 'outline' });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      <Card
        title="Ada Lovelace"
        subtitle={() => (s.following ? 'Following' : 'Mathematician')}
        avatar={{ name: 'Ada Lovelace' }}
        footer={<Button text={() => (s.following ? 'Unfollow' : 'Follow')} onclick={() => (s.following = !s.following)} />}
        style="inline-size: 18rem"
      >
        First to publish an algorithm meant to be carried out by a machine.
      </Card>
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Looks

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Stack, type CardVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const VARIANTS: CardVariant[] = ['elevated', 'filled', 'outline'];

/** Each look with a header, content and actions. */
export default function Variants() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Card
          key={variant}
          variant={variant}
          title={variant}
          subtitle="A card of this look"
          footer={
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap="sm">
              <Button text="Cancel" variant="ghost" />
              <Button text="Open" />
            </Stack>
          }
          style="inline-size: 16rem"
        >
          The same header, content and actions in each look.
        </Card>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Pictures

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { PICTURE } from './picture';

/** A picture above the rest, or at its start (`horizontal`); it runs to the card's edges and takes its corners. */
export default function Media() {

    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      <Card media={PICTURE} mediaAlt="A sunset over a field" title="Sunset" subtitle="Above the rest" style="inline-size: 16rem">
        The picture runs to the edges.

      <Card
        media={PICTURE}
        orientation="horizontal"

        subtitle="At the start"
```
