# BottomSheet

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A panel that comes up from the bottom of the page or of a container and stops at a few heights: a peek, half, full, as tall as its content, or heights of your own. Dragged by its handle and its title, flicked, swiped down to close; modal or not, with the browser's back closing it on a phone.

## Import

```tsx
import { BottomSheet, type BottomSheetDetent } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

In JSX, `x-model` opens and closes it with the state. From code, `show(host)` puts it in a component and disposes it when it closes; `open()` and `close()` work on one that stays. Without a `container` it opens over the whole page, in the browser's top layer.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { BottomSheet, Button, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A sheet written in JSX and bound to state, and one made in code and shown, both over the whole page. */
export default function JsxAndCode() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, name: 'Ada', said: '' });

  const share = () => {
    const sheet = new BottomSheet({
      title: 'Share',
      detent: 'fit',
      detents: ['fit', 'full'],
      content: (
        <Stack gap="sm">
          <p>Anyone with the link can see the report.</p>
          <Button text="Copy the link" variant="outline" onclick={() => sheet.close()} />
        </Stack>
      ),
      onClosed: (e) => (s.said = `The code sheet closed (${e.reason}).`),
    });
    // show() puts it in the page and disposes it when it closes.
    sheet.show(host);
  };
  let host!: Stack;

  return (
    <Stack ref={(c: Stack) => (host = c)} gap="sm">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Edit the name" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
        <Button text="Share (from code)" variant="outline" onclick={share} />
        <output>{() => s.said || `Name: ${s.name}`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <BottomSheet title="Your name" showClose detents={['half', 'full']} x-model={() => s.open}>
        <TextBox label="Name" x-model={() => s.name} />
      </BottomSheet>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Heights, dragging and options

`detents` are the heights it stops at, `detent` the one it is at. The handle and the title follow the finger and the mouse; the content takes the sheet along from its top. Here it opens over a frame (`container`), not modal, so the page under it stays usable. Every behaviour is a switch, live.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { BottomSheet, Button, RadioGroup, Stack, Switch, type BottomSheetDetent } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, text: `Place ${i + 1}` }));

/** A sheet over a frame, at a peek, half or full height: drag the handle or the title, flick, use the arrow keys on the handle. Every behaviour is a switch. */
export default function Detents() {
  const s = reactive({
    open: true,
    detent: 'peek' as BottomSheetDetent,
    modal: false,
    handle: true,
    draggable: true,
    content: true,
    swipe: true,
    back: true,
  });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Switch label="Modal" x-model={() => s.modal} />
        <Switch label="Handle" x-model={() => s.handle} />
        <Switch label="Draggable" x-model={() => s.draggable} />
        <Switch label="Content drags it" x-model={() => s.content} />
        <Switch label="Swipe down closes" x-model={() => s.swipe} />
        <Switch label="Back button closes" x-model={() => s.back} />
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Height"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'peek', text: 'Peek' },
            { value: 'half', text: 'Half' },
            { value: 'full', text: 'Full' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.detent}
        />
        <Button text="Open" variant="outline" enabled={() => !s.open} onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      </Stack>
      <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)} class="sheet-frame" style="position: relative; block-size: 28rem; overflow: hidden; border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg); background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer)">
        <p style="padding: var(--mx-space-4)">The page under the sheet. Non-modal, it stays usable.</p>
      </div>
      <BottomSheet
        title="Nearby"
        label="Nearby places"
        container={() => frame}
        detents={['peek', 'half', 'full']}
        x-model={() => s.open}
        detent={() => s.detent}
        onDetentChanged={(e) => (s.detent = e.to)}
        modal={() => s.modal}
        showHandle={() => s.handle}
        draggable={() => s.draggable}
        dragContent={() => s.content}
        swipeToClose={() => s.swipe}
        closeOnBack={() => s.back}
      >
        <ul style="margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none">
          {ROWS.map((row) => (
            <li key={row.id} style="padding-block: var(--mx-space-2); border-block-end: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-divider)">
              {row.text}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Events

Each opening, closing and change of height asks first and reports after. `onClosing` tells why (`reason`) and can keep it open; `onDetentChanging` can refuse a height or pick another.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { BottomSheet, Button, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The events in order. While "Keep it open" is on, onClosing refuses every closing but by code; "Not full" refuses the tallest height. */
export default function Events() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, keep: false, notFull: false, log: [] as string[] });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;

  const log = (line: string) => {
    s.log.push(line);
    if (s.log.length > 6) s.log.shift();
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Button text="Open" variant="outline" enabled={() => !s.open} onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
        <Switch label="Keep it open" x-model={() => s.keep} />
        <Switch label="Not full" x-model={() => s.notFull} />
      </Stack>
      <output>{() => s.log.join(' · ') || 'No events yet.'}</output>
      <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)} style="position: relative; block-size: 28rem; overflow: hidden; border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg); background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer)" />
      <BottomSheet
        title="Events"
        showClose
        container={() => frame}
        detents={['half', 'full']}
        x-model={() => s.open}
        onOpening={() => log('opening')}
        onOpened={() => log('opened')}
        onDetentChanging={(e) => {
          log(`detentChanging ${e.from} → ${e.to}`);
          if (s.notFull && e.to === 'full') e.cancel = true;
        }}
        onDetentChanged={(e) => log(`detentChanged ${e.to}`)}
        onClosing={(e) => {
          log(`closing (${e.reason})`);
          if (s.keep && e.reason !== 'code') e.cancel = true;
        }}
        onClosed={(e) => log(`closed (${e.reason})`)}
      >
        <p>Drag it, press Escape, the scrim, its close button or the browser's back.</p>
        <Button text="Close by code" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = false)} />
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Closes it (`closeOnEscape`). |
| `Tab, Shift+Tab` | Through its controls; modal, it goes round inside. |
| `Up, Right, Page Up (on the handle)` | The next taller height. |
| `Down, Left, Page Down (on the handle)` | The next lower height; it does not close it. |
| `Home, End (on the handle)` | The lowest and the tallest height. |

## Finger and mouse

| Gesture | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Drag the handle or the title` | The sheet follows the finger or the mouse; let go, it goes to the nearest height. Past the tallest it gives a little. |
| `Flick` | Faster than `flickSpeed`: on to the next height that way, however far it went. |
| `Drag or flick down past the lowest height` | It closes (`swipeToClose`), with `reason: 'swipe'`. |
| `Drag the content` | Down from its top, or up while the sheet is not at its tallest, the sheet moves; otherwise the content scrolls. A sideways swipe is the content's. |
| `Tap the handle` | The next height, round to the lowest. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | The panel is `role="dialog"`, named by its title (else `label`, else "Sheet"), `aria-modal` when modal. What is around it is made `inert`, so screen readers and the keys stay inside. |
| `Handle` | `role="slider"`, vertical, named "Sheet height"; its value is the share of the full height, read as the height's name ("Half height"). |
| `Focus` | Moves in when it opens (modal by default) and back to where it was when it closes. |
| `Motion` | It slides with the motion tokens; with reduced motion it just appears. |
| `Safe areas` | The panel keeps clear of the screen's rounded corners and bars (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`). |

## Localization

The handle's name and heights, the default name and the close button come from `uiLocale.strings` (`sheetHandle`, `sheetPeek`, `sheetHalf`, `sheetFull`, `sheetFit`, `sheetHeight`, `sheetLabel`, `close`).

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { BottomSheet, Button, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The handle's name and heights and the close button's name come from uiLocale. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, lang: 'en' });

  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <Button text="Open" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      <BottomSheet showClose detents={['peek', 'half', 'full']} detent="half" x-model={() => s.open}>
        <p>Focus the handle: a screen reader reads its name and the height it is at.</p>
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet` | The layer over the page or the container. `data-open`, `data-modal`, `data-scrim`, `data-contained`, `data-dragging`. |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet__scrim` | The dimmed layer. |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet__panel` | The dialog. `--_size` is its height, `--_drop` how far it is pulled below its lowest height. |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet__handle, .mx-bottom-sheet__grip` | The handle (the slider) and the line drawn in it. |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet__header, __title, __tools, __close` | The title row and its close button. |
| `.mx-bottom-sheet__body, .mx-bottom-sheet__footer` | The content that scrolls, and the row under it. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `sheet.scrim, sheet.panel` | Units: the dimmed layer; the surface (`max-width`: how wide it gets on a large screen; `full`: its top corners once it reaches the top of the room). |
| `sheet.handle, sheet.grip` | Units: the handle (`focus`: the keys) and its grip. |
| `sheet.header, sheet.title, sheet.tools, sheet.body, sheet.footer` | Units: inside (`body.focus`: a ring inside the content). |
| `sheet.top-gap, sheet.peek-height, sheet.inset` | The gap it leaves at the top at full height, the peek height, the room around the panel. |
| `sheet.handle-area, sheet.font-family` | The handle’s grab area; the type’s family. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Whether it is open. `x-model` binds it two-way: the user closing it writes `false`. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A title at the top; it names the dialog. The same property as `text`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Names it for screen readers when it has no title (else "Sheet", from `uiLocale`). |
| `detents` | `Bind<readonly BottomSheetDetent[]>` | `['half', 'full']` | The heights it stops at: `'peek'` (`sheet.peek-height`), `'half'`, `'full'` (the room but `sheet.top-gap`), `'fit'` (as tall as its content), pixels, or a share such as `'40%'`. |
| `detent` | `Bind<BottomSheetDetent>` | the first of `detents` | The height it opens at and is at now; the user moving it writes it, setting it moves the sheet. |
| `modal` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Nothing around it can be used: inside its container, or on the whole page. Tab stays inside. |
| `scrim` | `Bind<boolean>` | when modal | A dimmed layer under it. |
| `container` | `Bind<HTMLElement \| ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | Opens over this element (a static one is made relative while it is open); `null` over the page, in the top layer. |
| `content, footer` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | — | What fills it, next to JSX children, and a row under it that does not scroll. |
| `showClose` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A close button beside the title. |
| `showHandle` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The handle at the top: a grip for the finger and the mouse, a slider for the keys. |
| `draggable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The finger and the mouse move it between its heights by the handle and the title. |
| `dragContent` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A finger on the content takes the sheet along when the content cannot scroll that way: down from its top, up while the sheet is not at its tallest. |
| `swipeToClose` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Dragged or flicked down below its lowest height, it closes. |
| `flickSpeed` | `Bind<number>` | `0.4` | How fast a flick goes on to the next height, in pixels per millisecond. |
| `closeOnEscape, closeOnScrim` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Escape and a press on the scrim close it. |
| `closeOnBack` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The browser's back (Android's back button, the back gesture) closes it: it holds one history entry while open and takes it back when it closes otherwise, so no entry is left behind. |
| `focusOnOpen` | `Bind<boolean>` | when modal | Focus moves in when it opens: `[autofocus]`, the first field, the first control, else the panel. |
| `returnFocus` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Focus goes back where it was when it closes. |
| `disposeOnClose` | `Bind<boolean>` | see text | Disposed when it closes: by default when `show` put it in its host. |
| `enabled, visible` | see Control |  | The shared properties of every control. |

### Members and events

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open()` | `boolean` | Opens it at `detent`; `false` when `onOpening` said no. Placed nowhere, it opens from the end of the page (or in its container). |
| `close(reason?)` | `boolean` | Closes it; `false` when `onClosing` kept it open. |
| `toggle()` | `boolean` | Opens or closes it. |
| `show(host, disposeRef?)` | `boolean` | Adds it to `host` (a component or the application) unless it is placed, and opens it; it is disposed when it closes. |
| `snapTo(detent)` | `boolean` | Moves it to a height (and opens it there when closed). |
| `expand(), collapse()` | `boolean` | To the next taller or lower height; `false` at the end. |
| `isOpen, height` | read-only | Whether it is open (reactive), and its height now in pixels. |
| `panelElement, contentElement` | read-only | The surface with `role="dialog"`, and the area that scrolls. |
| `onOpening / onOpened` | events | `{ cancel, source }` / `{ source }`; opened comes after it slid in. |
| `onClosing / onClosed` | events | `{ cancel, reason, source }` / `{ reason, source }`: `'code'`, `'escape'`, `'scrim'`, `'swipe'`, `'back'`, `'button'`, `'owner'`. The owner going away cannot be refused. |
| `onDetentChanging / onDetentChanged` | events | `{ from, to, byUser, cancel, source }`: `to` can be changed; refused, the sheet goes back where it was. |

Every prop is a property too, taking a value or a function. The shared parts (the panel, the scrim, modality, focus and the back button) are `OverlayPanel`'s, which `Drawer` and `ActionSheet` build on as well.


---

# Drawer

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A panel that slides in from an edge of the page or of a container, over the content or pushing it aside. A finger swipes it in from the edge and back again; Escape, the scrim and the browser's back close it.

## Import

```tsx
import { Drawer, type DrawerSide, type DrawerMode } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## A drawer over the page

Bound with `x-model`, or opened with `open()` and `show(host)` as a bottom sheet is. Over the page it opens in the top layer, modal, with a scrim.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Drawer, ListBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLACES = [
  { id: 'inbox', text: 'Inbox' },
  { id: 'starred', text: 'Starred' },
  { id: 'sent', text: 'Sent' },
  { id: 'drafts', text: 'Drafts' },
];

/** A drawer over the whole page from the start edge, bound with x-model; a finger can swipe it back to close it. */
export default function Navigation() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, place: 'inbox' });

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Menu" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      <output>{() => `Showing: ${PLACES.find((p) => p.id === s.place)?.text}`}</output>
      <Drawer title="Mail" showClose x-model={() => s.open}>
        <ListBox label="Folders" items={PLACES} itemText="text" itemValue="id" x-model={() => s.place} onclick={() => (s.open = false)} />
      </Drawer>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Edges, push and swipes

Over a frame (`container`), from any edge. `push` moves the frame's content aside (`pushTarget`) and is not modal unless asked. With `edgeSwipe` a finger on a touch screen opens it from the edge; every option is live.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Drawer, RadioGroup, Stack, Switch, type DrawerMode, type DrawerSide } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A drawer over a frame: its edge, over or pushing the content, a swipe in from the edge, modal or not. Every option is live. */
export default function Options() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, side: 'start' as DrawerSide, mode: 'over' as DrawerMode, edge: true, modal: true, swipe: true, back: true });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;
  let content!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Switch label="Swipe in from the edge" x-model={() => s.edge} />
        <Switch label="Modal" x-model={() => s.modal} />
        <Switch label="Swipe back closes" x-model={() => s.swipe} />
        <Switch label="Back button closes" x-model={() => s.back} />
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Edge"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'start', text: 'Start' },
            { value: 'end', text: 'End' },
            { value: 'top', text: 'Top' },
            { value: 'bottom', text: 'Bottom' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.side}
        />
        <RadioGroup
          label="Mode"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'over', text: 'Over' },
            { value: 'push', text: 'Push' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.mode}
        />
        <Button text="Open" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      </Stack>
      <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)} style="position: relative; block-size: 28rem; overflow: hidden; border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg); background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer)">
        <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (content = c)} style="block-size: 100%; padding: var(--mx-space-4); box-sizing: border-box">
          <p>The content of the frame. On a touch screen, swipe in from its edge.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <Drawer
        title="Filters"
        showClose
        container={() => frame}
        side={() => s.side}
        mode={() => s.mode}
        pushTarget={() => content}
        edgeSwipe={() => s.edge}
        modal={() => s.modal}
        swipeToClose={() => s.swipe}
        closeOnBack={() => s.back}
        size={() => (s.side === 'top' || s.side === 'bottom' ? '12rem' : null)}
        x-model={() => s.open}
      >
        <Stack gap="sm">
          <Switch label="Only unread" />
          <Switch label="With attachments" />
          <Button text="Apply" onclick={() => (s.open = false)} />
        </Stack>
      </Drawer>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Events

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Drawer, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The events of a drawer in order; "Keep it open" refuses every closing but by code. */
export default function Events() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, keep: false, log: [] as string[] });

  const log = (line: string) => {
    s.log.push(line);
    if (s.log.length > 6) s.log.shift();
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Button text="Open" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
        <Switch label="Keep it open" x-model={() => s.keep} />
      </Stack>
      <output>{() => s.log.join(' · ') || 'No events yet.'}</output>
      <Drawer
        side="end"
        title="Events"
        showClose
        x-model={() => s.open}
        onOpening={() => log('opening')}
        onOpened={() => log('opened')}
        onClosing={(e) => {
          log(`closing (${e.reason})`);
          if (s.keep && e.reason !== 'code') e.cancel = true;
        }}
        onClosed={(e) => log(`closed (${e.reason})`)}
      >
        <Button text="Close by code" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = false)} />
      </Drawer>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Finger and keys

| Gesture or key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Swipe in from the edge (`edgeSwipe`)` | The drawer follows the finger; let go past half its size (or flicked), it stays open, else it goes back. |
| `Swipe it back towards its edge` | It follows; let go past half (or flicked), it closes. A swipe on something inside that scrolls sideways is that thing's. |
| `A press on the scrim, Escape, the back button` | It closes (each an option). |
| `Escape` | Closes it. |
| `Tab, Shift+Tab` | Through its controls; modal, it goes round inside. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | The panel is `role="dialog"`, named by its title, else `label`, else "Side panel"; `aria-modal` when modal, and what is around it is `inert`. |
| `Focus` | Moves in when it opens modal, back where it was when it closes. |
| `Reading direction` | `start` is the left edge left to right and the right edge right to left; the slide follows. |
| `Motion` | It slides with the motion tokens; with reduced motion it just appears. |

## Localization

Its default name and the close button come from `uiLocale.strings` (`drawerLabel`, `close`).

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-drawer` | The layer. `data-side` (`start`, `end`, `top`, `bottom`), `data-mode`, `data-open`, `data-modal`, `data-scrim`, `data-contained`, `data-dragging`. |
| `.mx-drawer__panel` | The dialog. `--_size`, and `--_shift-x` / `--_shift-y` while a finger moves it. |
| `.mx-drawer__scrim, __header, __title, __tools, __close, __body, __footer` | Its parts. |
| `[data-mx-drawer-push]` | The element a push drawer moves aside, by `--_mx-push`. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `drawer.scrim, drawer.panel` | Units: the dimmed layer; the surface at each edge (`start`, `end`, `top`, `bottom`: its sides towards the content and the room differ) and pushing the content (`push`). |
| `drawer.header, drawer.title, drawer.tools, drawer.body, drawer.footer` | Units: inside (`body.focus`: a ring inside the content). |
| `drawer.size, drawer.max-size, drawer.inset, drawer.font-family` | The size it opens at, the most of the room it takes, the room around it; the type’s family. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Whether it is open. `x-model` binds it two-way. |
| `side` | `Bind<'start' \| 'end' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom'>` | `'start'` | The edge it slides in from. `start` and `end` follow the reading direction; `left` and `right` do not. |
| `mode` | `Bind<'over' \| 'push'>` | `'over'` | Over the content, or moving `pushTarget` aside by its size. |
| `pushTarget` | `Bind<HTMLElement \| ComponentBase \| null>` | — | What `push` moves aside. Without it, `push` works as `over`. |
| `size` | `Bind<number \| string \| null>` | `null` | Its width (its height from the top or the bottom): pixels or a CSS length; `null` for `drawer.size`. Never more than 85% of the room. |
| `edgeSwipe` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A finger swiping in from the edge of the container (or the page) opens it, following the finger. |
| `edgeSize` | `Bind<number>` | `24` | How far from the edge, in pixels, that swipe may start. |
| `swipeToClose` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A finger swiping it back towards its edge closes it. |
| `flickSpeed` | `Bind<number>` | `0.4` | A flick faster than this, in pixels per millisecond, opens or closes it however far it went. |
| `modal` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` over, `false` in push | Nothing around it can be used; Tab stays inside. |
| `title, label, container, content, footer, showClose, scrim, closeOnEscape, closeOnScrim, closeOnBack, focusOnOpen, returnFocus, disposeOnClose` | see BottomSheet |  | The props every overlay panel shares, as on the [BottomSheet page](bottomsheet.md#api). |

### Members and events

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open(), close(reason?), toggle(), show(host)` | `boolean` | As on a bottom sheet. |
| `isOpen` | read-only, reactive | Whether it is open. |
| `onOpening / onOpened / onClosing / onClosed` | events | As on a bottom sheet; a swipe back closes with `reason: 'swipe'`. A swipe from the edge that `onOpening` refuses does not move it. |


---

# ActionSheet

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A list of commands that comes up from the bottom, made of the kit's menu items and large enough for a finger, with a title, a message and a cancel button apart. A context menu opens its items here on a touch screen.

## Import

```tsx
import { ActionSheet, type ActionSheetProps } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Choosing from code

`choose()` opens it and resolves with the item chosen, or `null`. An item with `items` opens its submenu in place, with a way back.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { ActionSheet, Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ITEMS: MenuItem[] = [
  { text: '&Share…' },
  { text: '&Rename…' },
  {
    text: '&Move to',
    items: [{ text: 'Reports' }, { text: 'Archive' }, { text: 'Shared with me' }],
  },
  { text: '&Delete', tone: 'danger', beginGroup: true },
];

/** choose() opens the sheet and resolves with the item chosen, or null; a submenu opens in place, with a way back. */
export default function Choose() {
  const s = reactive({ said: 'Nothing chosen yet.' });
  let host!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;

  const ask = async () => {
    const sheet = new ActionSheet({ title: 'report.pdf', message: 'Changed today at 09:41' });
    const item = await sheet.choose(ITEMS, host);
    s.said = item ? `Chosen: ${String(item.text).replace('&', '')}` : 'Closed without a choice.';
  };

  return (
    <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (host = c)} style="display: contents">
      <Button text="Actions…" variant="outline" onclick={ask} />
      <output>{() => s.said}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## In JSX

Bound with `x-model`; check and radio items show their marks, `cancelText` names the cancel button.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ActionSheet, Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An action sheet in JSX, bound with x-model, with checked items and its own cancel text; onItemClick reports the choice. */
export default function InJsx() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, sort: 'date', said: '' });

  const sortItem = (value: string, text: string): MenuItem => ({
    text,
    group: 'sort',
    checked: () => s.sort === value,
    click: () => (s.sort = value),
  });

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => `Sort by: ${s.sort}`} variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      <output>{() => s.said}</output>
      <ActionSheet
        title="Sort by"
        cancelText="Keep as it is"
        items={[sortItem('date', 'Date'), sortItem('name', 'Name'), sortItem('size', 'Size')]}
        x-model={() => s.open}
        onItemClick={(e) => (s.said = `Sorted by ${String(e.item.text).toLowerCase()}.`)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

## A context menu on a touch screen

`ContextMenu` has `presentation`: `'menu'` (the default), `'sheet'`, or `'auto'`, which opens an action sheet when a finger opened the menu (a long press). The items, `onOpening` and `onItemClick` stay the same.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { ContextMenu, RadioGroup, Stack, type ContextMenuPresentation, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ROWS = ['Invoice 1042', 'Invoice 1043', 'Invoice 1044'];

/** One ContextMenu, shown as a menu, as an action sheet, or (auto) as a sheet when a finger opened it: long press a row on a phone. */
export default function FromContextMenu() {
  const s = reactive({ presentation: 'auto' as ContextMenuPresentation, said: '' });
  let list!: Component<HTMLUListElement>;

  const items = (row: string): MenuItem[] => [
    { text: `&Open ${row}`, click: () => (s.said = `Opened ${row}`) },
    { text: '&Copy number', click: () => (s.said = `Copied ${row}`) },
    { text: '&Delete', tone: 'danger', click: () => (s.said = `Deleted ${row}`) },
  ];

  return (
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <RadioGroup
        label="Presentation"
        orientation="horizontal"
        items={[
          { value: 'menu', text: 'Menu' },
          { value: 'sheet', text: 'Sheet' },
          { value: 'auto', text: 'Auto' },
        ]}
        itemText="text"
        itemValue="value"
        x-model={() => s.presentation}
      />
      <ul ref={(c: Component<HTMLUListElement>) => (list = c)} aria-label="Invoices" style="margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none">
        {ROWS.map((row) => (
          <li key={row} tabindex="0" data-row={row} style="padding: var(--mx-space-3); border-block-end: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-divider); user-select: none">
            {row}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <output>{() => s.said || 'Right-click or long press a row; the Menu key on a focused row.'}</output>
      <ContextMenu
        label="Invoice"
        target={() => list}
        presentation={() => s.presentation}
        onOpening={(e) => {
          const row = (e.target as Element).closest('[data-row]')?.getAttribute('data-row');
          if (row) e.items = items(row);
          else e.cancel = true;
        }}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Up, Down, Home, End` | Between the items, round at the ends. |
| `Enter, Space, an item's `&` letter` | Chooses it; on a submenu, opens it in place. |
| `A letter` | The next item that starts with it. |
| `Escape` | Closes it without a choice. |
| `Tab` | To the cancel button and back. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog and menu` | The sheet is a `dialog` named by its title; the items are a `menu` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio`, as in the kit's menus. |
| `Focus` | Opened by a key, on the first item; by a finger or the pointer, on the list. It goes back where it was when the sheet closes. |
| `Submenus` | Open in place of their menu with "Back" first; the arrow at the end of an item says it has one. |
| `Touch` | Items are `control.height.lg` high (`actionsheet.item-height`), larger than the 24 pixels WCAG 2.2 asks for. |

## Localization

Cancel, the way back and its default name come from `uiLocale.strings` (`cancel`, `back`, `actionSheetLabel`); `cancelText` gives one of your own.

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-action-sheet` | On the bottom sheet's layer (`.mx-bottom-sheet`), whose hooks it has. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__message` | The line under the title. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__list` | The menu (`.mx-menu`). |
| `.mx-action-sheet__cancel` | The row of the cancel button. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__back` | The mark of the way back. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `actionsheet.message, actionsheet.back, actionsheet.cancel` | Units: the message, the mark of the item that goes back out of a submenu (`rtl`), the strip that holds the cancel button. |
| `actionsheet.menu.*, actionsheet.cancel-button.*, actionsheet.sheet.*` | Places: the items, large enough for a finger; the cancel button; the sheet’s content padding. |
| `sheet.*` | The surface, the handle and the title, as on the bottom sheet. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly MenuItem[]>` | `[]` | The commands: the kit's menu items, with their icons, check and radio marks, tones, `&` keys, groups and submenus (shortcuts are not shown). |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A title above the items; it names the sheet (else `label`, else "Actions"). |
| `message` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A line under the title that says what the choice is about. |
| `showCancel` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A cancel button apart, at the bottom. |
| `cancelText` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Its text; empty for `uiLocale`'s Cancel. |
| `detents` | `Bind<readonly BottomSheetDetent[]>` | `['fit']` | As tall as its items (up to full); any of the bottom sheet's heights. |
| `onItemClick` | `(e: MenuItemClickEventArgs) => void` | — | An item was chosen, after the sheet closed and the item's own `click` ran. |
| `every BottomSheet prop` | see BottomSheet |  | Modal, the handle, swipe down, Escape, the scrim and the back button work as on the [BottomSheet page](bottomsheet.md#api). |

### Members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `choose(items?, host?)` | `Promise<MenuItem \| null>` | Opens it (with these items) and resolves with the item chosen, or `null` when it was closed without one. `host` gives it a place when it has none. |
| `open(byKeyboard?)` | `boolean` | Opens it; `byKeyboard` puts focus on the first item, else on the list as a menu the pointer opened. |
| `chosenItem` | read-only | The item chosen the last time it was open. |
| `menu` | read-only | Its `MenuList`. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Your items may be plain or reactive; the sheet reads them as they are. After changing them in place, call `refresh()`. The level shown follows. |
| `ContextMenu presentation` | `Bind<'menu' \| 'sheet' \| 'auto'>` | On `ContextMenu`, default `'menu'`. `'sheet'` opens its items in an action sheet; `'auto'` does when a finger opened it (a long press), or on a screen with only a coarse pointer when not opened by a key. `onOpening`, `onItemClick` and `onClosed` work the same; `actionSheet` is the sheet. |


---

# Layout

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Containers that place controls: `Stack` (a row or a column), `Grid` (rows and columns), `Panel` (a plain box that can scroll), `GroupBox` (a titled frame), `DockPanel` (children stuck to its edges) and `SplitContainer` (two panes and a splitter). All of them are controls: they disable and hide what is inside, and lay out children added at any time.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stack, Grid, Panel, GroupBox, DockPanel, SplitContainer, type LayoutSpace } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## From JSX and from code

Children come as JSX or are added later with `controls.add`; either way the container picks them up. A child says where it goes in its own props (`grow`, `row`, `dock`…), whatever kind of component it is.

```tsx
import type { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Buttons added to a Stack with `controls.add`, and a Grid built with `new`. */
export default function FromCode() {
  let added = 0;
  let bar: Stack | null = null;

  const addButton = () => bar?.controls.add(new Button({ text: `Button ${++added}`, variant: 'outline', grow: added % 3 === 0 }));

  const buildFromCode = (host: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const grid = new Grid({ columns: '* *', gap: 'xs' });
    grid.element.classList.add('layout-coded');
    grid.controls.add(
      new TextBox({ label: 'From', stretch: true }),
      new TextBox({ label: 'To', stretch: true }),
      new TextBox({ label: 'Subject', stretch: true, columnSpan: 2 }),
    );
    host.controls.add(grid);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack ref={(c: Stack) => (bar = c)} orientation="horizontal" gap="sm" wrap align="center" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <Button text="Add a button" tone="accent" onclick={addButton} />
      </Stack>
      <div style="inline-size: 100%" ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => buildFromCode(c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Stack

A row or a column with a gap. `align` places the children across the direction, `justify` along it; `wrap` starts a new line when they do not fit. A child with `grow` takes the free space.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Panel, Stack, TextBox, type LayoutAlign, type StackJustify } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ALIGNS: LayoutAlign[] = ['start', 'center', 'end', 'stretch', 'baseline'];
const JUSTIFIES: StackJustify[] = ['start', 'center', 'end', 'space-between', 'space-evenly'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';

/** A Stack's orientation, align, justify, wrap and reverse, and a child that grows. */
export default function StackOptions() {
  const s = reactive({
    orientation: 'horizontal' as 'horizontal' | 'vertical',
    align: 'center' as LayoutAlign,
    justify: 'start' as StackJustify,
    wrap: false,
    reverse: false,
  });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Orientation">
        {(['horizontal', 'vertical'] as const).map((o) => (
          <Button key={o} text={o} size="sm" variant={() => (s.orientation === o ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.orientation === o} onclick={() => (s.orientation = o)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Align">
        {ALIGNS.map((a) => (
          <Button key={a} text={a} size="sm" variant={() => (s.align === a ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.align === a} onclick={() => (s.align = a)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Justify">
        {JUSTIFIES.map((j) => (
          <Button key={j} text={j} size="sm" variant={() => (s.justify === j ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.justify === j} onclick={() => (s.justify = j)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="wrap" size="sm" toggle x-model={() => s.wrap} variant="outline" />
        <Button text="reverse" size="sm" toggle x-model={() => s.reverse} variant="outline" />
      </Stack>
      <Stack
        class="layout-stack-demo"
        orientation={() => s.orientation}
        align={() => s.align}
        justify={() => s.justify}
        wrap={() => s.wrap}
        reverse={() => s.reverse}
        gap="sm"
        padding="sm"
        style={`inline-size: 100%; min-block-size: 10rem; ${FRAME}`}
      >
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">One</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="md">Two, taller</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">Three</Panel>
        <TextBox label="Grows" labelMode="hidden" placeholder="I grow" grow />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Spacing

`gap` and `padding` take a step of the spacing scale, a number of pixels or any CSS length.

| Value | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `'xxs' … 'xxl'` | A step of the spacing scale: `xxs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`, from the `layout.space.*` tokens (the design system's `space.1` … `space.12`). Density and themes reach them. |
| `12` | A number is pixels. |
| `'1.5rem'` | Any CSS length. |
| `'xs md'` | A padding takes one to four values, as in CSS (block-start, inline-end, block-end, inline-start), steps and lengths mixed. They follow the reading direction. |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const STEPS = ['xxs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', 'xxl'] as const;
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';

/** A gap from the spacing steps, a gap in pixels with a two-value padding, and a gap as a CSS length. */
export default function Spacing() {
  const s = reactive({ gap: 'sm' as string });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Gap">
        {STEPS.map((step) => (
          <Button key={step} text={step} size="sm" variant={() => (s.gap === step ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.gap === step} onclick={() => (s.gap = step)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack class="layout-gap-demo" orientation="horizontal" gap={() => s.gap} padding="xs">
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">A</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">B</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">C</Panel>
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={12} padding="xs md" style={FRAME}>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">12 pixels apart</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">padding xs md</Panel>
      </Stack>
      <Grid columns="* *" gap="1.5rem" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">1.5rem apart</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">in a Grid</Panel>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Grid

Rows and columns written like CSS. Children fill the cells in order, or say where they go: `row`, `column`, `rowSpan`, `columnSpan`, counted from 1.

| Tracks | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `'auto 1fr 2fr 120'` | CSS grid tracks; a bare number is pixels. |
| `'* 2*'` | `*` is `1fr`, `2*` is `2fr`. |
| `'minmax(8rem, 1fr) auto'` | Any CSS track, functions included. |
| `['auto', 120, '*']` | The same as a list. |
| `3` | A number: that many equal columns (or rows). |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A form on a Grid whose column count follows state; Street and the buttons span columns. */
export default function GridForm() {
  const s = reactive({ columns: 2 });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Columns">
        {[1, 2, 3].map((n) => (
          <Button key={n} text={`${n} column${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`} size="sm" variant={() => (s.columns === n ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.columns === n} onclick={() => (s.columns = n)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Grid class="layout-form" columns={() => s.columns} gap="sm" align="end" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <TextBox label="First name" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Last name" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Street" stretch column={1} columnSpan={() => Math.min(2, s.columns)} />
        <TextBox label="City" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Postal code" stretch />
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" justify="end" gap="xs" column="1" columnSpan={() => s.columns}>
          <Button text="Cancel" variant="ghost" />
          <Button text="Save" tone="accent" />
        </Stack>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Grid, Panel } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A fixed column and two flexible ones, a fixed row, and a child placed by row and column. */
export default function GridTracks() {
  return (
    <Grid class="layout-tracks" columns="120 * 2*" rows="auto 4rem" gap="xs" style="inline-size: 100%">
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">120px</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">1fr</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">2fr</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs" column={2} columnSpan={2}>
        row 2, columns 2–3
      </Panel>
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

## Panel

A plain box: padding, a frame if you want one, and its own scrolling. A scrolling panel is a Tab stop, so it can be scrolled with the keys; `text` names it.

```tsx
import { Panel } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A named panel that scrolls, a card and an outline. */
export default function Panels() {
  return (
    <>
      <Panel class="layout-scroll" text="Terms" scrollable="vertical" padding="md" variant="outline" style="block-size: 8rem; inline-size: 18rem">
        <p>1. The service is offered as it is.</p>
        <p>2. You keep the rights to what you upload.</p>
        <p>3. We may change these terms with a notice of 30 days.</p>
        <p>4. Either side may end the agreement at any time.</p>
        <p>5. The law of the place you live in applies.</p>
      </Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="md">
        A card
      </Panel>
      <Panel variant="outline" padding="md">
        An outline
      </Panel>
    </>
  );
}
```

## GroupBox

A titled frame around related controls: a `<fieldset>`, so screen readers name the group by its title and disabling it disables what is inside. The title's `&` key focuses the first control; `collapsible` makes the title show and hide the content.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, GroupBox, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A group with an access key that is enabled from state, and one that opens and closes. */
export default function GroupBoxes() {
  const s = reactive({ editing: true });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Enabled" size="sm" variant="outline" toggle x-model={() => s.editing} />
      <Grid columns="* *" gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%" align="start">
        <GroupBox title="&Address" enabled={() => s.editing}>
          <TextBox label="Street" stretch />
          <TextBox label="City" stretch />
        </GroupBox>
        <GroupBox title="More &options" collapsible collapsed>
          <TextBox label="Coupon" stretch />
          <TextBox label="Gift note" stretch />
        </GroupBox>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

## DockPanel

Children stick to the edges in the order they come — `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end` (these two follow the reading direction) — and `fill` takes what is left. A `float` child sits over the rest at its own `left` / `top` / `right` / `bottom`. Laid out with CSS grid: nothing runs when the size changes.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DockPanel, Panel, Stack, TextBox, type Dock } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const FOLDERS = ['Inbox', 'Drafts', 'Sent', 'Archive', 'Spam', 'Trash'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';
const BAR = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-bar);';
const LAYER = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer);';

/** A mail app laid out with DockPanel: a header, a sidebar that changes sides, a status bar, a float button and a panel added from code. */
export default function AppShell() {
  const s = reactive({ side: 'start' as Dock, messages: 3 });
  let shell: DockPanel | null = null;
  let notes: Panel | null = null;

  const toggleNotes = () => {
    if (notes) {
      shell?.controls.remove(notes);
      notes = null;
      return;
    }
    notes = new Panel({ dock: 'end', padding: 'sm' });
    notes.element.setAttribute('style', `inline-size: 9rem; ${LAYER}`);
    notes.element.classList.add('layout-notes');
    notes.controls.add(<span>Notes, added from code.</span>);
    shell?.controls.add(notes);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text={() => `Sidebar: ${s.side}`} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.side = s.side === 'start' ? 'end' : 'start')} />
        <Button text="Notes panel from code" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={toggleNotes} />
      </Stack>
      <DockPanel class="layout-shell" ref={(c: DockPanel) => (shell = c)} style={`block-size: 22rem; inline-size: 100%; overflow: hidden; ${FRAME}`}>
        <Stack dock="top" orientation="horizontal" align="center" gap="sm" padding="xs sm" style={BAR}>
          <strong>Mail</strong>
          <TextBox label="Search mail" labelMode="hidden" placeholder="Search" grow />
          <Button text="New" tone="accent" onclick={() => s.messages++} />
        </Stack>
        <Panel class="layout-side" dock={() => s.side} scrollable="vertical" padding="xs" text="Mailboxes" style={`inline-size: 11rem; ${LAYER}`}>
          <Stack gap="xxs">
            {FOLDERS.map((f) => (
              <Button key={f} text={f} variant="ghost" stretch />
            ))}
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
        <Stack class="layout-status" dock="bottom" orientation="horizontal" justify="space-between" padding="xxs sm" style={BAR}>
          <span>Ready</span>
          <span>{() => `${s.messages} messages`}</span>
        </Stack>
        <Panel class="layout-content" text="Message" scrollable padding="md">
          <h3 style="margin-block-start: 0">Welcome</h3>
          <p>The header, the folders and the status bar are docked; this panel fills the rest and scrolls on its own.</p>
          <p>Switch the sidebar to the other side, or add a panel from code: the layout follows at once.</p>
        </Panel>
        <Button class="layout-help" dock="float" right={16} bottom={48} text="Help" variant="outline" />
      </DockPanel>
    </>
  );
}
```

## SplitContainer

Two panes, `first` and `second`, with a splitter between them that the pointer drags and the keys move. `fixedPanel` keeps one pane's size when the container is resized; the minimum sizes hold; Enter hides the first pane and brings it back. Split containers nest.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Panel, SplitContainer, Stack, type SplitPanel, type SplitPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const FOLDERS = ['Inbox', 'Drafts', 'Sent', 'Archive', 'Spam', 'Trash'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';
const LAYER = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer);';

/** A split container inside another: a position bound with x-model, minimum sizes, a fixed pane, and hiding a pane from code. */
export default function NestedSplit() {
  const s = reactive({ tree: 180 as SplitPosition, fixed: 'first' as SplitPanel, log: '' });
  let outer: SplitContainer | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Hide folders" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => outer?.collapse('first')} />
        <Button text="Restore" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => outer?.restore()} />
        <Button text={() => `fixedPanel: ${s.fixed}`} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.fixed = s.fixed === 'first' ? 'none' : 'first')} />
        <output class="layout-split-out">{() => `position: ${s.tree}`}</output>
        <output class="layout-split-log">{() => s.log}</output>
      </Stack>
      <SplitContainer
        class="layout-split"
        ref={(c: SplitContainer) => (outer = c)}
        position={180}
        fixedPanel={() => s.fixed}
        firstMinSize={120}
        secondMinSize={200}
        x-model={() => s.tree}
        onSplitterMoved={(e: { position: SplitPosition; byUser: boolean; collapsed: SplitPanel }) => (s.log = `moved${e.byUser ? ' by you' : ''}${e.collapsed !== 'none' ? `, ${e.collapsed} hidden` : ''}`)}
        style={`block-size: 20rem; inline-size: 100%; ${FRAME}`}
      >
        <Panel text="Folders" scrollable padding="sm" style={LAYER}>
          <Stack gap="xxs">
            {FOLDERS.map((f) => (
              <Button key={f} text={f} variant="ghost" stretch />
            ))}
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
        <SplitContainer orientation="vertical" position="65%" secondMinSize={48}>
          <Panel text="Editor" scrollable padding="sm">
            <p>Drag the splitters, or Tab to one and use the arrow keys, Home, End and Enter.</p>
          </Panel>
          <Panel text="Output" scrollable padding="sm" style={LAYER}>
            <code>Build finished in 1.2 s.</code>
          </Panel>
        </SplitContainer>
      </SplitContainer>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | The splitter is one Tab stop between the panes; a scrolling `Panel` is a Tab stop of its own. |
| `Left / Right (side by side), Up / Down (one over the other)` | Move the splitter by `step`; Left and Right follow what you see in a right-to-left page. |
| `Home / End` | The first pane at its smallest / largest size. |
| `Enter` | Hides the first pane, or restores the splitter where it was. |
| `Alt + key (`&Address`)` | Focuses the first control in a `GroupBox` (Control + Option + key on Apple platforms). |
| `Arrows, Page Up / Down` | Scroll a focused scrolling `Panel`, as the browser does. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Splitter` | `role="separator"`, focusable, `aria-valuenow` (the first pane's share, 0–100), `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax`, `aria-orientation`, `aria-controls` the first pane, named from `splitterLabel` or `uiLocale` (the ARIA window splitter pattern). |
| `Hidden pane` | `inert`: out of reach of Tab and screen readers; focus inside moves to the splitter. |
| `GroupBox` | A native `<fieldset>`, named by its `<legend>`; disabled, it disables the native controls inside. A collapsible one has a button with `aria-expanded`. |
| `Panel` | With `text`, a region landmark of that name. Scrolling, it is a Tab stop. |
| `Order` | Stack, Grid and DockPanel place children with CSS only: Tab and screen readers keep the document order, so write the children in reading order. |

## Localization

The only text the containers write is the splitter's name, `uiLocale.strings.resize`, unless `splitterLabel` gives one.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { kitTexts } from '../../../shared/kit-texts';

/** Switches the texts of the kit; the splitters on the page take the new name at once. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ lang: 'en' });
  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };
  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <span>
        The splitter is named <output class="layout-resize">{() => kitTexts.strings.resize}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-stack` | `data-orientation`, `data-align`, `data-justify`, `data-wrap`, `data-reverse`, `data-inline`; a growing child gets `data-mx-grow`. |
| `.mx-grid` | `data-align`, `data-justify`, `data-inline`; tracks and child places are inline grid properties. |
| `.mx-panel` | `data-variant`, `data-scroll`. |
| `.mx-group-box` | `data-variant`, `data-collapsible`, `data-collapsed`, `data-disabled`; `.mx-group-box__legend`, `__title`, `__toggle`, `__chevron`. |
| `.mx-dock-panel` | Each child gets `data-mx-dock`; its place and the `gap` (a margin on the side facing the rest) are inline. |
| `.mx-split-container` | `data-orientation`, `data-collapsed`, `data-resizable`, `data-dragging`; `.mx-split-container__pane` (`data-pane`), `__splitter`. |
| `--_gap, --_row-gap, --_column-gap` | Written inline from `gap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap` (Stack, Grid, GroupBox). |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `layout.space.xxs … xxl` | The spacing steps of `gap` and `padding`. |
| `layout.gap` | The gap of Stack and Grid when none is given. |
| `layout.panel` | Unit: a panel (`outline`: a frame, `card`: a raised surface). |
| `layout.group, layout.group-caption, layout.group-toggle, layout.group-chevron` | Units: a group box (`plain`, `collapsed`), its caption, the button that folds it and its chevron. |
| `layout.group-box.gap, layout.group-box.legend-float` | The gap inside a group box when none is given; where its caption sits. |
| `layout.splitter-handle, layout.splitter-line, layout.splitter-grip` | Units: the splitter (`focus`), its line and its grip (`active`, `disabled`). |
| `layout.splitter.*` | `size` (the area that takes the pointer), `line-width`, `active-width`, `grip-length`, `grip-thickness`. |

## API reference

Every container also has the shared properties of `Control`: `enabled` / `disabled` (cascading to everything inside), `visible`, `tabStop`, `tabIndex`.

### Stack props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Bind<'horizontal' \| 'vertical'>` | `'vertical'` | `horizontal` follows the reading direction. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.gap` | The space between the children. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `align` | `Bind<LayoutAlign>` | `'stretch'` | Across the direction: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`, `baseline`. |
| `justify` | `Bind<StackJustify>` | `'start'` | Along it: `start`, `center`, `end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`. |
| `wrap` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Children that do not fit go on to a new line. |
| `reverse` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The children are laid out from the other end (Tab order stays the document order). |
| `inline` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Flows in a line of text, as wide as its children. |

### Grid props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns, rows` | `Bind<GridTracks>` | one column | See Grid tracks. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.gap` | Between rows and columns. |
| `rowGap, columnGap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `gap` | One direction only. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `autoRows, autoColumns` | `Bind<number \| string>` | `'auto'` | The size of tracks made as needed (a number is pixels). |
| `flow` | `Bind<GridFlow>` | `'row'` | How children without a place fill the grid: `row`, `column`, `row dense`, `column dense`. |
| `align` | `Bind<LayoutAlign>` | `'stretch'` | Where children sit in their cells, up and down. |
| `justify` | `Bind<GridJustify>` | `'stretch'` | Where children sit in their cells, along the row. |
| `inline` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Flows in a line of text. |

### Panel props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scrollable` | `Bind<boolean \| 'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'>` | `false` | Scrolls its content; it is then a Tab stop, so the keys scroll it. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `variant` | `Bind<PanelVariant>` | `'plain'` | `plain`, `outline` (a border), `card` (a card surface). |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Names the panel: it becomes a region landmark with that name. |

### GroupBox props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The legend; `&Address` makes Alt+A focus the first control inside. The same property as `text`. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The title is a button that shows and hides the content. |
| `collapsed` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The content is hidden (with `collapsible`). |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.group-box.padding` | The space inside the frame. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.group-box.gap` | The space between the children (they stack in a column). |
| `variant` | `Bind<GroupBoxVariant>` | `'outline'` | `outline` (a frame, the title on its edge) or `plain` (the title over the content). |

### DockPanel props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space between a docked child and what it docks against. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |

### SplitContainer props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Bind<'horizontal' \| 'vertical'>` | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal`: the panes side by side, as in Stack; `vertical`: one over the other. |
| `position` | `Bind<SplitPosition>` | `'50%'` | The size of the pane that keeps its size (the first one with `fixedPanel="none"`): pixels, a share, a CSS length. `x-model` binds it. |
| `fixedPanel` | `Bind<'none' \| 'first' \| 'second'>` | `'none'` | The pane that keeps its size when the container is resized. `none`: both grow, the position is kept as a share. |
| `firstMinSize, secondMinSize` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The smallest size of each pane, in pixels. |
| `collapsed` | `Bind<'none' \| 'first' \| 'second'>` | `'none'` | A pane that is hidden; the other takes all the room. |
| `resizable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The pointer and the keys move the splitter. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Enter and a double click hide and restore the first pane. |
| `step` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | How far an arrow key moves the splitter, in pixels. |
| `splitterLabel` | `Bind<string>` | `uiLocale.strings.resize` | The splitter's accessible name. |

### Props a child gives its container

| Prop | Read by | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grow` | Stack | `Bind<boolean \| number>` | Takes the free space along the direction; numbers share it in proportion. |
| `row, column` | Grid | `Bind<number \| string>` | The line it starts at, from 1 (a string goes to CSS as it is: `-1`). |
| `rowSpan, columnSpan` | Grid | `Bind<number>` | How many tracks it covers. |
| `dock` | DockPanel | `Bind<Dock>` | `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`, `fill` (default) or `float`. |
| `left, top, right, bottom` | DockPanel | `Bind<number \| string>` | The anchors of a `float` child; a number is pixels; `left` + `right` stretch it. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write, reactive | A value or a function, like the prop. |
| `SplitContainer.first, second` | read-only | The panes, two `Panel`s: `split.first.controls.add(…)`, `split.second.scrollable = true`. |
| `SplitContainer.splitterElement` | read-only | The `role="separator"` element. |
| `SplitContainer.value` | read/write | `position`, for `x-model`. |
| `GroupBox.legendElement` | read-only | The `<legend>`. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stack.setGrow(child, grow), growOf(child)` | `void`, value | A child's `grow` from code (a value or a function). |
| `Grid.setCell(child, cell), cellOf(child)` | `void`, `GridCell` | A child's `row`, `column`, `rowSpan`, `columnSpan` from code. |
| `DockPanel.setDock(child, dock), dockOf(child)` | `void`, `Dock` | A child's `dock` from code. |
| `DockPanel.setAnchors(child, anchors)` | `void` | The `left` / `top` / `right` / `bottom` of a `float` child. |
| `SplitContainer.collapse(pane?), restore()` | `void` | Hides a pane (the first by default) / shows both again. |
| `GroupBox.focus()` | `boolean` | Focuses the first control inside, opening a collapsed box. |

### Events

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `SplitContainer.onSplitterMoved(e)` | The splitter moved (at the end of a drag), or a pane was hidden or restored. `e`: `{ position, collapsed, byUser, source }`. |
| `GroupBox.onToggled(e)` | The content was shown or hidden. `e`: `{ collapsed, byUser, source }`. |

`ChildSettings` — the part that reads a child's settings from its props and follows children added later — is exported for containers of your own.

# ScrollView

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Content that scrolls in a box of its own: the bars shown as told, a pull from the top that asks for what is new, a reach near the end that asks for more. Moved from code to a position or to an element.

## Import

```tsx
import { ScrollView } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## A box that scrolls

The JSX children are the content. `showScrollbar` says when the bars show; `scrollTo` and `scrollToElement` move the content from code, `onScrolled` tells where it stands.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, ScrollView, Stack, type ScrollViewBars } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const LINES = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => `Line ${i + 1} of a long text that needs a box of its own to scroll in.`);
const MODES: ScrollViewBars[] = ['onScroll', 'onHover', 'always', 'never'];

/** A box that scrolls, its bars shown as told; moved from code to a line and back to the top. */
export default function Bars() {
    const s = reactive({ bars: 'onScroll' as ScrollViewBars, top: 0 });
    let view!: ScrollView;
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                {MODES.map(mode => (
                    <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.bars === mode ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.bars = mode)} />
                ))}
                <Button text="Line 20" variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => view.scrollToElement(view.content.element.querySelectorAll('p')[19], true)} />
                <Button text="Top" variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => view.scrollTo(0, true)} />
                <output class="sv-top">{() => `scrollTop: ${Math.round(s.top)}`}</output>
            </Stack>
            <ScrollView ref={(v: ScrollView) => (view = v)} label="Long text" class="sv-text" showScrollbar={() => s.bars} style="block-size: 12rem" onScrolled={e => (s.top = e.top)}>
                {LINES.map(line => (
                    <p key={line}>{line}</p>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Pull to refresh

With `pullToRefresh`, the content pulled down from its top asks `onPullDown`. Set `promise` (or call `release()`) and the panel goes when the work is done.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Panel, ScrollView, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Pulled down from the top, the list asks for what is new and shows the panel until the promise settles. */
export default function Pull() {
    const s = reactive({ notes: ['Welcome aboard', 'Your plan was renewed', 'A new comment on "Roadmap"'], count: 0 });
    const reload = () =>
        new Promise<void>(resolve =>
            setTimeout(() => {
                s.count++;
                s.notes = [`Fresh note ${s.count}`, ...s.notes];
                resolve();
            }, 1200)
        );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <span>Drag the list down from its top (a finger, or the mouse) and let go.</span>
            <ScrollView label="Notes" class="sv-notes" pullToRefresh onPullDown={e => (e.promise = reload())} style="block-size: 12rem">
                {s.notes.map(note => (
                    <Panel key={note} variant="outline" padding="sm">
                        {note}
                    </Panel>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Load more near the end

With `loadOnReachBottom`, a scroll within `reachBottomOffset` of the end asks `onReachBottom` once; `release()` lets the next reach ask again, `release(true)` says there is no more. Content that does not fill the box asks at once.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Panel, ScrollView, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TOTAL = 60;
const PAGE = 15;

// A page of rows, as a server would send them.
const fetchRows = (from: number) =>
    new Promise<string[]>(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve(Array.from({ length: Math.min(PAGE, TOTAL - from) }, (_, i) => `Order #${1000 + from + i}`)), 800));

/** Near the end the view asks for more; the indicator stays until the rows are in, and `release(true)` ends it for good when there is no more. */
export default function More() {
    const s = reactive({ rows: [] as string[] });
    const more = () =>
        fetchRows(s.rows.length).then(rows => {
            s.rows = [...s.rows, ...rows];
            return s.rows.length >= TOTAL;
        });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <output class="sv-more-told">{() => (s.rows.length >= TOTAL ? `All ${TOTAL} orders are in.` : `${s.rows.length} of ${TOTAL} orders`)}</output>
            <ScrollView label="Orders" class="sv-orders" loadOnReachBottom reachBottomOffset={80} onReachBottom={e => more().then(done => e.release(done))} style="block-size: 14rem">
                {s.rows.map(row => (
                    <Panel key={row} variant="outline" padding="sm">
                        {row}
                    </Panel>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Behaviour

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Scrolling` | The box scrolls with the wheel, the keys when focused, a finger, and from code. `direction` locks the other axis; the page behind does not scroll on when the content ends. |
| `Scrollbars` | The design system’s bars. With `onScroll` the thumb shows while the content moves and goes a moment after; with `onHover` while the pointer is over the view or focus is in it; `always` leaves them; `never` hides them, the content still scrolls. |
| `Pull to refresh` | From the top, with a finger or the pointer: the content comes down (harder the farther it goes) and the panel above it says to pull, then to release. Let go far enough it refreshes: the spinner turns until `release()` or the promise. A short pull goes back. |
| `Load more` | Within `reachBottomOffset` of the end, `onReachBottom` is asked once; the panel under the content shows meanwhile. Released, the next reach asks again, until `release(true)`. Content that does not fill the box asks at once, and again as it grows. |
| `Texts` | The kit’s, in the kit language, unless the text props say otherwise. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Region` | A focusable box named by `label`; the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End scroll it as the browser does. |
| `Panels` | Live regions: “Refreshing…” and “Loading…” are read when they appear. |
| `Spinners` | Decorative; the texts say what is going on. |
| `Motion` | A finger that pulls does not scroll the page; a finger that scrolls does not pull. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-scroll-view` | The box. `data-direction`, `data-bars`, `data-scrolling` while the content moves, `data-pull` when pulling is on, `data-pulling` during a pull, `data-pull-state` (`pull`, `release`, `refreshing`), `data-loading`. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__content` | What holds the children; it moves down during a pull. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__pull, .mx-scroll-view__pull-text, .mx-scroll-view__pull-spinner` | The panel above the content, its text and the kit’s spinner. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__bottom, .mx-scroll-view__bottom-text, .mx-scroll-view__bottom-spinner` | The panel under the content while more loads. |

### Component tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `scroll-view.box` | Unit: the box (`focus`). |
| `scroll-view.pull, .pull-text, .bottom, .bottom-text` | Units: the two panels (the pull one `release` and `refreshing`) and their texts. |
| `scroll-view.panel-height, .panel-gap` | The panels’ height; the space between a panel’s spinner and its text. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `Bind<ScrollViewDirection>` | `'vertical'` | `vertical`, `horizontal` or `both`: which way the content scrolls. |
| `showScrollbar` | `Bind<ScrollViewBars>` | `'onScroll'` | When the bars show: `onScroll` while scrolling, `onHover` while the pointer is over the view, `always`, `never`. |
| `pullToRefresh` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Pulling the content down from its top asks `onPullDown` for what is new. |
| `loadOnReachBottom` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Scrolling near the end asks `onReachBottom` for more; so does content that does not reach the end. |
| `reachBottomOffset` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | Pixels before the end at which `onReachBottom` is asked. |
| `pullDownText, releaseText, refreshingText` | `Bind<string>` | the kit’s texts | The pull panel’s texts: while pulling, once far enough, while refreshing. |
| `reachBottomText` | `Bind<string>` | the kit’s “Loading…” | The text under the content while more loads. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | What screen readers call the scrolling region. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onPullDown` | event | The content was pulled down and let go. Load what is new, then `release()`, or set `promise` and the panel goes when it settles. |
| `onReachBottom` | event | The content was scrolled near its end. Load more, then `release()`; `release(true)` says there is no more and the view stops asking. A `promise` releases too. |
| `onScrolled` | event | The position changed: `top`, `left`. |
| `scrollTo(where, smooth?)` | `void` | To a top, or `{ top, left }`; `smooth` animates. |
| `scrollBy({ top, left }, smooth?)` | `void` | By a distance. |
| `scrollToElement(target, smooth?)` | `void` | Brings an element (or a component) of the content into view. |
| `refresh(), release()` | `void` | Starts a refresh as a pull would; ends it. |
| `loadMore(), update()` | `boolean` / `void` | Asks for more now; looks at the position again after the content changed. |
| `scrollTop, scrollLeft` | read-only | Where the content stands. |
| `isRefreshing, isLoading` | read-only | A refresh or a loading is going on. |
| `content` | read-only | The element that holds the children, between the two panels. |
