## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Up / Down` | The row above or below (it is the selected one). |
| `Home / End, PageUp / PageDown` | The first and the last row; a screen of rows. |
| `Space` | Shows the tooltip, as a click does. |
| `Enter` | Opens the form, as a double click does. |
| `Delete` | Deletes the appointment (asking first). |
| `T, N / P, A` | Today, the next and the previous days; `keys.agendaView` (A) shows the agenda. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `List` | A list box; each day (in its group) is a group of options named by the day. |
| `Rows` | An option per appointment: its text, its time, whether it goes on and how it repeats. The focused row is the selected one. |
| `Empty` | With no appointments the list is left out and the text says so. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `scheduler.agenda, agenda-group (`first`), agenda-resource` | Units: the list, a day (and the line over it), a group’s name. |
| `scheduler.agenda-day (`today`), agenda-weekday (`today`), agenda-month, day-number `agenda`` | Units: a day’s head and its parts. |
| `scheduler.agenda-row (`hover`, `selected`, `open`, `focus`, `past`, `disabled`), agenda-content` | Units: a row and its parts side by side. |
| `scheduler.agenda-time, agenda-dot, agenda-text, agenda-empty` | Units: the time column, the appointment’s colour (none unless a language draws it), the text, the empty text. |
| `agenda-time-width` | Plain token: the time column’s width. |

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agendaDuration` | `Bind<number>` | 7 | The days the agenda shows, from the date shown; a view’s own wins. Previous and next move by them. |
| `groups` | `Bind<string[]>` | `[]` | With groups, each group’s days stand under its name (the group’s own appointments). |
| `agendaRowTemplate` | `Bind<((context: AgendaRowContext) => Component) \\| null>` | `null` | A row’s content: `{ appointment, start, end, text, time, allDay, date, group }`; the row keeps its colour, keys and name. |
| `appointmentTooltipTemplate` | `Bind<((context: TooltipTemplateContext) => Component) \\| null>` | `null` | The tooltip’s content, in every view. |
| `texts.schedulerNoAppointments` | `string` | "No appointments" | What it says when its days have none (`uiLocale`). |

## Example files

`Agenda.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { NumberBox, Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * The coming days as a list: each day with its appointments in time order, a day with none left
 * out. Up and Down move over the rows, Space shows the tooltip, Enter opens the form, Delete
 * deletes. Previous and next move by the days shown.
 */
export default function Agenda() {
  const s = reactive({ days: 7 });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <NumberBox label="Days" labelMode="side" min={1} max={31} x-model={() => s.days} />
      <Scheduler<Meeting> appointments={sampleAppointments()} views={['agenda', 'week', 'month']} currentView="agenda" agendaDuration={() => s.days} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`AgendaTemplates.tsx`

```tsx
import { Button, Scheduler, type AgendaRowContext, type TooltipTemplateContext } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { jobs, members, type Job } from './timeline-data';

/**
 * An agenda row drawn by `agendaRowTemplate` (the person's name after the job), and a tooltip of
 * its own (`appointmentTooltipTemplate`) with the time and a button to open the form. The row
 * keeps its colour, keys and name.
 */
export default function AgendaTemplates() {
  const resources = [{ field: 'ownerId', label: 'Person', items: members, useColorAsDefault: true }];
  const person = (job: Job) => members.find((m) => m.id === job.ownerId)?.text ?? '';
  const row = (c: AgendaRowContext<Job>) => (
    <span class="sched-agenda-row">
      <strong>{c.time}</strong>
      <span>{c.text}</span>
      <small>{person(c.appointment)}</small>
    </span>
  );
  const tip = (c: TooltipTemplateContext<Job>) => (
    <div class="sched-tip">
      <strong>{() => c.text}</strong>
      <span>{() => c.time}</span>
      <span>{() => (c.appointment ? person(c.appointment) : '')}</span>
      <Button text="Open" visible={() => c.canEdit} onclick={() => c.edit()} />
    </div>
  );
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Scheduler<Job>
        appointments={jobs()}
        resources={resources}
        views={[{ type: 'agenda', agendaDuration: 2 }, 'week']}
        currentView="agenda"
        agendaRowTemplate={row}
        appointmentTooltipTemplate={tip}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Scheduler: Big data

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Thousands of resources and appointments: the scheduler builds only what is in view, and lays out only what changed.

## 1,000 resources, 10,000 appointments

A timeline week with a row for each of 1,000 lines and 10,000 tasks over them (generated). Scroll down and sideways: the rows, cells and tasks in view are built as they come. The line under it says how long the first show took and how many elements the scheduler holds.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';

export interface Task {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  resourceId: number;
}

export interface Machine {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  color: string;
}

const COLORS = ['#1565c0', '#2e7d32', '#6a1b9a', '#ad1457', '#ef6c00', '#00838f', '#455a64', '#5d4037'];
const WORK = ['Cut', 'Weld', 'Paint', 'Check', 'Pack', 'Load', 'Clean', 'Test'];

/** `count` resources, named and coloured in turn. */
export function machines(count: number): Machine[] {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, text: `Line ${String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`, color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] }));
}

/**
 * `count` tasks over the week of `day`, spread over the resources: each one an hour or a few long,
 * in the working hours, some over each other (a pseudo-random spread, the same each time).
 */
export function tasks(count: number, resources: number, day = new Date()): Task[] {
  const monday = new Date(day.getFullYear(), day.getMonth(), day.getDate() - ((day.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  let seed = 7;
  const next = () => (seed = (seed * 48271) % 2147483647) / 2147483647;
  const out: Task[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const start = new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + Math.floor(next() * 7), 6 + Math.floor(next() * 12), next() < 0.5 ? 0 : 30);
    const end = new Date(start.getTime() + (1 + Math.floor(next() * 4)) * 3_600_000);
    out.push({ id: i + 1, text: `${WORK[i % WORK.length]} ${i + 1}`, startDate: start, endDate: end, resourceId: 1 + (i % resources) });
  }
  return reactive(out) as Task[];
}
```

## 200 groups in a week

A week grouped by 200 lines: 1,400 columns of 48 cells and 4,000 tasks. Only the columns in view (and a screen on each side) are built.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';

export interface Task {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  resourceId: number;
}

export interface Machine {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  color: string;
}

const COLORS = ['#1565c0', '#2e7d32', '#6a1b9a', '#ad1457', '#ef6c00', '#00838f', '#455a64', '#5d4037'];
const WORK = ['Cut', 'Weld', 'Paint', 'Check', 'Pack', 'Load', 'Clean', 'Test'];

/** `count` resources, named and coloured in turn. */
export function machines(count: number): Machine[] {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, text: `Line ${String(i + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`, color: COLORS[i % COLORS.length] }));
}

/**
 * `count` tasks over the week of `day`, spread over the resources: each one an hour or a few long,
 * in the working hours, some over each other (a pseudo-random spread, the same each time).
 */

  const monday = new Date(day.getFullYear(), day.getMonth(), day.getDate() - ((day.getDay() + 6) % 7));

  const out: Task[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const start = new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + Math.floor(next() * 7), 6 + Math.floor(next() * 12), next() < 0.5 ? 0 : 30);
    const end = new Date(start.getTime() + (1 + Math.floor(next() * 4)) * 3_600_000);
    out.push({ id: i + 1, text: `${WORK[i % WORK.length]} ${i + 1}`, startDate: start, endDate: end, resourceId: 1 + (i % resources) });
  }
  return reactive(out) as Task[];
}
```

## How it stays fast

| Part | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Rows of a timeline` | Through `Virtualization`: only the rows in view (and a few on each side) are built. Each row is as tall as its lanes; the model works the height out (lanes × lane height), the list reads it. While an appointment is dragged its rows grow in place and the list is given the heights after. |
| `Cells along the time` | A window kept by the model (`setWindow`): the cells and appointments of the part in view and a screen on each side. Scrolling moves the window on by a few cells at a time; the rows show it through a keyed `.map` over the window’s slice. |
| `Columns of a day or a week` | The same window over the columns: with many groups only the columns in view are built, each at its own place. |
| `Layout` | Each row of a timeline is laid out on its own; a drag lays out only the rows it was and is in. The appointments are read once for every layout until they change. |
| `Data source` | The range shown is what is asked for (`rangeFilter`), with the resources shown when grouped by a field of one value. |

```tsx
// A data source is asked for what is shown: the days, and the resources of the groups.
<Scheduler dataSource={source} remoteFiltering groups={['resourceId']} views={['timelineWeek']} />
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scrolling` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'standard' \| 'virtual'>` | `'auto'` | Every row and cell built (`'standard'`), or only what is in view (`'virtual'`); `'auto'`: virtual past about 2,000 cells (rows × cells along the time, columns × time rows). A view’s own wins. |

## Example files

`BigTimeline.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { machines, tasks, type Task } from './big-data';

/**
 * 1,000 resources and 10,000 tasks in a timeline week. Only the rows in view are built (through
 * `Virtualization`, each as tall as its lanes), and in each row only the cells and tasks of the part
 * of the week in view. The numbers under it are measured as it shows and as you scroll.
 */
export default function BigTimeline() {
  const resources = [{ field: 'resourceId', label: 'Line', items: machines(1000), useColorAsDefault: true }];
  const s = reactive({ shown: '', nodes: 0 });
  const started = performance.now();
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Scheduler<Task>
        appointments={tasks(10_000, 1000)}
        resources={resources}
        groups={['resourceId']}
        views={['timelineWeek', 'timelineDay']}
        currentView="timelineWeek"
        cellDuration={60}
        onContentReady={(e) => {
          // Shown: the frame after its first appointments are on the page.
          const look = () => {
            const el = e.source.element;
            if (!el.querySelector('.mx-scheduler__scroll .mx-scheduler__appointment')) return void requestAnimationFrame(look);
            requestAnimationFrame(() => {
              if (!s.shown) s.shown = `${Math.round(performance.now() - started)} ms`;
              s.nodes = el.querySelectorAll('*').length;
            });
          };
          look();
        }}
      />
      <p class="sched-log">{() => (s.shown ? `Shown in ${s.shown}; ${s.nodes.toLocaleString()} elements on the page.` : 'Building…')}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Scheduler: Tablet and phone

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

On a tablet and a phone the scheduler keeps its appointments, views and date and shows them another way: a phone gets the agenda, a compact bar and sheets from the bottom; a finger lifts, resizes, swipes and pinches.

## Import

```tsx
import { Scheduler, type SchedulerPresentation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Three ways to show one scheduler

| Presentation | What shows |
| --- | --- |
| `Desktop` | As it is: the bar with Today, the steps, the date and a button per view; the tooltip next to the appointment, the form in a window. |
| `Tablet` | As on a desktop, its view kept (a week, as tablet calendars open); on a touch screen everything a finger taps is larger. |
| `Phone` | The agenda (a day when the views have no agenda). The bar holds Today as an icon, the month (opening the calendar) and one menu of the views; a swipe moves between days. The tooltip is an action sheet, the form a sheet from the bottom. A narrower ruler, resource column and time column, so a week still fits the screen; every view works. |

## A finger

The listeners are on the scheduler before a finger lands, so a lifted appointment, a swipe and a pinch keep the page still; anything else scrolls natively. After a drag no click follows, and nothing a finger touched stays looking hovered. Open this page on a phone, or with the browser's touch emulation.

| Gesture | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Tap an appointment` | Its tooltip (an action sheet on a phone): Edit, Delete. |
| `Hold an appointment, then drag` | Lifts it after a moment and moves it; the page does not scroll while it is lifted. Let go where it may go. |
| `Let go of a lifted appointment` | It stays selected with a handle in the middle of its start and its end; drag a handle to resize it. A tap elsewhere puts it down. |
| `Swipe sideways over the view` | The next or the previous days. A view that can still scroll that way (a wide week, a timeline) scrolls first; at its end the swipe moves on. |
| `Pinch` | Zooms the hours of the day views and the cells of a timeline (`timeZoom`, 0.5 to 4). |
| `Tap a free cell, then tap it again` | Selects it, then opens the form for a new appointment there. |
| `Scroll` | Native scrolling, as everywhere on the page. |


## Accessibility

| Topic | How |
| --- | --- |
| `Without gestures` | Everything a gesture does has a button or a key: the month opens the calendar, the arrows move the focused appointment (Shift: its end), N and P the days. |
| `Sheets` | The tooltip and the form are dialogs: focus moves in and back, Escape and the back button close them. |
| `Sizes` | On a touch screen the bar, the agenda rows and the lines of the month take the language’s large control height. |

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `scheduler.bar `phone`` | Unit: the bar as on a phone. |
| `scheduler.appointment `lifted`, `selected`` | Unit states: the appointment a finger holds, and the one it let go (with its handles). |
| `scheduler.resize-grip (`active`)` | Unit: a handle, in the middle of an edge; down the side of a bar it is turned. |
| `scheduler.swipe-edge (`ready`), swipe-icon (`previous`, `ready`)` | Units: the mark at the side the next days come from while swiping. |
| `touch-target, touch-lane-size, phone-ruler-width, phone-column-min-width, phone-timeline-resource-width, phone-bar-size, swipe-inset, grip-ring, grip-ring-mix` | Plain tokens. |
| `today-icon-button, view-menu-button, tooltip-sheet, form-sheet` | Places: the kit’s buttons and sheets inside. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `presentation` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'desktop' \| 'tablet' \| 'phone'>` | `'auto'` | How it shows itself: by its own width, or always one way. The appointments, the views and the date stay the same. |
| `phoneWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `560` | Under this width (of the scheduler, not of the screen) `auto` shows it as on a phone, whatever the pointer. |
| `tabletWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `1024` | Under this width `auto` shows it as on a tablet, on a touch screen (see `tabletWhen`). |
| `tabletWhen` | `Bind<'touch' \| 'width'>` | `'touch'` | `'touch'`: as on a tablet only when the screen's pointer is a finger (`(pointer: coarse)`, followed live); `'width'`: the width alone. |
| `phoneView` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `'agenda'` | The view (by name or type) it shows as on a phone; a day when the views have none of it. Going back, it shows the view it had, unless the user chose another. `null` keeps the view. |
| `tabletView` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | The same, as on a tablet; `null` keeps the view. |
| `swipeNavigation` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A finger swiping sideways goes to the next or the previous days. |
| `pinchZoom` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Two fingers zoom the time scale. |
| `timeZoom` | `Bind<number>` | `1` | How far the time scale is zoomed: 1 as the design language sizes it, 0.5 to 4. |
| `onPresentationChanging` | `(e: SchedulerPresentationChangingEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to, width, cancel }`: refused, it keeps showing as it does until the width or the setting changes again. |
| `onPresentationChanged` | `(e: SchedulerPresentationChangedEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to, width }`. |
| `onTimeZoomChanging` | `(e: TimeZoomChangingEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to, cancel }`, as two fingers start to zoom; refused, the page zooms instead. |
| `onTimeZoomChanged` | `(e: TimeZoomChangedEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to }`, when the fingers let go. |
| `onFormOpening` | `(e: FormOpeningEventArgs) => void` | — | `e.form` is the window, or on a phone the `BottomSheet` the form comes up in. |

### Members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currentPresentation` | read-only, reactive | How it shows itself now: `'desktop'`, `'tablet'` or `'phone'`. |

The sheets are the kit's [BottomSheet](bottomsheet.md) and [ActionSheet](actionsheet.md).

## Example files

`Presentations.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { RadioGroup, Scheduler, Stack, type SchedulerPresentation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * One scheduler shown three ways. As on a phone it shows the agenda (a day where it has none), the
 * bar holds the month, Today and a menu of the views, the tooltip and the form come up from the
 * bottom. Going back, it shows the view it had. The appointments and the date stay the same.
 */
export default function Presentations() {
  const s = reactive({ presentation: 'phone' as SchedulerPresentation, said: '' });
  const scheduler = (
    <Scheduler<Meeting>
      appointments={sampleAppointments()}
      views={['day', 'week', 'month', 'agenda']}
      presentation={() => s.presentation}
      startDayHour={7}
      onPresentationChanged={(e) => (s.said = `${e.from} → ${e.to}${e.width ? ` (${e.width} px wide)` : ''}`)}
    />
  ) as Scheduler<Meeting>;
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Presentation"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'auto', text: 'By its width' },
            { value: 'desktop', text: 'Desktop' },
            { value: 'tablet', text: 'Tablet' },
            { value: 'phone', text: 'Phone' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.presentation}
        />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => (s.said ? `Shown: ${s.said}` : `Shown as: ${scheduler.currentPresentation}`)}</output>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
    </div>
  );
}
```

`PhoneFrame.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * A scheduler that goes by its own width (`presentation: 'auto'`), in a frame the size of a phone:
 * under 560 pixels it shows as on a phone, under 1024 as on a tablet (here by the width alone,
 * `tabletWhen: 'width'`, so a mouse shows it too). Drag the frame's corner, or pick a width.
 */
export default function PhoneFrame() {
  const s = reactive({ shown: '' });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;
  const width = (px: string) => (frame.element.style.inlineSize = px);
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="390 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('390px')} />
        <Button text="820 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('820px')} />
        <Button text="Full width" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('100%')} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.shown}</output>
      </Stack>
      <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)} class="sched-phone-frame">
        <Scheduler<Meeting>
          appointments={sampleAppointments()}
          views={['day', 'week', 'month', 'agenda']}
          tabletWhen="width"
          startDayHour={7}
          onPresentationChanged={(e) => (s.shown = `${e.to} at ${e.width} px`)}
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { NumberBox, Scheduler, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * A finger: hold an appointment to lift it and drag it; let go and its handles stay, drag one to
 * resize. Swipe sideways for the next or the previous days; pinch to zoom the hours. Tap a free
 * cell, then tap it again for a new appointment.
 */
export default function Touch() {

  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Switch label="Swipe between days" x-model={() => s.swipe} />
        <Switch label="Pinch to zoom" x-model={() => s.pinch} />
        <NumberBox label="Zoom" labelMode="side" min={0.5} max={4} step={0.25} x-model={() => s.zoom} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.said}</output>
      </Stack>
      <Scheduler<Meeting>
        appointments={sampleAppointments()}
        views={['day', 'week', 'timelineDay']}
        currentView="week"
        presentation="tablet"
        swipeNavigation={() => s.swipe}
        pinchZoom={() => s.pinch}
        timeZoom={() => s.zoom}
        onTimeZoomChanged={(e) => {
          s.zoom = e.to;
          s.said = `Zoomed from ${e.from.toFixed(2)} to ${e.to.toFixed(2)}`;
        }}
        onMoveEnd={(e) => (s.said = `${e.appointment.text} moved`)}
        onDateChanged={(e) => (s.said = e.byUser ? `Moved to ${e.to.toDateString()}` : s.said)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

# Scheduler: iCalendar and print

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

Appointments out to an iCalendar file and back in (RFC 5545), for use with other calendar applications; and the scheduler on paper.

## Import

```tsx
import { Scheduler, parseICalendar, writeICalendar } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Export

`exportICalendar()` writes the appointments of the days shown, or all of them. A series goes whole with its rule, so another calendar repeats it the same way.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { formatRuleDate } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export interface Booking {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  recurrenceRule?: string;
  recurrenceException?: string;
  recurrenceId?: number;
  startDateTimeZone?: string;
  endDateTimeZone?: string;
}

/** Series around this week: a daily standup with one day left out and one moved, a review every other week, a report on the last Friday, an all-day Friday. */
export function recurringAppointments(): Booking[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  const day = (offset: number, hour = 0, minute = 0) => new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
    {
      id: 1,
      text: 'Team standup',
      startDate: day(-21, 9),
      endDate: day(-21, 9, 30),
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR',
      // This Tuesday is left out; this Wednesday's is moved (appointment 2).
      recurrenceException: [day(1, 9), day(2, 9)].map((d) => formatRuleDate({ time: d.getTime(), utc: true, dateOnly: false })).join(','),
    },
    { id: 2, text: 'Team standup', startDate: day(2, 11), endDate: day(2, 11, 30), recurrenceId: 1 },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Design review',
      startDate: day(-11, 14),
      endDate: day(-11, 15, 30),
      color: '#7c4dff',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH',
    },
    {
      id: 4,
      text: 'Monthly report',
      startDate: day(-60, 16),
      endDate: day(-60, 17),
      color: '#c62828',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR',
    },
    {
      id: 5,
      text: 'Remote day',
      startDate: day(-3),
      endDate: day(-2),
      allDay: true,
      color: '#00838f',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR;COUNT=12',
    },
    { id: 6, text: 'Lunch with Ana', startDate: day(3, 12, 30), endDate: day(3, 13, 30), color: '#2e7d32' },
  ]) as Booking[];
}
```

## Import a file

`importICalendar(text)` reads the events and adds them as any new appointment is added: to the array, or through a data source's adapter.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack, TextArea } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Booking } from './recurring-appointments';

const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
const today = new Date();
const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
const date = (offset: number) => {
  const d = new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}${pad(d.getDate())}`;
};

/** A zone by its Windows name with its VTIMEZONE, a weekly series with one day left out, an all-day event, text folded and escaped. */
const FILE = [
  'BEGIN:VCALENDAR',
  'VERSION:2.0',
  'PRODID:-//Example//Calendar//EN',
  'BEGIN:VTIMEZONE',
  'TZID:W. Europe Standard Time',
  'BEGIN:STANDARD',
  'DTSTART:16010101T030000',
  'TZOFFSETFROM:+0200',
  'TZOFFSETTO:+0100',
  'RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU;BYMONTH=10',
  'END:STANDARD',
  'BEGIN:DAYLIGHT',
  'DTSTART:16010101T020000',
  'TZOFFSETFROM:+0100',
  'TZOFFSETTO:+0200',
  'RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU;BYMONTH=3',
  'END:DAYLIGHT',
  'END:VTIMEZONE',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:sync-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(0)}T100000`,
  `DTEND;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(0)}T110000`,
  'RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=12',
  `EXDATE;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(2)}T100000`,
  'SUMMARY:Sync with Berlin',
  'DESCRIPTION:Agenda:\n1. Status\, risks\n2. Next steps',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:offsite-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:${date(3)}`,
  `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:${date(5)}`,
  'SUMMARY:Team offsite',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:call-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART:${date(1)}T130000Z`,
  'DURATION:PT45M',
  'SUMMARY:Call with the customer about the long running rollout of the new pl',
  ' anning tool',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'END:VCALENDAR',
].join('\r\n');

/**
 * A file read in: each event is added through the data layer as any new appointment is (here an
 * array; a data source gets the same adds through its adapter), with `onAppointmentAdding` first.
 * Read it in again: an event whose UID is there already changes that appointment.
 */
export default function ImportCalendar() {
  const s = reactive({ text: FILE, said: '' });
  const scheduler = (<Scheduler<Booking> appointments={reactive([] as Booking[])} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} />) as Scheduler<Booking>;
  const read = async () => {
    const result = await scheduler.importICalendar(s.text);
    s.said = result ? `${result.added.length} added, ${result.updated.length} changed, ${result.failed.length} refused` : 'Not read in';
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <TextArea label="iCalendar file" rows={8} spellcheck={false} wrap="off" x-model={() => s.text} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Read in" tone="accent" onclick={() => void read()} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.said}</output>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## What is written and read

| iCalendar | The appointment |
| --- | --- |
| `UID` | The appointment’s key; an occurrence changed apart takes its series’ key. Read in, the UID is the new appointment’s key (with a data source, the adapter gives the key). |
| `DTSTART, DTEND (DURATION read too)` | On the appointment’s own zone (`fields.startTimeZone`, `endTimeZone`), else the scheduler’s `timeZone`, else the browser’s, with `TZID`; an all-day one as dates (`VALUE=DATE`, the end the day after). |
| `SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION` | The text and the description; escaped and folded at 75 octets as RFC 5545 says. |
| `RRULE` | The series’ rule; an `UNTIL` on the wall clock is written in UTC, as the RFC asks of a rule with a zone. |
| `EXDATE` | The times left out of a series, in the form of its start. |
| `RECURRENCE-ID` | An occurrence changed apart: the time of its series it replaces (the left-out time nearest to it). Read in, the series leaves that time out and the event names it (`fields.recurrenceId`). |
| `VTIMEZONE` | Written for every zone used, from the browser’s own time zone data (a rule a year when the changes follow one). Read in, a zone that is not an IANA name (`W. Europe Standard Time`) is followed by its VTIMEZONE. |
| `STATUS:CANCELLED` | Read in: a cancelled occurrence is left out of its series; a cancelled event is not added. |

## Print

On paper every hour, row and column is built and shown (a big view is built whole while it prints), nothing is scrolled, the colours are kept and the bar is left out; a week of the month, a timeline row, a day of the agenda and an appointment are not split between pages.

## Styling

| Hook | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `scheduler.scheduler `print`, appointment `print`` | Unit states: the look on paper, where a language draws it otherwise (no card frame). |
| `[data-printing]` | On the scheduler while it prints; `print()` also marks the page so only this scheduler prints. |

## API reference

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exportICalendar(options?)` | `string \| null` | `{ range: 'visible' (default) \| 'all' \| { start, end }, appointments, name }`: the file's text; `null` when `onICalendarExporting` said no. |
| `importICalendar(text)` | `Promise<ICalendarImportResult \| null>` | `{ added, updated, failed }`: each event added through the data layer (with `onAppointmentAdding` first); an event whose UID is an appointment’s key changes it. |
| `print()` | `Promise<boolean>` | Prints the scheduler alone; `false` when `onPrinting` said no. |

### Events

| Event | Arguments | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onICalendarExporting` | `{ appointments, range, cancel }` | Before writing; change `appointments` to write others. |
| `onICalendarExported` | `{ text, appointments }` | After writing. |
| `onICalendarImporting` | `{ text, appointments, cancel }` | Before adding: `appointments` are the values read, to change or filter. |
| `onICalendarImported` | `{ added, updated, failed }` | After adding. |
| `onPrinting` | `{ cancel }` | Before the print dialog. |
| `onPrinted` | `{}` | The print dialog closed (also after the browser’s own print). |

### The iCalendar part

The reader and the writer are DOM-free parts of the kit, usable without a scheduler.

| Function | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parseICalendar(text)` | `ICalendar` | The events, the time zones and the calendar’s name of a file; folded lines, escaped text, several calendars, components inside events; never throws. |
| `writeICalendar(options)` | `string` | `{ events, name, prodId, method, timeZones, stamp }`. |
| `timeZoneLines(zone, fromYear, toYear)` | `string[]` | The VTIMEZONE of an IANA zone, from `Intl`. |
| `icalendarMoment(date, zones, fallback)` | `number` | The moment a date of a file names: UTC, an IANA zone, the file’s VTIMEZONE, else `fallback`. |

## Example files

`ExportCalendar.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack, TextArea } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { recurringAppointments, type Booking } from './recurring-appointments';

/**
 * The appointments as an iCalendar file (RFC 5545): the days shown or all of them. A series goes
 * whole with its rule, the times left out of it and the one moved apart (`RECURRENCE-ID`); every zone
 * used comes with its `VTIMEZONE`. Open the file in any calendar application.
 */
export default function ExportCalendar() {
  const s = reactive({ text: '', url: '' });
  const scheduler = (<Scheduler<Booking> appointments={recurringAppointments()} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} label="Team calendar" />) as Scheduler<Booking>;
  const write = (range: 'visible' | 'all') => {
    s.text = scheduler.exportICalendar({ range }) ?? '';
    if (s.url) URL.revokeObjectURL(s.url);
    s.url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([s.text], { type: 'text/calendar' }));
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Export the days shown" variant="outline" onclick={() => write('visible')} />
        <Button text="Export all" variant="outline" onclick={() => write('all')} />
        <a href={() => s.url || null} download="team-calendar.ics" x-display={() => !!s.url}>
          Download team-calendar.ics
        </a>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
      <TextArea label="The file" rows={10} readOnly spellcheck={false} wrap="off" x-model={() => s.text} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`recurring-appointments.ts`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { formatRuleDate } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export interface Booking {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  recurrenceRule?: string;
  recurrenceException?: string;
  recurrenceId?: number;
  startDateTimeZone?: string;
  endDateTimeZone?: string;
}

/** Series around this week: a daily standup with one day left out and one moved, a review every other week, a report on the last Friday, an all-day Friday. */
export function recurringAppointments(): Booking[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  const day = (offset: number, hour = 0, minute = 0) => new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
    {
      id: 1,
      text: 'Team standup',
      startDate: day(-21, 9),
      endDate: day(-21, 9, 30),
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR',
      // This Tuesday is left out; this Wednesday's is moved (appointment 2).
      recurrenceException: [day(1, 9), day(2, 9)].map((d) => formatRuleDate({ time: d.getTime(), utc: true, dateOnly: false })).join(','),
    },
    { id: 2, text: 'Team standup', startDate: day(2, 11), endDate: day(2, 11, 30), recurrenceId: 1 },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Design review',
      startDate: day(-11, 14),
      endDate: day(-11, 15, 30),
      color: '#7c4dff',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH',
    },
    {
      id: 4,
      text: 'Monthly report',
      startDate: day(-60, 16),
      endDate: day(-60, 17),
      color: '#c62828',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR',
    },
    {
      id: 5,
      text: 'Remote day',
      startDate: day(-3),
      endDate: day(-2),
      allDay: true,
      color: '#00838f',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR;COUNT=12',
    },
    { id: 6, text: 'Lunch with Ana', startDate: day(3, 12, 30), endDate: day(3, 13, 30), color: '#2e7d32' },
  ]) as Booking[];
}
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
```

# DataGrid

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

A grid for data entry and large data: rows in memory or from any adapter of the data layer, a virtual list or pages, sorting, column layout, editing with the kit's editors, new rows with the Tab chain, three save modes, row actions, selection, filters, a search panel, grouping, summaries, a toolbar, lookup columns from other services, copy and paste, export and a layout that is kept — and every feature can be turned off, for the grid or for one column.

## Import

```tsx
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
```

## From JSX and from code

Give rows in memory with `rows` and their key with `rowKey`; the grid puts them in a `DataSource` over an `ArrayAdapter` itself. Every prop takes a value or a function. Created with `new`, the grid is an object like any other: add it, sort it, ask it.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Server data, virtual

With a `DataSource` that loads by `blocks`, the scroll bar is sized from the total and only the rows where the list looks are asked for. A jump (Ctrl+End, dragging the bar) asks only where it lands; a block left behind while loading is aborted. A row that has not come yet shows as a placeholder. Above 10 million pixels of rows the bar is scaled.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Pages

A `DataSource` that loads by `page` makes a paged grid: one page is asked for at a time, and a sort goes back to the first page. Rows in memory page with `mode` set to `paged`.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Pager

The pager under the rows shows the page sizes (`pageSizeSelector`, the sizes of `allowedPageSizes`, `all` for one page with every row), “Page 3 of 12 (250 items)” (`pagerInfo`, `pagerInfoText` with `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`), the first, previous, next and last buttons (`pagerNavigation`) and the pages around the current one (`pagerNeighbors`). `pagerDisplayMode` picks its look: `full` with page buttons and the sizes as buttons, `compact` with a box for the page number and a drop-down of the sizes, `adaptive` (the default) full while it fits in the grid's width. The rows per page change from code with `pageSize(n)` too; either way `onPageSizeChanging` can keep the old size, the grid goes back to the first page, and with `layoutKey` the size is kept with the layout. PageUp and PageDown turn the page (`pageKeys`).

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Example files

`FromCode.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

/** Rows in memory given with `rows`, rows added from code, and a grid created with `new`. */
export default function FromCode() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(40) });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  let host: Stack | null = null;

  // The grid reads the array as it is: after a push it loads it again.
  const pushOrder = () => {
    s.orders.push({ ...makeOrders(1)[0], id: s.orders.length + 1, customer: 'Pushed' });
    grid?.refresh();
  };

  const addGrid = () => {
    if (!host) return;
    host.controls.clear();
    const made = new DataGrid<Order>({ rows: makeOrders(8), rowKey: 'id', columns: columns.slice(0, 4), settings: { striped: true }, label: 'Created with new' });
    made.element.style.blockSize = '24rem';
    host.controls.add(made);
    made.sort = [{ field: 'customer', dir: 'asc' }];
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-local"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, striped: true }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Add a row from code" variant="outline" onclick={() => void grid?.addRow({ customer: 'Ada Lovelace' })} />
        <Button text="Push an order into the array" variant="outline" onclick={pushOrder} />
        <Button text="Add a grid from code" variant="outline" onclick={addGrid} />
        <output class="dg-local-count">{() => `${s.orders.length} orders in the array`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" ref={(c: Stack) => (host = c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`Virtual.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders from a server, loaded by blocks only where the list looks. */
export default function Virtual() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0 });
  // Stands in for a server: new data.ODataAdapter({ url: '/odata/Orders', key: 'OrderID' }) goes in its place.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid class="dg-virtual" style="block-size: 32rem" dataSource={orders} columns={columns} label="100,000 orders" locale="en" ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Go to the end" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(grid.total - 1, 'end')} />
        <Button text="Back to the top" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(0)} />
        <Button text="Fit the columns" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.autoSizeColumns()} />
        <output class="dg-loads">{() => `${s.loads} loads for ${grid?.total ?? 0} rows`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { makeOrders } from './orders';

/** How many times the server below was asked for rows. */
export const pagedLoads = reactive({ count: 0 });

const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 250);
server.onLoading(() => pagedLoads.count++);

/** 100,000 orders on a server, loaded a page at a time; the paged grid shows them, the export reads them. */
```

`Pager.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The page sizes, the info text and the full, compact and adaptive looks of the pager. */
export default function Pager() {
  const s = reactive({ look: 'adaptive' as 'adaptive' | 'compact' | 'full', told: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Full" variant={() => (s.look === 'full' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'full')} />
        <Button text="Compact" variant={() => (s.look === 'compact' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'compact')} />
        <Button text="Adaptive" variant={() => (s.look === 'adaptive' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'adaptive')} />
        <Button text="50 rows a page" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.pageSize(50)} />
        <output class="dg-pager-state">{() => s.told}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-pager"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(1000)}
        rowKey="id"
        mode="paged"
        pageSize={20}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders in pages of a size you choose"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          pageSizeSelector: true,
          allowedPageSizes: [10, 20, 50, 'all'],
          pagerDisplayMode: () => s.look,
        }}
        onPageSizeChanged={(e) => (s.told = `${e.pageSize || 'All'} rows a page (was ${e.previous || 'all'})`)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Editing

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Editing and save modes

Typing on a cell, Enter, F2 or a double-click opens its editor; only the active cell has one. What is typed goes into the row's draft in the grid's `ChangeTracker`, kept by key, and the row is saved when it is left: `wait` sends it and waits, `background` sends it through one queue and goes on, `batch` keeps everything until “Save changes”. A row with a message cannot be left; Escape gives up. This service turns down a note with “error” in it.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Saving all at once

With `saveMode: 'batch'` every edit, new row and deletion waits for `saveChanges()`; then the deletions, the updates and the new rows go out, each kind in one call, and rows the server turns down keep their marks. Here over a server that loads by page: the changes stay while the pages turn, and the page's own buttons follow `hasChanges`.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## New rows

`addRow()` or the toolbar's “New row” opens a row at the bottom (the grid goes to the very end; in a virtual list only the last block is loaded) or at the top, with its first cell a new row can fill in edit mode. Tab on the last cell of a new row saves it and opens the next one; Escape drops it; one left untouched goes by itself.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Row actions

`actions` gives each row its buttons, as a list or as a function of the row and its state (`isNew`, `isEditing`, `isDirty`, `isSaving`, `hasError`, `isRemoved`, `isSelected`); when what the function reads changes, the row's buttons change. The grid's ready actions are named by strings. The buttons that do not fit the column go into the “more” menu, the first ones in the list stay. The column sits at the start or the end, pinned to its edge or scrolling with the rows.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

The actions can show in the toolbar (`actionsLocation: 'toolbar'`, the `rowActions` item) or in the bottom bar (`'bottom'`) instead, for the rows they act on: the selected rows, or the active row without selection (`actionsTarget`). With no row nothing shows; with one row its own actions, as the row would show them; with several only the ones every row has, each with the count of rows it runs on (“Approve (3)”), dimmed while it is disabled for one of them (`actionsMultipleEnabled: 'any'` lets it run on the rows where it is enabled). An action’s `location` wins, so “Approve” can sit in the toolbar while “Edit” stays in the row; the column shows only while an action sits there. `onclickMany` runs once with every row; without it `onclick` runs row by row, a promise waited for, with progress and a Stop button over the rows, and the outcome is announced (“2 of 3 done, 1 failed”). The ready `remove` marks all the rows in batch mode and in the other modes sends them in one save (`ChangeTracker.removeRows`: one request when the adapter saves in batches, OData `$batch`, a REST batch endpoint or a SOAP `save`). An action’s `tone` colours its button and its menu items (`'danger'` for the ready `remove`, `'accent'` for `save`).

Every row's actions are also in its context menu (right click, Shift+F10), wherever they show: inside a selection of several rows the common ones for all of them. With `actionsDisplay: 'menu'` a row shows only its “more” button, with every action in its menu, and the bars one “Actions” menu button; an action's `menu` keeps it in the menu always, or a button always.

After “select all” over a server the rows are not loaded: only actions with `onclickSelection` show then, and they get the selection as `grid.selection` has it (`all`, `keys`, `except`, `filter`) to send to the server, so nothing has to load every row.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actionsLocation` | `'row'` | Where the actions show: `'row'`, `'toolbar'` (the `rowActions` toolbar item, at the start; place it through `toolbar.items` like the other items) or `'bottom'` (the start of the bottom bar). |
| `actionsTarget` | `'auto'` | The rows the bars act on: `'selection'`, `'focused'` (the active row) or `'auto'` (the selected rows while selection is on, else the active row). |
| `actionsDisplay` | `'auto'` | `'auto'`: the buttons that fit, the rest in “more”. `'menu'`: only the “more” button per row (the column is as wide as that button; with an action that is a button always, `actionsWidth`), one “Actions” menu button in the bars. The context menu always lists them all. |
| `actionsMultipleEnabled` | `'all'` | On several rows an action can be used while it is enabled for all of them, or for any (`'any'`: it runs on those). |
| `actionsShowCount` | `true` | The count of rows after the text of an action that acts on several (“Approve (3)”). |
| `actionsStopOnError` | `false` | Row by row, a failed row stops the rest. |
| `actionsProgress, actionsStopButton` | `true`, `true` | The panel over the rows while an action works on several rows (once one of them returned a promise), and its Stop button. |
| `actionsContextMenu` | `true` | A row’s actions in its context menu. |

| Action field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `id, text, icon, showText, hint` | As in the row. Rows share an action by its `id`. |
| `tone` | `'standard' \| 'accent' \| 'danger'`, default `'standard'`: the colour of its button and of its item in the “more” menu, the context menu and the bars’ “Actions” menu. |
| `visible, disabled` | `boolean` or `(row, state) => boolean`, asked for each row; several rows: visible for every row, disabled as `actionsMultipleEnabled` says. |
| `location` | `Bind<'row' \| 'toolbar' \| 'bottom'>`; wins over `actionsLocation`. |
| `menu` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'always' \| 'never'>`, default `'auto'`: in the “more” menu when it does not fit, always, or never (a button even in the `'menu'` display). |
| `multiple` | `Bind<boolean>`, default `true` (the ready `edit`: `false`): it can run on several rows. |
| `multipleEnabled, stopOnError, showCount, contextMenu` | The action’s own `actionsMultipleEnabled`, `actionsStopOnError`, `actionsShowCount`, `actionsContextMenu`; each wins. |
| `beginGroup` | A line before it in a menu. |
| `onclick(row, state)` | Runs for one row; on several rows (without `onclickMany`) for each in turn. A promise is waited for; a throw, a rejection or a promise of `false` counts the row as failed. |
| `onclickMany(rows, e)` | Runs once for several rows (one row too without `onclick`). `e`: `{ location, signal, progress(done, total?) }`; `signal` is aborted by Stop. |
| `onclickSelection(selection, e)` | Runs for a selection whose rows are not loaded (“select all” over a server), with the selection state; only such actions show then. |

| Member | Gets / returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onActionRunning` | `{ action, rows, selection, location, cancel }` | An action is about to run (in a row, a bar, a row’s menu or from code); `cancel` keeps it from running. `rows` is empty for a selection that is not loaded. |
| `onActionRan` | `{ action, rows, location, done, failed, canceled, errors }` | An action ran. Without a listener, what failed rows threw goes to the console. |
| `runAction(id, rows?)` | `Promise<GridActionRanEventArgs \| null>` | Runs an action on `rows`, or on the rows the bars act on now, where it is visible and enabled; `null` when it is not there or was cancelled. |
| `actionTargets` | `T[]`, reactive | The rows the bars act on now; empty for a selection that is not loaded. |
| `barActions` | `GridBarAction[]`, reactive | The actions the toolbar and the bottom bar show now: `{ action, location, text, count, disabled, rows }`. |
| `stopAction()` | `void` | Stops the action working on several rows, as its Stop button does. |

## Example files

`SaveModes.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: data.SaveMode[] = ['wait', 'background', 'batch'];

/** Edits saved as the save mode says, to a server that turns down a note with "error" in it. */
export default function SaveModes() {
  const s = reactive({ saveMode: 'wait' as data.SaveMode });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(30), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 300);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'all' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Save mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.saveMode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.saveMode === mode} onclick={() => (s.saveMode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-editing"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to edit"
        locale="en"
        saveMode={() => s.saveMode}
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, striped: true }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        validateRow={(row: Order) => (row.status === 'Cancelled' && row.paid ? { paid: 'A cancelled order is not paid.' } : null)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Delete the active row" variant="outline" onclick={() => void grid?.deleteRow()} />
        <Button text="Undo the deletion" variant="ghost" visible={() => s.saveMode === 'batch'} onclick={() => grid?.activeRow && grid.restoreRow(grid.activeRow)} />
        <output class="dg-changes">{() => `${grid?.changes.count ?? 0} unsaved, ${grid?.errorCount ?? 0} with errors`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`order-service.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';

/** Orders in memory that answer like a server, and turn down a note with "error" in it. */
export class OrderService extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  protected override updateRow(key: number, changes: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(changes, () => super.updateRow(key, changes));
  }

  protected override insertRow(values: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(values, () => super.insertRow(values));
  }

  private later(values: Partial<Order>, save: () => Promise<Partial<Order>>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    const message = 'The server does not take this note.';
    return new Promise((done, fail) =>
      setTimeout(() => {
        if (String(values.note ?? '').includes('error')) fail(data.DataError.create('MJD202', { operation: 'save', fields: { note: message } }, message));
        else save().then(done, fail);
      }, 300),
    );
  }
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

`BatchSave.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

/** Every change kept until "Save changes", over a server that loads by page; the page's own buttons. */
export default function BatchSave() {
  const s = reactive({ note: '' });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(200), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 250);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'page', pageSize: 15 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const save = async () => {
    const result = await grid?.saveChanges();
    if (result) s.note = `${result.saved} saved, ${result.failed} failed`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-batch"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders saved together"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, saveButtons: false, actionsWidth: 100 }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : ['remove'])}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Save changes" tone="accent" enabled={() => !!grid?.hasChanges} onclick={save} />
        <Button text="Discard" variant="outline" enabled={() => !!grid?.hasChanges} onclick={() => grid?.discardChanges()} />
        <output class="dg-batch-note">{() => `${grid?.changes.count ?? 0} unsaved${s.note ? ` · ${s.note}` : ''}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`RowActions.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const PLACES = ['start', 'end'] as const;
const WIDTHS = [100, 140, 260];

/** Buttons per row from a function of the row and its state; the rest go into "more". */
export default function RowActions() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(30), at: 'end' as 'start' | 'end', sticky: true, width: 260, note: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const approve: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'approve',
    text: 'Approve',
    tone: 'accent',
    visible: (row) => row.status === 'Draft',
    onclick: (row) => {
      row.status = 'Approved';
      // The grid reads the row as it is: draw it again, its buttons with it.
      grid?.repaintRows([row.id]);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} approved`;
    },
  };
  const print: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'print', text: 'Print', onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Order ${row.id} sent to the printer`) };
  const mail: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'mail', text: 'Mail the customer', disabled: (row) => !row.paid, onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Mail to ${row.customer}`) };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Actions column">
        {PLACES.map((at) => (
          <Button key={at} text={at} size="sm" variant={() => (s.at === at ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.at === at} onclick={() => (s.at = at)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Pinned" x-model={() => s.sticky} />
        {WIDTHS.map((w) => (
          <Button key={`w${w}`} text={`${w}px`} size="sm" variant={() => (s.width === w ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.width === w} onclick={() => (s.width = w)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-actions"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders with actions"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : [approve, 'edit', 'remove', print, mail])}
        settings={{ editable: true, actionsPosition: () => s.at, actionsSticky: () => s.sticky, actionsWidth: () => s.width }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-action-note">{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`BarActions.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction, type GridActionLocation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const LOCATIONS: GridActionLocation[] = ['row', 'toolbar', 'bottom'];

const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

/** The actions of the selected rows in the toolbar or the bottom bar; several rows share the ones they all have. */
export default function BarActions() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(40), location: 'toolbar' as GridActionLocation, menu: false, note: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  // The grid reads the rows as they are: after a change in place it draws them again and asks their actions again.
  const changed = (rows: readonly Order[]) => {
    grid?.repaintRows(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    grid?.refreshActions();
  };

  const approve: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'approve',
    text: 'Approve',
    tone: 'accent',
    visible: (row) => row.status === 'Draft',
    // Once for every selected row: one request to the server.
    onclickMany: async (rows) => {
      await wait(300);
      for (const row of rows) row.status = 'Approved';
      changed(rows);
      s.note = `${rows.length} orders approved`;
    },
    onclick: (row) => {
      row.status = 'Approved';
      changed([row]);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} approved`;
    },
  };
  // Row by row: the grid shows the progress and a Stop button.
  const print: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'print',
    text: 'Print',
    onclick: async (row) => {
      await wait(400);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} printed`;
    },
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Where the actions show">
        {LOCATIONS.map((at) => (
          <Button key={at} text={at} size="sm" variant={() => (s.location === at ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.location === at} onclick={() => (s.location = at)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Menu only" x-model={() => s.menu} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-bar-actions"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to approve"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : [approve, print, 'remove'])}
        settings={{ selection: 'multiple', actionsLocation: () => s.location, actionsDisplay: () => (s.menu ? 'menu' : 'auto') }}
        onActionRan={(e) => {
          if (e.canceled) s.note = `${e.action.id}: stopped after ${e.done} rows`;
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-bar-note">{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```
