# DataGrid: Edit forms and popups

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Edit forms and popups

`settings.editMode` decides how a row is edited and when it is handed to saving; `saveMode` decides how a row handed over is sent — waiting for the answer, in the background, or kept for `saveChanges()`. In `form` mode the row opens as a form in its place, the kit's `FormLayout` with a field per column: each the editor its cell would get, framed and labelled, the messages of the checks under it. The rows after it move down by its height, also in the virtual list. Save (or Enter in a field) saves the row as the save mode says, Cancel or Escape gives it up; focus moves into the form and back to the row. Here the form has two groups; the buttons switch the edit mode.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| editMode | Edited | Handed to saving | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | In the cells, one editor at a time | Leaving the row | The grid's default. With `saveMode: 'batch'` it is the same as `batch`. |
| `cell` | In the cells | Leaving each cell (Enter, Tab, an arrow, a click elsewhere); a new row on leaving the row | A message keeps the cell until it is fixed or Escape. |
| `batch` | In the cells | `saveChanges()` (“Save changes”) | Sets the save mode to `'batch'`, whatever `saveMode` says. |
| `form` | In a form that takes the row’s place, as wide as the grid | Save (or Enter); Cancel and Escape give up | Typing on a cell does not open it: Enter, F2, the start-edit click, the `edit` action, `editRow()` and `addRow()` do. |
| `popup` | In the same form in a modal window | Save (or Enter); Cancel, Escape and the close button give up | Focus stays in the window and comes back to the row. |

In `popup` mode the same form opens in the kit's `MxForm` as a modal window: for an existing row and for a new one (`addRow()`, “New row”). Focus stays in the window; Enter presses Save and Escape Cancel; when it closes, focus is back on the row. `popup` sets its title and size, `form` and the columns' `formItem` the fields.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editMode` | `'row'` | How rows are edited and when a row is handed to saving (the table above). Changing it to or from `batch` starts again with the data, like `saveMode`. |
| `confirmDelete` | `true` | Deleting a row (`deleteRow()`, `deleteRows()`, the `remove` action) asks first, once for all the rows an action deletes; not in batch mode, where a deletion is only marked and can be taken back. Texts: `gridConfirmDelete`, `gridConfirmDeleteRows`, `gridConfirmDeleteTitle`. |
| `selectTextOnEditStart` | `true` | The text of a cell or a form field is selected when its editor opens; off, the caret goes to its end. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form.items` | `Bind<(string \| FormItem)[]>` | every column | What the form holds, in order: a column by field name, or a kit `FormItem`. An item whose `field` is a column’s gets that column’s editor (by type, a lookup’s, the column’s own `editor`), with the item’s `label`, `colSpan`, `helpText`, `visible` and `editorProps`; groups (`group`, `items`, `columns`), buttons and `template`s are the form’s own. By default every column, the visible ones first, hidden ones too; a column the user cannot fill shows read-only. |
| `form.colCount` | `Bind<number>` | `2` | Columns of the form. |
| `form.minColWidth` | `Bind<string>` | — | As many columns as fit, each at least this wide; `colCount` is the most. |
| `form.labelMode` | `Bind<'top' \| 'side' \| 'floating' \| 'hidden'>` | `'top'` | Where the labels go. |
| `popup.title, popup.showTitle` | `Bind<string>`, `Bind<boolean>` | “Edit row” / “New row”, `true` | The window’s title; hidden, it still names the window for screen readers. |
| `popup.width, popup.height` | `Bind<number \| string>` | as the form needs | A CSS length, or pixels. |
| `popup.resizable, popup.movable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Resized from its edges, moved by its title bar. |
| `popup.showCloseButton, popup.showMaximize, popup.fullScreen` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true`, `false`, `false` | The close button (it cancels), the maximize button, opening maximized. |

| Column field | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formItem.visible` | `Bind<boolean>` | The column in the form or not. |
| `formItem.colSpan` | `number \| 'all'` | Form columns it spans. |
| `formItem.label, formItem.helpText` | `Bind<string>` | The label (default: the title) and a line under the editor. |
| `formItem.editorOptions` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Props of its editor in the form only, over the column’s. |
| `formItem.order` | `number` | Its place in the form; lower first. |
| `validationRules` | `GridValidationRule[]` | The rules below, checked after `required` and `validate`. |

## Validation rules

A column's `validationRules` are the standard rule set, checked with the kit's own validation rules as a value is written and again before its row is saved; `required` and `validate` keep working before them. The rules run in order and the `async` ones last, together: the row waits for their answer, its cell busy meanwhile. A value is not checked twice: only `reevaluate` (on for `async`) and `compare` run on every check of the row. `onRowValidating` comes after the cells, for the row as a whole. The messages show in the cells, in the form and in the window. Here the server turns down a customer with “test” in the name.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Rule type | Options | Passes when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | `trim` (default `true`) | An empty value (spaces only, with `trim`) fails. |
| `numeric` | `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | A number, or a text that is one. |
| `range` | `min`, `max` (`Bind<number \| Date>`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`), `reevaluate` | Between the bounds; numbers or dates. |
| `stringLength` | `min`, `max`, `trim` (`true`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`) | The length of the text. |
| `pattern` | `pattern` (`Bind<RegExp \| string>`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | Matches; a string is found anywhere in the value, as `new RegExp(pattern)` does. |
| `email` | `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | An e-mail address. |
| `compare` | `comparisonTarget(row, context)` (`context.getValue('password')`: the entered value, else the row's), `comparisonType` (`'=='`, `'!='`, `'==='`, `'!=='`, `'<'`, `'<='`, `'>'`, `'>='`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`) | The value against what the function returns (another field of the row); checked on every check of the row. |
| `custom` | `validationCallback({ value, row, context, column, rule })` (`row` is the row itself, `context` the values entered: `values`, `getValue(field)`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`), `reevaluate` (`false`) | `true` passes, `false` fails with `message`, a string fails with that text. |
| `async` | `validationCallback(…)` returning a promise, `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`), `reevaluate` (`true`) | The answer: `true`, `false`, a message or `{ isValid, message }`; a rejection fails with its message. The row waits for it before it is sent; its cell shows that it is busy. |

Every rule takes a `message` (`Bind<string>`); without it the text comes from `uiLocale` (or the grid's `texts`): `required`, `gridInvalidNumber`, `tooShort` / `tooLong`, `outOfRange` / `tooSmall` / `tooLarge`, `invalidFormat`, `invalidEmail`, `noMatch`, `invalid`.

## Events and methods

| Event | Gets | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onEditingStart` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, rowIndex, isNew, cancel }` | A cell editor, or the form of a row (`field` `''`), is about to open; `cancel` keeps the row as it is. `row` is the row itself (a class instance stays one); `values` holds what was entered and not saved yet, `getValue(field)` the entered value else the row’s. |
| `onEditorPreparing` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, isNew, options, cancel }` | Before an editor of a cell or of a form field is made: change its props; `cancel` leaves a field out of the form. |
| `onEditorPrepared` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, isNew, editor, element, place: 'cell' \| 'form' }` | An editor was made. |
| `onRowValidating` | `{ key, row, values, getValue, isNew, changed, errors, isValid, errorText, cancel }` | A row is checked before it is saved, after its cells (and their async rules): add or take out messages in `errors` (by field, `''` the row), or `isValid = false` with `errorText`. Once per check of the row. |
| `onInitNewRow, onSaving, onRowInserting, onRowUpdating, onEditCanceling …` | see [Events](datagrid-layout.md#events) | The same in every edit mode: Save in a form is a save, Cancel a cancel. |

| Member | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editRow(i) / editRowByKey(key)` | `boolean` | Opens the first editor of a row, or its form (`form`, `popup`); by key while the row is loaded. |
| `addRow(values?)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Opens a new row: in its cells, in place as a form, or in the window. |
| `saveEditData()` | `Promise<boolean>` | Saves what is being edited, as Save does: the form, else the row being edited; in batch mode every unsaved change. |
| `cancelEditData()` | `void` | Gives up what is being edited, as Cancel does; in batch mode every unsaved change. |
| `closeEditCell()` | `boolean` | Keeps the open editor’s value and closes it; in a form, keeps every field’s value. |
| `form, popup` | read/write, live | `grid.form.colCount = 3`, `grid.popup.width = '40rem'`; a function is followed; `onOptionChanged` tells `form.colCount`, `popup.width` …. |

## Example files

`FormMode.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn, type GridSettings } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: GridSettings['editMode'][] = ['row', 'cell', 'batch', 'form', 'popup'];

/** The note gets the whole width of the form and a line of help. */
const formColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'note' ? { ...c, formItem: { colSpan: 'all', helpText: 'Shown to the courier.' } } : c));

/** One grid in every edit mode; in 'form' the row opens as a form with two groups. */
export default function FormMode() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'form' as GridSettings['editMode'] });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(40), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 300);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'all' });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Edit mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-form"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={formColumns}
        label="Orders in an edit form"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, editMode: () => s.mode }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        actions={['edit', 'remove']}
        form={{
          colCount: 2,
          items: [
            { group: 'Order', items: [{ field: 'customer' }, { field: 'date' }, { field: 'status' }, { field: 'amount' }] },
            { group: 'Delivery', items: [{ field: 'city' }, { field: 'paid' }, { field: 'note' }] },
          ],
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

`order-service.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';

/** Orders in memory that answer like a server, and turn down a note with "error" in it. */
export class OrderService extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  protected override updateRow(key: number, changes: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(changes, () => super.updateRow(key, changes));
  }

  protected override insertRow(values: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(values, () => super.insertRow(values));
  }

  private later(values: Partial<Order>, save: () => Promise<Partial<Order>>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    const message = 'The server does not take this note.';
    return new Promise((done, fail) =>
      setTimeout(() => {
        if (String(values.note ?? '').includes('error')) fail(data.DataError.create('MJD202', { operation: 'save', fields: { note: message } }, message));
        else save().then(done, fail);
      }, 300),
    );
  }
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

```tsx
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

/** In the window the note takes a line of its own and the number stays out. */
```

`ValidationRules.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn, type GridSettings } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: GridSettings['editMode'][] = ['row', 'form', 'popup'];

/** A pretend server: half a second to answer whether a customer may order. */
function customerAllowed(name: string): Promise<{ isValid: boolean; message?: string }> {
  return new Promise((done) => setTimeout(() => done(/test/i.test(name) ? { isValid: false, message: 'The server does not take test customers.' } : { isValid: true }), 500));
}

/** the standard rule set on the columns, checked as values are written and before a row is saved. */
const ruleColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => {
  if (c.field === 'customer') {
    return {
      ...c,
      required: false,
      validationRules: [
        { type: 'required' },
        { type: 'stringLength', min: 3, max: 40 },
        { type: 'async', validationCallback: ({ value }) => customerAllowed(String(value)) },
      ],
    };
  }
  if (c.field === 'amount') return { ...c, validate: undefined, validationRules: [{ type: 'range', min: 1, max: 5000, message: 'An order is between 1 and 5,000.' }] };
  if (c.field === 'note') return { ...c, validationRules: [{ type: 'stringLength', max: 60 }, { type: 'pattern', pattern: /^[^<>]*$/, message: 'No angle brackets.' }] };
  return c;
});

/** Rules on the cells, a check of the whole row, and the messages in the cells, the form or the window. */
export default function ValidationRules() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'row' as GridSettings['editMode'] });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Edit mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-rules"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(20)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={ruleColumns}
        label="Orders with rules"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, editMode: () => s.mode }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        onRowValidating={(e) => {
          if (e.row.status === 'Cancelled' && e.row.paid) e.errors.paid = 'A cancelled order is not paid.';
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Filtering and search

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Filters

The filter row has a cell per column: a condition chosen in the cell, by the column type (contains, starts with, =, <, between, empty…), and the kit's field for the value; typing applies after a short pause. The header filter lists the column's values with their counts, honoring the other filters: rows in memory are counted by the grid, an adapter that groups is asked with `group`, any other server answers `loadValues`. Both feed the data source's filter (`data.where`, `data.and`, `data.or`), together with AND.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Filter panel and builder

`settings.filterPanel` puts a panel under the rows that reads the filter value as text — `[City] Equals 'Ankara' And [Amount] Is greater than '900.00'`, in the columns' titles, formats and lookup texts. Pressing it opens the kit's [FilterBuilder](filterbuilder.md) in a modal window on every column (`filterBuilder` per column turns one off), with “is any of” and “is none of” for each; OK makes its value the filter value, Cancel and Escape leave it. The check box turns the filter value off and on, Clear takes it away.

With `filterSyncEnabled` (on while the panel shows) the filter row and the header filters are part of the filter value: a condition the builder sets shows in the column's cell or its value list when they can show it (one each), and what they set reads in the panel and opens in the builder. Conditions they cannot show — an OR group, a second condition on a column — stay in the filter value only. The filter goes to the data source as any other: here 100,000 orders on a server, or 200 in memory. The layout kept with `layoutKey`, and `state()`, keep the filter value and the check box.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.filterPanel` | The panel under the rows: the check box, the filter as text (pressing it opens the builder), “Create Filter” while there is none, and “Clear”. `boolean`, default `false`. |
| `settings.filterSyncEnabled` | The filter row and the header filters are part of the filter value, both ways. `'auto'`: while the panel shows. `boolean \| 'auto'`, default `'auto'`. |
| `settings.filterBuilder, column `filterBuilder`` | The column is a field of the builder. `boolean`, default `true`. |
| `filterValue` | The filter value; a function is followed, the user's changes come in `onFilterChanged` (`e.filterValue`). Also a property. `Bind<data.FilterExpression \| null>`, default `null`. |
| `filterEnabled` | Whether the filter value applies: the panel's check box. Also a property. `Bind<boolean>`, default `true`. |
| `filterPanelText` | The panel's text, from the one it would show. `({ text, filterValue }) => string`. |
| `filterBuilder` | Any prop of `FilterBuilder` but `value` and `fields` (`customOperations`, `maxGroupLevel`, `groupOperations`, its events…); live as `grid.filterBuilder`. `GridFilterBuilderOptions`, default `{}`. |
| `filterBuilderPopup` | The window: `title`, `showTitle`, `width` (`'40rem'`), `height`, `resizable`, `movable`, `showCloseButton`, `showMaximize`, `fullScreen`; live as `grid.filterBuilderPopup`. `GridFilterBuilderPopup`, default `{}`. |
| `openFilterBuilder(), closeFilterBuilder(apply?), clearFilterValue()` | What the panel does, from code. `filterText` is the panel's text, `filterBuilderInstance` the open builder. |
| `onFilterBuilderOpening / Opened, onFilterBuilderClosing / Closed` | `e.cancel` keeps the builder closed, or open; `e.apply` / `e.applied` say whether OK was pressed. `onFilterChanging` (cancelable) and `onFilterChanged` carry `filterValue` and `filterEnabled` too. |

## Ranges, dates and entries

A column's `headerFilterInterval` groups its header filter: a number column in ranges of that size (“0 – 250”, “250 – 500”; several sizes, `[1000, 100]`, make a tree), a date column in a tree of years, months and days — down to the part it names (`'year'`, `'quarter'`, `'month'`, `'day'`, `'hour'`, `'minute'`, `'second'`; `null` lists the dates one by one). Dates are a tree by default, down to the day (`headerFilterDateInterval`). The tree is the kit's `TreeView` with check boxes and “Select all”; a month checked keeps the month (`'2026/3'`), a year `2026`, and filters with `>=` its first moment and `<` the next one's, so a server runs it too. The counts are worked out in the browser from the column's distinct values: counted in memory, grouped by an adapter that groups, or from `loadValues`.

`headerFilterItems` gives the header filter entries of its own, `{ text, value }`, where a value is a value or a filter expression (`data.where('city', 'in', […])`); a function gets the other filters and `values()`, the entries it would list, to add to. `filterValues` and `filterType` (both may be functions that are followed) set what the header filter holds: `'exclude'` leaves those values out, so values that come later show. In the list, choosing every value and then taking some away leaves those out the same way.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Search panel

`searchPanel` puts a search box in the toolbar: its text is looked for in every searchable column at once, after a short typing pause. Each column reads it by its type — text columns contain it (without case, in the locale), number, date and yes/no columns match it when it reads as one of their values, list columns by their option texts — and the columns are joined with OR, then with the filter row and the header filter with AND. A text no column can read leaves no row. The filter goes to the data source like any other (`data.where`, `data.or`), so a server runs it; what was found is marked in the cells. `searchText` binds the text both ways with `onSearchTextChanged`; `searchByText()` searches from code.

A lookup column is searched by its texts: the lookup source — here a customers service apart from the sales' server — is asked for the items whose text holds the search (at most `searchLimit`), and their keys go to the rows' server as `customerId in [...]`. A column with a `textFrom` field searches that field of the row instead.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Example files

`Filters.tsx`

```tsx
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The filter row and the header filter, on rows in memory. */
export default function Filters() {
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const setFilters = () => {
    if (grid) grid.filters = { city: { values: ['Ankara', 'İzmir'] }, amount: { op: 'between', value: 100, value2: 500 } };
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-filters"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders to filter"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ striped: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Ankara and İzmir, 100 to 500" variant="outline" onclick={setFilters} />
        <Button text="Clear the filters" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearFilters()} />
        <output class="dg-filter-count">{() => `${grid?.total ?? 0} of 200 orders`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, RadioGroup, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The filter panel and its builder, on 100,000 orders of a server or 200 in memory, the filter row and header filters kept in step. */
export default function FilterPanel() {
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 200), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const rows = makeOrders(200);
  const s = reactive({ where: 'server', sync: true, filter: null as data.FilterExpression | null });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Rows"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'server', text: '100,000 on a server' },
            { value: 'memory', text: '200 in memory' },
          ]}
          x-model={() => s.where}
        />
        <Switch label="filterSyncEnabled" x-model={() => s.sync} />
        <Button text="Open the builder" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.openFilterBuilder()} />
        <Button
          text="Paid, over 900"
          variant="ghost"
          onclick={() => (s.filter = data.and(data.where('paid', '=', true), data.where('amount', '>', 900)))}
        />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-server-filters"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        dataSource={() => (s.where === 'server' ? orders : null)}
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders with a filter panel"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ filterPanel: true, filterSyncEnabled: () => s.sync }}
        filterValue={() => s.filter}
        filterBuilder={{ maxGroupLevel: 2 }}
        filterBuilderPopup={{ title: 'Filter the orders' }}
        onFilterChanged={(e) => (s.filter = e.filterValue)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-server-filter">{() => `${(grid?.total ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} orders · ${JSON.stringify(grid?.filter ?? null)}`}</output>
      <output class="dg-filter-value">{() => `filterValue: ${JSON.stringify(s.filter)}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

`HeaderFilterIntervals.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const COAST = ['Antalya', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Trabzon'];

/** The order columns with header filters: amounts in ranges, dates in a tree, cities by entries of their own, statuses left out. */
const intervalColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => {
  switch (c.field) {
    case 'amount':
      // "0 – 250", "250 – 500" …
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true, headerFilterInterval: 250 };
    case 'date':
      // Year → month → day, by the grid's headerFilterDateInterval.
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true };
    case 'city':
      return {
        ...c,
        headerFilter: true,
        headerFilterItems: [
          { text: 'On the coast', value: data.where('city', 'in', COAST) },
          { text: 'Inland', value: data.not(data.where('city', 'in', COAST)) },
          { text: 'Ankara only', value: 'Ankara' },
        ],
      };
    case 'status':
      // Every status but Cancelled: statuses that come later show too.
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true, filterValues: ['Cancelled'], filterType: 'exclude' };
    default:
      return c;
  }
});

/** The header filter in ranges of amounts, a tree of dates, entries of its own, and values left out. */
export default function HeaderFilterIntervals() {
  const s = reactive({ months: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text={() => (s.months ? 'Dates down to the day' : 'Dates down to the month')} variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.months = !s.months)} />
        <Button text="Amounts in ranges of 1,000" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('amount', 'headerFilterInterval', 1000)} />
        <Button text="Clear the filters" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearFilters()} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-intervals"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(300)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={intervalColumns}
        label="Orders filtered by ranges and dates"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ headerFilterDateInterval: () => (s.months ? 'month' : 'day') }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-intervals-filter">{() => `${grid?.total ?? 0} orders · ${JSON.stringify(grid?.filters ?? {})}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```


```tsx
/** A customer, as another made-up service keeps it. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` made-up customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {

    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
```

---

# DataGrid: Lookup columns

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Lookup columns

A column with `lookup` keeps a key (a customer id) and shows the text of its item, from a `DataSource` of any adapter — another service, another protocol than the rows — or from an array. Only the keys on the screen are asked for: the unknown ones of a moment go out together (`id in [...]`, at most `batchSize` each), or one by one with `resolve: 'byKey'` for a service that gives one item by key. The texts are kept per source and shared by every column and grid using it. While a key loads its cell is empty and busy; a key the source does not have shows as it is, muted, and stops its row from being saved.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

Editing opens a `DropDown` with search (or `editor: 'combobox'`, or the kit's `Lookup` with columns) over a data source of its own on the same adapter, so its search never moves a source the page shows. Typing on the cell opens the list and searches what was typed; the picked text shows at once. `filter(row, context)` narrows the list for the row (by `context.getValue`, so a province just picked counts), `setCellValue` writes other fields with the value — here a new province empties the district — and `onEditorPreparing` changes the editor's props: the district waits for a province (`e.getValue('province')`).

```tsx
/** Provinces and their districts, for the cascading lists. */
export interface Province {
  code: string;
  name: string;
}

export interface District {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  province: string;
}

export const PROVINCES: Province[] = [
  { code: 'AN', name: 'Ankara' },
  { code: 'IS', name: 'İstanbul' },
  { code: 'IZ', name: 'İzmir' },
];

export const DISTRICTS: District[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Çankaya', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Keçiören', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Yenimahalle', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 4, name: 'Kadıköy', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Beşiktaş', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 6, name: 'Üsküdar', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 7, name: 'Bornova', province: 'IZ' },
  { id: 8, name: 'Karşıyaka', province: 'IZ' },
  { id: 9, name: 'Konak', province: 'IZ' },
];
```

When the row already brings the text (OData `$expand`), `textFrom` reads it there and the lookup source is asked only to edit and to list; `sortField` sorts the server by it. Without them a lookup column sorts by its key; rows in memory can sort by the text with `sortBy: 'text'`. The filter row offers “(All)” and the texts (always `=`), the header filter the texts with “(empty)” first, both searched by text and, with `syncLookupFilterValues`, holding only the keys of the rows the other filters leave. Copy and export write the text (`raw`: the key); a pasted text becomes the key of the one item that has it.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Lookup field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `dataSource` | `Bind<DataSource \| unknown[]>`: the items, searched and resolved on their own service, or an array in memory. |
| `valueField, textField` | The field that matches the cell value (default: the source’s key; an array of plain values: the value); the text shown, a field or `(item) => text` (default: the value). |
| `searchFields` | Fields the editor and the text searches look in. Default: `textField` when it is a field. |
| `filter` | `(row, context) => FilterExpression`: narrows the items for a row (cascading lists: `context.getValue('province')`, the value entered, else the row’s); `null` row: the filter lists. |
| `allowClearing` | `Bind<boolean>`: a clear button in the editor. Default `false`. |
| `resolve, batchSize` | `'batch'` (default: keys in one request, `batchSize` 100 each) or `'byKey'` (one request per key). |
| `sortBy` | `Bind<'key' \| 'text'>`: rows in memory sorted by the key (default) or by the text shown. |
| `editor, editorOptions` | `'dropdown'` (default), `'combobox'` or `'lookup'`, and props for it (a `Lookup`’s `columns`). A column’s own `editor` still wins and gets the lookup in its context. |
| `searchLimit` | How many items whose text holds the search panel’s text the search turns into keys, at most. Default 100. |
| `filterSearchLimit` | The same for the header filter’s search box. Default 1000. |
| `pageSize` | Items the editor’s list loads per request while it scrolls (a data source). Default 50. |
| `parallelRequests` | `'byKey'`: requests at the same time. Default 6. |
| `pasteSearchLimit` | Items a pasted text is looked for in. Default 50. |

## Example files

`Lookups.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

type Sale = { id: number; customerId: number | null; amount: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** Sales in memory whose customer comes from another service: only the customers on the screen are asked for, several in one request. */
export default function Lookups() {
  const s = reactive({ requests: 0, keys: 0 });
  // Stands in for another service: new data.RestAdapter({ url: '/api/customers', key: 'id' }) goes in its place.
  const service = new SlowAdapter<Customer, number>({ data: makeCustomers(600), key: 'id' }, 400);
  // Counts the requests that turn keys into names; the editor's own list loads are not among them.
  service.onLoading((e) => {
    const asked = e.options.filter as data.FilterCondition | undefined;
    if (asked?.op !== 'in' || !Array.isArray(asked.value)) return;
    s.requests++;
    s.keys = asked.value.length;
  });
  const customers = new data.DataSource<Customer, number>({ adapter: service });
  const sales: Sale[] = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, customerId: i === 4 ? 9999 : ((i * 37) % 600) + 1, amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100 }));
  const columns: GridColumn<Sale>[] = [
    { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, editable: false },
    {
      field: 'customerId',
      title: 'Customer',
      width: 220,
      flex: 1,
      required: true,
      filterRow: true,
      headerFilter: true,
      lookup: {
        dataSource: customers,
        valueField: 'id',
        textField: 'name',
        editor: 'lookup',
        editorOptions: { columns: [{ field: 'name', caption: 'Name' }, { field: 'city', caption: 'City', width: '7rem' }] },
      },
    },
    { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 120, filterRow: true, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
  ];
  let grid: DataGrid<Sale> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-lookups"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={sales}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sales with customers from another service"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        settings={{ editable: true, filterDelay: 200 }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Sale>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Read the names again" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.refreshLookups()} />
        <output class="dg-lookup-requests">{() => `${s.requests} requests for names to the customers service, the last for ${s.keys} customers`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Cascade.tsx`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { DISTRICTS, PROVINCES } from './places';

type Branch = { id: number; name: string; province: string | null; district: number | null };

const branches: Branch[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Head office', province: 'AN', district: 1 },
  { id: 2, name: 'Harbour', province: 'IZ', district: 9 },
  { id: 3, name: 'Bridge', province: 'IS', district: 6 },
  { id: 4, name: 'Not placed yet', province: null, district: null },
];

const columns: GridColumn<Branch>[] = [
  { field: 'name', title: 'Branch', width: 160, flex: 1, required: true },
  {
    field: 'province',
    title: 'Province',
    width: 150,
    lookup: { dataSource: PROVINCES, valueField: 'code', textField: 'name' },
    // Another province empties the district.
    setCellValue: (values) => {
      values.district = null;
    },
  },
  {
    field: 'district',
    title: 'District',
    width: 150,
    lookup: {
      dataSource: DISTRICTS,
      valueField: 'id',
      textField: 'name',
      allowClearing: true,
      // The districts of the province entered (else the row's); every district for the filter lists.
      filter: (row, { getValue }) => (row ? data.where('province', '=', getValue('province')) : null),
    },
  },
];

/** Province and district: a new province clears the district, whose list follows the province and waits for one. */
export default function Cascade() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-cascade"
      style="block-size: 24rem"
      rows={branches}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={columns}
      label="Branches"
      locale="en"
      settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, filterRow: true, headerFilter: true }}
      newRow={{ create: () => ({ id: Math.max(0, ...branches.map((b) => b.id)) + 1, province: null, district: null }) }}
      onEditorPreparing={(e) => {
        if (e.field === 'district') e.options.enabled = e.getValue('province') !== null;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

`TextFrom.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

/** An invoice as its service sends it: the customer comes along with it (OData `$expand=customer`). */
type Invoice = { id: number; customerId: number; customer: { name: string }; total: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The name read from the row itself: the customers' service is asked only to edit. */
export default function TextFrom() {
  const s = reactive({ requests: 0 });
  const people = makeCustomers(600);
  const invoices: Invoice[] = Array.from({ length: 5_000 }, (_, i) => {
    const customer = people[(i * 53) % people.length];
    return { id: i + 1, customerId: customer.id, customer: { name: customer.name }, total: ((i * 4337) % 50_000) / 10 };
  });
  // Stand in for two services: new data.ODataAdapter({ url: '/odata/Invoices', key: 'id' }) with expand: ['customer'], and the customers'.
  const invoiceSource = new data.DataSource<Invoice, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Invoice, number>({ data: invoices, key: 'id' }, 250), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const customerService = new SlowAdapter<Customer, number>({ data: people, key: 'id' }, 400);
  customerService.onLoading(() => s.requests++);
  const columns: GridColumn<Invoice>[] = [
    { field: 'id', title: 'Invoice', type: 'number', width: 100, editable: false },
    {
      field: 'customerId',
      title: 'Customer',
      width: 220,
      flex: 1,
      textFrom: 'customer.name',
      sortField: 'customer.name',
      lookup: { dataSource: new data.DataSource<Customer, number>({ adapter: customerService }), valueField: 'id', textField: 'name' },
    },
    { field: 'total', title: 'Total', type: 'number', width: 120, editable: false, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid class="dg-text-from" style="block-size: 28rem" dataSource={invoiceSource} columns={columns} label="Invoices" locale="en" saveMode="batch" settings={{ editable: true }} />
      <output class="dg-text-from-requests">{() => `${s.requests} requests to the customers service`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Grouping and summaries

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Grouping

Rows are grouped by one column or several: a row per group shows “Column: value (count)” — a lookup column its text, rows in memory the column's format — with an arrow that opens and closes it, and the groups below it moved in. Grouped columns leave the columns unless `showWhenGrouped`. `groupIndex` on the columns groups at the start; `groupPanel` puts the panel at the start of the toolbar, where a header dropped groups by its column; a chip turns the order of its groups when clicked, moves along the panel and, dragged back onto the headers, ungroups the column where it lands. The column menu does the same from the keyboard. A sort sorts the rows inside the groups; the header of a grouped column, like its chip, sorts its groups; `calculateGroupValue` groups by a value of its own. Paged, the pages count group rows and data rows; a closed group is one row.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

On a server: a `DataSource` that loads by `blocks` over an adapter that groups is asked only for the groups with their counts (`loadGroups`, `group` with `groupsOnly`); the rows come in group order, in blocks, only for the open groups where the list looks — here the groups start closed (`autoExpandGroup: false`). An adapter that cannot group (OData, REST), a source that loads by page, or a `calculateGroupValue` function gets every matching row, grouped in the browser without remote grouping. Filters, the search and selection work over the groups; “select all” stays every row of the filter. The CSV export writes a “Column: value” line before each group; `group` is kept with the layout.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Summaries

`summary` gives values of the rows under the filter and the search: `totalItems` in a row of totals under the rows — it stays at the bottom while the rows scroll and moves sideways with the columns — and `groupItems` for each group: after the group row's count, under their column in the group row (`alignByColumn`), or in a footer row after the group's rows (`showInGroupFooter`). An item aggregates a `column` (its `value` reader too) with `summaryType` `sum`, `min`, `max`, `avg`, `count` or `custom`, shows under `showInColumn` (else its column), several in one column one under the other, and its text is `displayFormat` (`{0}` the value, `{1}` the column) or a text of `summary.texts` and `uiLocale`, formatted by `valueFormat` (`Intl` options or a function; else the column's format), or `customizeText`. A `custom` item goes through `calculateCustomSummary` in three steps: `start`, `calculate` per row, `finalize`. Empty values are left out (`skipEmptyValues`; `count` counts every row). Unsaved edits count once saved, or as they are made with `recalculateWhileEditing`. `getTotalSummaryValue(name)` and `getGroupSummaryValue(key, name)` read the values; `onSummaryChanged` tells when they are worked out again; the CSV and `exportRows()` write the footers and the totals.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

On a server: a source that loads pages or blocks asks its adapter for the totals of the query when the adapter has the `summary` capability (`remoteSummary`; `DataSource.loadSummary`), and asks for the group summaries with the groups when it groups (`loadGroups` with `groupSummary`). Here the made-up server does both: one request for the totals, one for the groups, whatever the list shows. An adapter without it, a `custom` item or a computed column get every matching row, loaded once per row set (`groupLoadPageSize` a request), and the values are worked out in the browser; group summaries only the browser can work out group the rows in the browser too.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `totalItems, groupItems` | The items of the row of totals and of each group; a function is followed. The items are kept as given: after a change in place call `grid.refreshSummary()`. |
| `calculateCustomSummary` | `(e) => void` with `{ name, summaryProcess, value, totalValue, groupIndex, component }`: one function for every `custom` item; set `e.totalValue` at `start`, fold `e.value` (the column’s value, or the row without a column) into it at each `calculate`, adjust it at `finalize`. |
| `recalculateWhileEditing` | `false`: the values follow unsaved edits, new rows and rows marked for deletion. Off, they change once the changes are saved. |
| `skipEmptyValues` | `true`: empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `''`) are left out of what the browser works out; off, `sum` and `avg` count them as 0. An item can set its own. |
| `texts` | The item texts by type: `sum`, `sumOtherColumn`, `min`, `minOtherColumn`, `max`, `maxOtherColumn`, `avg`, `avgOtherColumn`, `count`; over the `gridSummary…` texts of `uiLocale` and the grid’s `texts`. |

| Item field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `column` | The column aggregated. Without one, `count` counts rows and `custom` gets the rows themselves. |
| `summaryType` | `'sum' \| 'min' \| 'max' \| 'avg' \| 'count' \| 'custom'`, default `'count'`. |
| `name` | Names the item for `getTotalSummaryValue` and `calculateCustomSummary`. |
| `showInColumn` | The column the item shows under (default: `column`); away from its column the text names the column (“Sum of Amount: …”). |
| `valueFormat` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`, `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` or `(value) => string`; default: the column’s format (`count`: a plain number). |
| `displayFormat, customizeText` | The text, `{0}` the formatted value and `{1}` the column’s title; `({ value, valueText }) => string` wins over it. |
| `alignment, cssClass` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` (default: the column's); a class of your own on the item. |
| `skipEmptyValues` | Leave empty values out for this item; default `summary.skipEmptyValues`. |
| `visible` | Show the item; default the `totalSummary` (`groupSummary`) setting. |
| `showInGroupFooter, alignByColumn` | Group items: in the group footer; under their column in the group row, not under the first column, which holds the text. |

## Example files

`Grouping.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Orders in memory grouped by city, then by status; the group panel and the switches change it. */
export default function Grouping() {
  const s = reactive({ panel: true, dragging: true, open: true, collapsing: true, rowClick: false, showCity: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  const grouped = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, showWhenGrouped: () => s.showCity } : c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 1 } : c));

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Group panel" x-model={() => s.panel} />
        <CheckBox label="Drag to group" x-model={() => s.dragging} />
        <CheckBox label="Groups start open" x-model={() => s.open} />
        <CheckBox label="The user can open and close" x-model={() => s.collapsing} />
        <CheckBox label="A click on the row opens" x-model={() => s.rowClick} />
        <CheckBox label="City stays a column" x-model={() => s.showCity} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-grouping"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        rows={makeOrders(500)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={grouped}
        label="Orders by city and status"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          groupPanel: () => s.panel,
          groupPanelDragging: () => s.dragging,
          autoExpandAll: () => s.open,
          allowCollapsing: () => s.collapsing,
          groupExpandMode: () => (s.rowClick ? 'rowClick' : 'button'),
          selection: 'multiple',
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <Button text="Open only the cities" variant="outline" onclick={() => (grid?.expandAll(0), grid?.collapseAll(1))} />
        <Button text="Ungroup" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.clearGrouping()} />
        <output class="dg-grouping-state">{() => `Grouped by ${grid?.group.map((g) => `${g.field} ${g.dir}`).join(', ') || 'nothing'}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders grouped on the server: the groups come with their counts, the rows only where the list looks. */
export default function GroupingServer() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0 });
  // An adapter that groups (here rows in memory acting as a server) answers `group` itself; one
  // that cannot (OData, REST) gets every matching row grouped in the browser instead.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const grouped = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, autoExpandGroup: false } : c));
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-grouping-server"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={grouped}
        label="100,000 orders by status"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ groupPanel: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open “Shipped”" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandGroup(['Shipped'])} />
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <output class="dg-grouping-loads">{() => `${s.loads} loads for ${grid?.total ?? 0} rows`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Summaries.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridCustomSummaryInfo, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Totals under the rows, group summaries in the group rows and footers, and a custom one: paid orders. */
export default function Summaries() {
  const s = reactive({ grouped: true, footers: true, aligned: true, live: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  // The amount gets room for its totals.
  const byCity = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: () => (s.grouped ? 0 : undefined) } : c.field === 'amount' ? { ...c, width: 170 } : c));

  // Counts the paid orders: start, then each row, then the result.
  const calculateCustomSummary = (e: GridCustomSummaryInfo<Order>) => {
    if (e.summaryProcess === 'start') e.totalValue = 0;
    else if (e.summaryProcess === 'calculate' && (e.value as Order).paid) e.totalValue = (e.totalValue as number) + 1;
  };

  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    recalculateWhileEditing: () => s.live,
    totalItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
      { name: 'paid', summaryType: 'custom', showInColumn: 'paid', displayFormat: '{0} paid' },
      { column: 'date', summaryType: 'max', displayFormat: 'Last: {0}' },
      { name: 'total', column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'avg', valueFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 0 } },
    ],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: () => s.aligned },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max', showInGroupFooter: true, visible: () => s.footers },
      { name: 'paid', summaryType: 'custom', showInColumn: 'paid', showInGroupFooter: true, displayFormat: '{0} paid', visible: () => s.footers },
    ],
    calculateCustomSummary,
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Group by city" x-model={() => s.grouped} />
        <CheckBox label="Group footers" x-model={() => s.footers} />
        <CheckBox label="Sum under its column in the group row" x-model={() => s.aligned} />
        <CheckBox label="Follow unsaved edits" x-model={() => s.live} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-summaries"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        rows={makeOrders(300)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders with totals"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ editable: true, filterRow: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-summaries-total">{() => `The amounts add up to ${Number(grid?.getTotalSummaryValue('total') ?? 0).toLocaleString('en', { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`SummariesServer.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders on a server that computes the totals itself and gives the group summaries with the groups. */
export default function SummariesServer() {
  const s = reactive({ asked: 0 });
  // An adapter with the `summary` capability is asked for the values (`remoteSummary: 'auto'`); one
  // without it gets every matching row loaded once and the values worked out in the browser.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading((e) => {
    if (e.options.summary || e.options.groupSummary) s.asked++;
  });
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const byStatus = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, autoExpandGroup: false } : { ...c, filterRow: c.field === 'city' || c.field === 'amount', width: c.field === 'amount' ? 170 : c.width }));
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-summaries-server"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={byStatus}
        label="100,000 orders with server totals"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ groupPanel: true }}
        summary={{
          totalItems: [
            { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
            { name: 'total', column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max' },
          ],
          groupItems: [
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'avg', showInGroupFooter: true, valueFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 2 } },
            { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer', showInGroupFooter: true },
          ],
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <output class="dg-summaries-server-state">{() => `${s.asked} summary requests · totals ${grid?.summaryStatus ?? 'loading'}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```
