# DataGrid: Master-detail

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Master-detail

`masterDetail` gives every row details of its own: the expand column opens a row to show what `template` makes for it — here another grid over a data source of its own, filtered by the customer's key — in a row across the grid that stays in place while the columns scroll sideways. The details are made the first time they show and kept while the row is open; they go when the row leaves the data, or with the grid. The list stays virtual: each detail is measured as it is drawn (and again when its content changes size), so the scroll bar, the rows after it and moving to a row stay right, and the rows themselves are still a small pool.

```tsx
/** A customer, as another made-up service keeps it. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` made-up customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `masterDetail.enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The expand column, after the status and check box columns and pinned like them: the user opens and closes the details. Off, they open from code only. |
| `masterDetail.template` | `(ctx: DetailContext<T>) => unknown` | — | What a row’s details hold: a component (another `DataGrid`, a `FormLayout`, `Tabs` …), an element or a text. Made the first time the details show. `ctx`: `row` (the row itself) and `rowIndex`, both read again in getters when the row shows another one and on `grid.repaint()` or `grid.repaintRows(keys)`, `key`, `grid`, `collapse()`. |
| `masterDetail.autoExpandAll` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Every row starts open. Changing it, `enabled` or `template` opens or closes every row again. |
| `masterDetail.canExpand` | `Bind<boolean> \| (row) => boolean` | `true` | Whether a row has details; a row without has no arrow, and `expandRow` leaves it closed. New rows not saved yet have none. |
| `masterDetail.keepDetails` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A closed row keeps what its details hold and shows it as it was when it opens again; off, closing disposes it. |
| `masterDetail.keepAcrossPages` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Paged grid: the details of the page left keep what they hold while the user pages (up to `keepLimit`); off, another page or page size disposes them, and they are made again when their page shows. A row stays open either way. |
| `masterDetail.keepLimit` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | Details out of view that keep their content (open ones, and closed ones with `keepDetails`); past it the ones seen longest ago are disposed, and made again when they show. |
| `masterDetail.height` | `Bind<number> \| (row) => number` | the content’s | A height of their own in pixels, the content scrolling inside; a function gives each row its own. |
| `masterDetail.estimatedHeight` | `Bind<number>` | `200` | What details count as before they are drawn and measured, while none is; then the average of those measured. Only the scroll bar uses it. |
| `masterDetail.columnWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `36` | Width of the expand column, in pixels. |
| `masterDetail.toggleKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Enter', ' ']` | Keys on the expand cell that open and close the details. |
| `masterDetail.arrowKeys` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Right on the expand cell of a closed row opens it, Left on an open one closes it; otherwise they move as on any cell. |

Open rows are kept by key: sorting, the filters, the search, grouping and paging leave them open, and a row that comes back after a filter opens again. Selecting and editing the rows work as before; a row edited in the edit form keeps its details under the form. Copying and exporting leave the details out, and the saved layout does not keep which rows are open.

## Tabs and forms in the details

The details can hold any component. Here they are tabs: a read-only `FormLayout` with the customer, and a list of its orders made when the tab is first shown — the row takes its height, the rows after it move. `canExpand` leaves the customers without orders without an arrow; `ctx.collapse()` closes a row from inside its details; the buttons call `expandAllRows()` and `collapseAllRows()`.

```tsx
/** A customer, as another made-up service keeps it. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` made-up customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

The arrow is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the row says `aria-expanded` too. A row's details are a row of their own in the grid's reading order (`aria-owns`), right after it and counted in `aria-rowindex` and `aria-rowcount`, with one cell across the columns named “Details of row 3” (`gridDetailsOf`, `gridDetails` for the arrow and its column; both in `uiLocale` and the grid's `texts`).

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter, Space (`toggleKeys`)` | On the expand cell: opens or closes the row’s details. |
| `Right / Left (`arrowKeys`)` | On the expand cell: Right opens a closed row, Left closes an open one; then they move to the next cell. Mirrored right to left. |
| `Up / Down, Page Up / Page Down` | Move from row to row; a row’s details are passed over. |
| `Tab` | On a row whose details show: into the details, to their first stop. With details on the screen Tab otherwise leaves the grid, as Shift+Tab does from a row. |
| `Tab in the details` | Moves through their content; from the last stop it leaves the grid. |
| `Escape, Shift+Tab on the first stop` | Back to the row the details belong to (Escape the content does not use itself). |
| `Enter on the details’ own cell` | Into the content, to its first stop. |

## Events and methods

| Event | Gets | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onRowExpanding / onRowCollapsing` | `{ kind: 'detail', key, row, cancel }` | A row’s details are about to open or close, by the user or from code; `cancel` keeps them as they are. The same events as for groups (`kind: 'group'`). |
| `onRowExpanded / onRowCollapsed` | `{ kind: 'detail', key, row }` | They opened or closed. |
| `onRowPrepared` | `{ rowType: 'detail', row, rowIndex, element }` | A row’s details were drawn for a row. |
| `onOptionChanged` | `{ name: 'masterDetail.enabled', value, previous }` | A `masterDetail` option was assigned through `grid.masterDetail`. |

| Member | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expandRow(key) / collapseRow(key)` | `boolean` | Opens or closes a row’s details by its key, as the arrow does (the events come, `cancel` holds); a row not loaded, or one without details, does not. |
| `isRowExpanded(key)` | `boolean` | Whether a row’s details are open. Reactive. |
| `expandAllRows() / collapseAllRows()` | `void` | Opens or closes every row’s details at once, without row events (as `expandAll()` does for groups). |
| `masterDetail` | read/write, live | `grid.masterDetail.enabled = true`; a function is followed. |
| `getVisibleRows()` | `GridVisibleRow[]` | A row's details are listed right after it, `rowType: 'detail'`, with its index and key. |

## Example files

`MasterDetail.tsx`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { CustomerOrder } from './customer-order';
import { makeCustomerOrders, orderColumns } from './customer-orders';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

const customers = makeCustomers(2000);
const orders = new data.ArrayAdapter<CustomerOrder, number>({ data: makeCustomerOrders(customers), key: 'id' });

const columns: GridColumn<Customer>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'name', title: 'Customer', width: 220, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 140 },
];

/** A customer's orders: a grid over a source of its own, filtered by the customer's key, disposed with the details. */
function Orders(props: { customerId: unknown; name: string }) {
  const source = new data.DataSource<CustomerOrder, number>({ adapter: orders, loadMode: 'all', filter: data.where('customerId', '=', props.customerId) });
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-orders"
      style="block-size: 14rem"
      dataSource={source}
      columns={orderColumns}
      label={`Orders of ${props.name}`}
      locale="en"
      settings={{ rowCount: true }}
      onDisposing={() => source.dispose()}
    />
  );
}

/** Two thousand customers in a virtual list; each opens to a grid of its own orders. */
export default function MasterDetail() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-master"
      style="block-size: 30rem"
      rows={customers}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={columns}
      label="Customers and their orders"
      locale="en"
      masterDetail={{ enabled: true, template: (ctx) => <Orders customerId={ctx.key} name={ctx.row.name} /> }}
    />
  );
}
```

`customer-orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Customer } from './customers';
import type { CustomerOrder } from './customer-order';

const ITEMS = ['Notebook', 'Pencil set', 'Desk lamp', 'Chair', 'Monitor', 'Keyboard', 'Coffee beans', 'Tea', 'Backpack', 'Umbrella'];
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** A few orders of every customer (none for every seventh), the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomerOrders(customers: Customer[]): CustomerOrder[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  const out: CustomerOrder[] = [];
  for (const c of customers) {
    const count = c.id % 7 === 0 ? 0 : 2 + (c.id % 5);
    for (let k = 0; k < count; k++) {
      const n = out.length + 1;
      out.push({
        id: n,
        customerId: c.id,
        date: new Date(day + ((n * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
        item: ITEMS[(n * 3) % ITEMS.length],
        quantity: 1 + (n % 4),
        amount: ((n * 7919) % 50_000) / 100,
      });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** The columns of a customer's orders. */
export const orderColumns: GridColumn<CustomerOrder>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130 },
  { field: 'item', title: 'Item', width: 180, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'quantity', title: 'Qty', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 120, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
];
```

`customer-order.ts`

```tsx
/** One order of a customer, for the master-detail examples. */
export interface CustomerOrder {

  customerId: number;
  date: string;
  item: string;
  quantity: number;
  amount: number;
}
```

`DetailTabs.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, FormLayout, Stack, Tab, Tabs, type DetailContext, type FormItem, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { makeCustomerOrders } from './customer-orders';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

const customers = makeCustomers(60);
const orders = makeCustomerOrders(customers);
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

/** What the details show of a customer: its fields and what its orders come to. */
interface Profile extends Customer {
  orders: number;
  total: string;
  since: string;
}

const profiles: Profile[] = customers.map((c) => {
  const own = orders.filter((o) => o.customerId === c.id);
  return { ...c, orders: own.length, total: money.format(own.reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.amount, 0)), since: own[0]?.date ?? '' };
});

const columns: GridColumn<Profile>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'name', title: 'Customer', width: 220, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 140 },
  { field: 'orders', title: 'Orders', type: 'number', width: 100 },
];

const items: FormItem[] = [
  { field: 'name', label: 'Name' },
  { field: 'city', label: 'City' },
  { field: 'since', label: 'First order' },
  { field: 'total', label: 'Orders total' },
];

/** A customer's details: tabs, the first a read-only form; the other tab is made when first shown, and the row grows with it. */
function CustomerTabs(props: { ctx: DetailContext<Profile> }) {
  const profile = reactive({ ...props.ctx.row });
  return (
    <Tabs label={`About ${profile.name}`} size="sm">
      <Tab title="Profile">
        <FormLayout data={profile} items={items} columns={2} readOnly />
      </Tab>
      <Tab title="Orders">
        <ul class="dg-detail-list">
          {orders
            .filter((o) => o.customerId === profile.id)
            .map((o) => (
              <li key={String(o.id)}>{`${o.date} · ${o.item} × ${o.quantity} · ${money.format(o.amount)}`}</li>
            ))}
        </ul>
        <Button text="Close" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => props.ctx.collapse()} />
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

/** Customers with tabs in their details; those without orders have none. The buttons open and close every row. */
export default function DetailTabs() {
  const s = reactive({ log: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Profile> | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Details">
        <Button text="Open all" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAllRows()} />
        <Button text="Close all" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAllRows()} />
        <output class="dg-detail-log">{() => s.log}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-detail-tabs"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Profile>) => (grid = g)}
        rows={profiles}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Customers with their details"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: 'single' }}
        masterDetail={{ enabled: true, canExpand: (row: Profile) => row.orders > 0, template: (ctx) => <CustomerTabs ctx={ctx} /> }}
        onRowExpanded={(e) => e.kind === 'detail' && (s.log = `Opened ${(e.row as Profile).name}`)}
        onRowCollapsed={(e) => e.kind === 'detail' && (s.log = `Closed ${(e.row as Profile).name}`)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Bands and adaptive columns

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Band headers

A band is a header over several columns (band column): give it a `title` and the `columns` under it — columns and other bands, to any depth. The header becomes a row per level of bands over the columns' own titles, each band spanning its columns. Drag a column: it moves only inside its band; drag a band: its columns go with it. A band is pinned, hidden and moved as a whole, from its own menu (its header's button, Alt+Down) or with `columnOption` by its `name`. Here “Payment” sits over three columns and “Order” over two columns and the “Delivery” band.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Band field | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title, columns` | `Bind<string>`, `(GridColumn \| GridBand)[]` | — | The band’s caption and what sits under it: columns and bands, to any depth. A band holds no data. |
| `name` | `string` | `band-` and its place | Its identity in the layout, `columnOption`, `columnSettings` and the events (`band-1`, `band-1-2` when it has none). |
| `isBand, ownerBand` | `boolean`, `string \| number` | — | Bands given flat’s `customizeColumns` does: a band with `isBand`, and columns (or bands) that name it in `ownerBand`, by `name` or by its place in `columns`. |
| `align` | `Bind<'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'>` | the `bandAlign` setting | Where the caption sits over its columns. |
| `sticky, hidden` | `'start' \| 'end'`, `boolean` | — | The band pinned, or hidden, with all its columns. A column inside a band takes its band’s side; pinning it pins the band. |
| `movable, hideable, pinnable, menu` | `Bind<boolean>` | the grid’s settings | What the user may do with the band: drag it among its neighbours, hide it, pin it, open its menu. |
| `headerCell` | `(ctx) => unknown` | — | Content of your own in the band’s header, made once; `ctx.band`, `ctx.title`. |
| `settings.bandAlign` | `Bind<'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'>` | `'center'` | Where the captions sit when a band does not say. |

| Topic | How bands do it |
| --- | --- |
| `Moving` | A column moves only among the columns and bands of its own band, a band among those beside it, both inside their pinned zone and not across one that cannot move (`movable: false`), by dragging the header, with “Move” in the menu and the arrow keys, or with `columnOption(name, 'visibleIndex', n)`. |
| `Sizing` | The columns are resized as always (the edge of a column’s header, a double-click fits it); a band follows its columns. |
| `Sorting and filters` | A band’s header does not sort and has no filter: its columns do, as before. |
| `Hiding` | Hiding every column of a band hides the band; hiding a band (its menu, `columnOption(name, 'visible', false)`) hides its columns. The last shown column stays. |
| `Column chooser` | With bands the list of columns is a tree with check boxes, the bands over their columns; a band’s check box shows or hides all of them. |
| `Layout` | `grid.layout` keeps the columns’ order, widths and hidden state, and `bands` with each band’s hidden state and side; a band’s place comes from its columns. A layout that tears a band apart puts it together where its first column is. `layoutKey` keeps it all. |
| `Export` | CSV writes a line per level of bands above the titles, each band’s title over its first column; `exportSheet()` adds header rows, and `merges` names the cells a band (and a column down the band rows) spans for the writer to merge. |
| `Rows` | Only the header changes: the rows, the virtual list and paging are as before. |

Band rows are `row`s of `columnheader`s in the head's row group: a band's header carries the `aria-colindex` of its first column and `aria-colspan` its columns, the columns keep their own index, and the band rows count in `aria-rowindex` and `aria-rowcount`. Over a pinned column no band covers an empty piece stays with the column, so the band rows scroll under it.

## Adaptive columns

With `settings.columnHidingEnabled` the grid hides columns while it is narrower than they are, the last one first; with a `hidingPriority` on some columns only those hide, the lowest first. A “…” column then opens a row's adaptive detail under it: the hidden columns' titles and values (editors where the row can be edited), one row at a time. It is worked out from the column widths and the grid's width (a `ResizeObserver`), never from what it draws, and again whenever either changes: drag the splitter. The hidden columns still count as shown — the column chooser, `getVisibleColumns()`, the export and copying have them.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.columnHidingEnabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Columns hide while the grid is narrower than they are, the last one first, and show in the rows’ adaptive detail. |
| `column.hidingPriority` | `Bind<number>` | — | Given on any column, only columns with one hide (without `columnHidingEnabled` too), the lowest first. Pinned and grouped columns never hide. |
| `adaptiveDetail.colCount, minColWidth, labelMode` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<string>`, `Bind<'top' \| 'side' \| 'floating' \| 'hidden'>` | `2`, —, `'side'` | How the detail lays out its form (the kit’s `FormLayout`). |
| `adaptiveDetail.editors` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Editors instead of texts for the cells the user can fill, in the `row`, `cell` and `batch` edit modes; they write into the row’s draft as its cells do. |
| `adaptiveDetail.expandOnEdit` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Editing a row whose hidden columns it can fill opens its detail, and leaving the row closes it again (the `row` edit mode). |
| `adaptiveDetail.columnWidth, toggleKeys` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<string[]>` | `36`, `['Enter', ' ']` | The “…” column’s width; the keys on its cell that open and close the detail. |

The detail is a row of its own right after its row, before the row's master-detail when both are open (order): measured as it is drawn, in the reading order (`aria-owns`), counted in `aria-rowindex`, its one cell named “Hidden columns of row 3” (`gridAdaptiveOf`; `gridAdaptive` names the “…” and its column). Grouped rows, paging and the virtual list keep it under its row; a wider grid with nothing hidden closes it.

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Up on a column’s header` | To its band’s header; again to the band above. |
| `Down on a band’s header` | To the first column or band under it. |
| `Left / Right, Home / End on a band’s header` | Along the bands of its row. |
| `Alt+Down, the context menu key on a band’s header` | Its menu: pin, move, hide the band, the column chooser, reset. |
| `Enter, Space on the “…” cell (`toggleKeys`)` | Opens or closes the row’s adaptive detail. |
| `Tab on a row whose detail shows` | Into the detail; from its last stop into the row’s master-detail, or, while the row is edited, on to the next row’s cells. |
| `Tab on the last cell editor of a row` | Into the editors of its open adaptive detail. |
| `Escape, Shift+Tab on the detail’s first stop` | Back to the row. |

## Events and methods

| Member | Gets or returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowPreparing` | `{ row, key, rowIndex, editors, formOptions }` | A row’s detail is about to lay out its form, when it opens and again when other columns hide or show: change `formOptions` (`items` — the hidden fields, or kit form items —, `colCount`, `minColWidth`, `labelMode`). |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowExpanding / onAdaptiveDetailRowCollapsing` | `{ row, key, rowIndex, cancel }` | A row’s detail is about to open or close, from its “…”, its keys or code; `cancel` keeps it as it is. |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowExpanded / onAdaptiveDetailRowCollapsed` | `{ row, key, rowIndex }` | It opened or closed. |
| `expandAdaptiveDetailRow(key) / collapseAdaptiveDetailRow()` | `boolean` | Opens a row’s detail by its key (the one open closes first), or closes the one open. |
| `isAdaptiveDetailRowExpanded(key)` | `boolean` | Whether that row’s detail is open. Reactive. |
| `adaptiveHiddenColumns` | `string[]`, reactive | The columns the width hides now, in display order. |
| `adaptiveDetail` | read/write, live | `grid.adaptiveDetail.colCount = 1`; `onOptionChanged` tells `adaptiveDetail.colCount`. |
| `getVisibleRows()` | `GridVisibleRow[]` | The open detail right after its row, `rowType: 'detailAdaptive'`, before the row's master-detail. |

## Example files

`BandHeaders.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumnItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { makeOrders } from './orders';

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** Two levels of bands over the order columns. */
const columns: GridColumnItem<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 70 },
  {
    name: 'order',
    title: 'Order',
    columns: [
      { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 170 },
      { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 120 },
      {
        name: 'delivery',
        title: 'Delivery',
        columns: [
          { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 120 },
          { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 220 },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    name: 'payment',
    title: 'Payment',
    align: 'end',
    columns: [
      { field: 'status', title: 'Status', width: 110 },
      { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 70 },
      { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 110, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
    ],
  },
];

/** Band headers: drag a column inside its band or a band among its neighbours, pin and hide bands from their menus. */
export default function BandHeaders() {
  const s = reactive({ csv: '', layout: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  const showLayout = () => (s.layout = grid ? JSON.stringify(grid.layout.bands) : '');

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Pin “Order”" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('order', 'sticky', grid.columnOption('order', 'sticky') ? null : 'start')} />
        <Button text="Hide or show “Delivery”" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('delivery', 'visible', !grid.columnOption('delivery', 'visible'))} />
        <Button text="Columns…" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.showColumnChooser()} />
        <Button
          text="CSV header"
          variant="ghost"
          onclick={async () => {
            const csv = (await grid?.exportCsv({ download: false, bom: false, separator: ',' })) ?? '';
            s.csv = csv.split('\r\n').slice(0, 3).join('\n');
          }}
        />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-bands"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders under band headers"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ columnChooserButton: true }}
        onLayoutChange={() => showLayout()}
        onContentReady={() => showLayout()}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-bands-layout">{() => `bands: ${s.layout}`}</output>
      <pre class="dg-bands-csv" x-display={() => s.csv !== ''}>
        {() => s.csv}
      </pre>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

```tsx
import { createSignal, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Panel, SplitContainer, Stack, type GridColumn, type SplitPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { makeOrders } from './orders';

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The columns hide in this order as the grid gets narrower: the note first, the customer never. */
const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 60, editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 140 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 100, hidingPriority: 3 },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 110, hidingPriority: 2, editable: false },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', width: 100, hidingPriority: 4 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 180, hidingPriority: 0 },
  { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 100, hidingPriority: 1, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
];

/** Adaptive columns: drag the splitter (or use the buttons) to make the grid narrower; the "…" opens a row's hidden values. */
export default function AdaptiveColumns() {
  const s = reactive({ width: '70%' as SplitPosition });
  const grid = createSignal<DataGrid<Order> | null>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Narrow" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.width = 420)} />
        <Button text="Medium" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.width = 640)} />
        <Button text="Wide" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.width = '100%')} />
        <Button text="Open row 3" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid.value?.expandAdaptiveDetailRow(3)} />
        <output class="dg-adaptive-hidden">{() => `hidden: ${grid.value?.adaptiveHiddenColumns.join(', ') || 'none'}`}</output>
      </Stack>

          class="dg-adaptive"
          style="block-size: 100%"
          rows={makeOrders(300)}
          rowKey="id"
          columns={columns}
          label="Orders that adapt to their width"
          locale="en"
          settings={{ editable: true }}
          saveMode="batch"
          ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid.value = g)}
        />
        <Panel text="Room" padding="sm">
          <p>The space the grid gives up.</p>
        </Panel>
      </SplitContainer>
    </>
  );
}
```

---

# DataGrid: Selection and export

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Selection

`selection` is `single` (the selection follows the active row) or `multiple`, with a check box column. A click selects a row, Ctrl adds or takes out, Shift selects a range; Shift+Space, Shift+arrows and Ctrl+A do it from the keyboard. The header check box selects every row of the filter — on a server too: the grid keeps a state, “all but these keys”, never the rows. `selection` gives that state, `selectionFilter` the same as a filter for the server. Selected rows wear the design language's own selection look, as its lists and trees do: its fill and text colour, and its frame, raised effect or bar at the start where it has them; the hover and the active row's tint lie over it, the keyboard focus ring on top, and a selected row stays one row high.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Copy and paste

Ctrl+C copies the selected rows, or the active cell, as tab-separated text and an HTML table: a spreadsheet or a document takes it as a table. Ctrl+V on a cell writes tab-separated text — from a spreadsheet, or copied here — into the editable cells from that cell rightwards and downwards. Each value is read by the column type (numbers and dates in the locale, yes or no, a list option by its text) and goes into the row's draft with its checks, as if typed; cells that cannot be edited keep their values. The rows below the active one are saved as the save mode says.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Export

`exportCsv()` saves the rows of the filter, in the sort order, with the visible columns in their order, as a CSV file a spreadsheet opens as it is: UTF-8 with a byte order mark, the locale's separator (`;` where decimals take a comma), the column titles first, and text that would run as a formula made harmless. `exportRows()` gives the same rows as objects. Rows in memory are taken as they are; a server's are asked for in parts through the data source, so its filter, search and sort apply and nothing on the screen changes. `exportButton` puts an “Export” button in the toolbar; `exportable` takes a column out.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Export to Excel

the grid does not carry an xlsx writer: the app brings ExcelJS (`npm i exceljs`, an optional peer dependency) and calls `exportDataGrid({ component, worksheet })` from `@motifx-community/ui/excel` — a separate entry, so apps that never export to Excel never load it. With `export: { formats: ['xlsx', 'csv'] }` the toolbar's export button becomes a menu (“Export all data to Excel”, “Export selected rows to Excel” with `allowExportSelectedData`); the Excel commands raise `onExporting` with `format: 'xlsx'` and `selectedRowsOnly`, and the handler writes the workbook and saves it, here as a Blob download with ExcelJS loaded on the first export.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

The sheet holds the header row (frozen), the rows in the grid's order with its filter, search and grouping — every matching row, a server's loaded in parts while a panel over the rows shows the progress and a button that stops it — the group rows (“Column: value” with their summary items, those aligned by column under their columns) with outline levels Excel folds, the group footers and the totals. Numbers stay numbers with a number format made from the column's `Intl` format, dates stay dates, yes/no cells are Excel's `TRUE` / `FALSE` (`booleanText` writes the grid's text), lookup and list cells hold their texts, a column with a `format` function its text, and widths follow the grid. `customizeCell({ gridCell, excelCell })` changes any cell; `gridCell` has `rowType`, `column`, `data`, `value`, `groupIndex`, `groupSummaryItems` and `totalSummaryItemName`. The promise resolves with the cells written, `{ from, to }`.

| exportDataGrid option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `component, worksheet` | — | The grid, and the ExcelJS worksheet to write to (`workbook.addWorksheet('Orders')`). |
| `topLeftCell` | `{ row: 1, column: 1 }` | Where the first cell goes: `{ row, column }` or a reference such as `'B2'`. |
| `customizeCell` | — | `({ gridCell, excelCell }) => void` for every cell, after its value and style are set. |
| `autoFilterEnabled` | `false` | Excel’s filter buttons on the header row. |
| `keepColumnWidths` | `true` | Columns as wide as in the grid. |
| `selectedRowsOnly` | the toolbar’s command, else `false` | Only the selected rows (no group rows or summaries, as with CSV). |
| `loadPanel` | on | The panel over the rows while they load: `true` / `false`, or `{ enabled, text, showProgress, cancelButton }`. |
| `encodeExecutableContent` | `false` | Text a spreadsheet would run as a formula gets a `'` in front. |
| `headers, frozenHeader` | `true` | The row of column titles; it stays in view while the sheet scrolls. |
| `groups, outline, summaries` | `true` | Group rows; outline levels by group (at most 7); group summary items, footers and the totals. |
| `numberFormats, booleanText` | `true`, `false` | Excel number formats from the columns’ `Intl` formats; the grid’s yes/no text instead of `TRUE` / `FALSE`. |
| `pageSize, onProgress, signal` | the `exportPageSize` setting | Rows per request to a server; told after each part; stops the export (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`). |

## Export to PDF

The same way for PDF: the app brings jsPDF (`npm i jspdf`, an optional peer dependency) and calls `exportDataGrid({ jsPDFDocument, component })` from `@motifx-community/ui/pdf`, its own entry. Add `'pdf'` to `export.formats` and the toolbar's menu offers “Export all data to PDF” (and the selected rows); the command raises `onExporting` with `format: 'pdf'`, and the handler makes the document, draws the grid on it and saves it. The table is drawn with jsPDF's own calls, no table plugin: the header rows with bands merged over their columns, the rows in the grid's order with its filter, search and grouping and the texts and alignment the grid shows, the group rows across the row, the group footers and the totals. Columns take the grid's widths, narrowed to fit the page; rows that do not fit go on to the next page under the header rows again; right to left, the columns run from the right edge.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

jsPDF's own fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier) write Latin-1 only: Turkish letters such as İ, ş and ğ, and Cyrillic, Greek or Arabic text, need a TrueType font that has them, added to the document before the export (`doc.addFileToVFS`, `doc.addFont`, `doc.setFont`) — with a bold style too, which group rows and totals use. This example fetches Noto Sans the first time it exports and keeps jsPDF's font when it cannot. The promise resolves with where the table ends (`{ page, y }`), to go on writing under it.

| exportDataGrid option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jsPDFDocument, component` | — | The jsPDF document to draw on (`new jsPDF()`; the table starts on its current page), and the grid. |
| `topLeft` | `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` | Where the table starts, from the top left margin, on its first page. |
| `margin` | 40 points on every side | Space kept free at the page’s edges: a number, or `{ top, right, bottom, left }`. |
| `columnWidths` | the grid’s, made to fit | Each column’s width, in order; one left out takes the grid’s. |
| `fitColumns` | `'shrink'` | Without `columnWidths`: the grid's widths narrowed when wider than the page (`'shrink'`), always as wide as it (`'fill'`), or as they are (`'none'`). |
| `repeatHeaders` | `true` | The header rows (bands included) again at the top of every page. |
| `indent` | `0` | How far the rows of a group sit in from its group row, per level. |
| `customizeCell` | — | `({ gridCell, pdfCell }) => void` for every cell before the rows are measured: `text`, `font` (`size`, `name`, `style`), `textColor`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, the four `draw…Border`s, `horizontalAlign`, `verticalAlign`, `padding`, `wordWrapEnabled`. |
| `customDrawCell` | — | `({ doc, rect, gridCell, pdfCell, cancel }) => void` before a cell is drawn: draw it yourself (an image, a bar) and set `cancel` (the borders are still drawn). |
| `onRowExporting` | — | `({ rowCells, rowHeight }) => void` before a row is placed: a taller `rowHeight` (never less than its text needs). |
| `wordWrapEnabled, fontSize` | `false`, `10` | Long text on more lines (off: a line that does not fit ends in “…”); the cells’ font size in points. |
| `selectedRowsOnly` | the toolbar’s command, else `false` | Only the selected rows (no group rows or summaries, as with CSV and Excel). |
| `loadPanel` | on | The panel over the rows while they load, with the progress and a Stop button; `true` / `false`, or `{ enabled, text, showProgress, cancelButton }`. |
| `headers, groups, summaries` | `true` | The header rows; a row per group; group summary items, footers and the totals. |
| `pageSize, onProgress, signal` | the `exportPageSize` setting | Rows per request to a server; told after each part; stops the export (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`, nothing is drawn). |

## Example files

`Selection.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction, type GridSelection } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const MODES = ['none', 'single', 'multiple'] as const;

const describe = (sel: GridSelection | undefined) =>
  !sel ? '' : sel.all ? `all but ${sel.except.length} (${sel.except.slice(0, 5).join(', ')})` : `${sel.keys.length} picked (${sel.keys.slice(0, 5).join(', ')})`;

/** Single and multiple selection; over 100,000 rows on a server "all" is a state, never the rows. */
export default function Selection() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'multiple' as 'none' | 'single' | 'multiple', selection: undefined as GridSelection | undefined, note: '' });
  // The server groups, so "all but these keys" goes to it as a filter.
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 200), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  let server: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const print: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'print', text: 'Print', onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Order ${row.id} sent to the printer`) };
  const mail: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'mail', text: 'Mail the customer', disabled: (row) => !row.paid, onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Mail to ${row.customer}`) };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Selection mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-selection"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(40)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to select"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: () => s.mode }}
        onSelectionChanged={(e) => (s.selection = e.selection)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-selection-state">{() => `${(grid?.selectedCount ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} selected: ${describe(s.selection)}`}</output>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-server-selection"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="100,000 orders to select"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: 'multiple' }}
        actions={[print, mail]}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (server = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-server-selection-state">{() => `${(server?.selectedCount ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} selected: ${describe(server?.selection)}`}</output>
      <output>{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Clipboard.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V as tab-separated text, and the same from code. */
export default function Clipboard() {
  const s = reactive({ raw: false, headers: false, newRows: false, copied: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Values, not the shown text" x-model={() => s.raw} />
        <CheckBox label="Column titles" x-model={() => s.headers} />
        <CheckBox label="New rows from extra lines" x-model={() => s.newRows} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-clipboard"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(20)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to copy"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        settings={{
          editable: true,
          addRows: true,
          selection: 'multiple',
          copyValues: () => (s.raw ? 'raw' : 'shown'),
          copyHeaders: () => s.headers,
          pasteNewRows: () => s.newRows,
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Copy from code" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.copied = grid?.copy() ?? '')} />
        <Button text="Paste two lines at the active cell" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.paste('Ada Lovelace\tİzmir\nGrace Hopper\tAnkara')} />
        <output class="dg-copied">{() => (s.copied ? `Copied: ${s.copied.replace(/\t/g, ' → ').replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ¶ ')}` : '')}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Export.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';
import { pagedOrders } from './paged-orders';

/** The bar's "Export" button, rows as objects, and 100,000 rows of a server saved in parts. */
export default function Export() {
  const s = reactive({ exported: '', progress: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const firstTwo = async () => {
    const rows = (await grid?.exportRows({ values: 'raw' })) ?? [];
    s.exported = JSON.stringify(rows.slice(0, 2));
  };

  // A grid made with `new` exports without being shown; this one reads the orders of the paged grid.
  const exportServer = async () => {
    const server = new DataGrid<Order>({ dataSource: pagedOrders, columns, label: 'Orders by page', locale: 'en' });
    s.progress = 'starting…';
    try {
      await server.exportCsv({ pageSize: 10_000, fileName: 'orders', onProgress: (n, total) => (s.progress = `${n.toLocaleString('en')} of ${total.toLocaleString('en')}`) });
      s.progress += ' — saved';
    } catch {
      s.progress = 'failed';
    } finally {
      server.dispose();
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-export"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders to export"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ exportButton: true, filterRow: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="The first two rows as objects" variant="outline" onclick={firstTwo} />
        <Button text="Export the 100,000 orders by page" variant="outline" onclick={() => void exportServer()} />
      </Stack>
      <output class="dg-exported">{() => s.exported}</output>
      <output class="dg-export-progress">{() => (s.progress ? `Server export: ${s.progress}` : '')}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`ExcelExport.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, type GridExportingEventArgs, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { exportDataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui/excel';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Saves a file through a link the browser downloads. */
function saveFile(blob: Blob, name: string) {
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const link = document.createElement('a');
  link.href = url;
  link.download = name;
  link.click();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}

/** The toolbar's export menu: Excel through ExcelJS and `exportDataGrid`, CSV by the grid itself. */
export default function ExcelExport() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  // Grouped by city; the amount in `Intl` options, which become its Excel number format.
  const byCity = columns.map((c) =>
    c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0 } : c.field === 'amount' ? { ...c, width: 150, format: { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 } } : c,
  );
  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    totalItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
    ],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: true },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max', showInGroupFooter: true },
    ],
  };

  // The grid raises onExporting for 'xlsx'; the file is written here. ExcelJS
  // loads the first time, so the page does not carry it until someone exports.
  const onExporting = async (e: GridExportingEventArgs) => {
    if (e.format !== 'xlsx') return;
    const { default: ExcelJS } = await import('exceljs');
    const workbook = new ExcelJS.Workbook();
    const worksheet = workbook.addWorksheet('Orders');
    const range = await exportDataGrid({
      component: e.component,
      worksheet,
      selectedRowsOnly: e.selectedRowsOnly,
      autoFilterEnabled: true,
      customizeCell: ({ gridCell, excelCell }) => {
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'data' && gridCell.column?.field === 'status' && gridCell.value === 'Cancelled') excelCell.font = { color: { argb: 'FFB42318' } };
      },
    });
    const buffer = await workbook.xlsx.writeBuffer();
    saveFile(new Blob([buffer], { type: 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet' }), 'Orders.xlsx');
    s.saved = `Orders.xlsx: rows ${range.from.row}–${range.to.row}, columns ${range.from.column}–${range.to.column}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-excel"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders for Excel"
        locale="en"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ exportButton: true, selection: 'multiple' }}
        export={{ formats: ['xlsx', 'csv'], allowExportSelectedData: true }}
        onExporting={onExporting}
      />
      <output class="dg-excel-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`PdfExport.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, type GridExportingEventArgs, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { exportDataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui/pdf';
import type { jsPDF } from 'jspdf';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

// jsPDF's own fonts write Latin-1 only: "İzmir" and "İlhan Koman" need a font that has their letters.
const FONT = 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@expo-google-fonts/noto-sans@0.2.3/';
let font: Promise<{ regular: string; bold: string }> | null = null;

async function base64(url: string): Promise<string> {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer());
  let text = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 0x8000) text += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));
  return btoa(text);
}

/** Noto Sans in the document, fetched once; without the network the document keeps jsPDF's own font. */
async function useNotoSans(doc: jsPDF) {
  font ??= Promise.all([base64(`${FONT}NotoSans_400Regular.ttf`), base64(`${FONT}NotoSans_700Bold.ttf`)]).then(([regular, bold]) => ({ regular, bold }));
  try {
    const { regular, bold } = await font;
    doc.addFileToVFS('NotoSans-Regular.ttf', regular);
    doc.addFont('NotoSans-Regular.ttf', 'NotoSans', 'normal');
    doc.addFileToVFS('NotoSans-Bold.ttf', bold);
    doc.addFont('NotoSans-Bold.ttf', 'NotoSans', 'bold');
    doc.setFont('NotoSans', 'normal');
  } catch {
    font = null;
  }
}

/** The toolbar's export menu with PDF: `onExporting` draws the grid on a jsPDF document and saves it. */
export default function PdfExport() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  const byCity = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0 } : c));
  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    totalItems: [{ column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' }],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', showInGroupFooter: true },
    ],
  };

  // the grid raises onExporting for 'pdf' and the file is made here. jsPDF loads
  // the first time someone exports.
  const onExporting = async (e: GridExportingEventArgs) => {
    if (e.format !== 'pdf') return;
    const { jsPDF } = await import('jspdf');
    const doc = new jsPDF({ orientation: 'landscape' });
    await useNotoSans(doc);
    doc.setFontSize(14);
    doc.text('Orders by city', 14, 14);
    const end = await exportDataGrid({
      jsPDFDocument: doc,
      component: e.component,
      selectedRowsOnly: e.selectedRowsOnly,
      topLeft: { y: 6 },
      margin: 14,
      indent: 4,
      customizeCell: ({ gridCell, pdfCell }) => {
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'group') pdfCell.backgroundColor = '#EEF2F8';
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'data' && gridCell.column?.field === 'status' && gridCell.value === 'Cancelled') pdfCell.textColor = '#B42318';
      },
    });
    doc.save('Orders.pdf');
    s.saved = `Orders.pdf: ${doc.getNumberOfPages()} pages, the table ends on page ${end.page}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-pdf"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(120)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders for PDF"
        locale="en"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ exportButton: true, selection: 'multiple' }}
        export={{ formats: ['pdf', 'csv'], allowExportSelectedData: true }}
        onExporting={onExporting}
      />
      <output class="dg-pdf-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Row drag and drop

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Reorder rows

With `rowDragging: { allowReordering: true }` a column of drag icons comes at the start: take a row by its icon and drag it, a copy of the row follows the pointer and a line shows where it would land — or, with `dropFeedbackMode: 'push'`, the rows move aside to make room for it. Near the top or bottom edge the rows scroll. Drop it and `onReorder` tells where it went:, the grid does not move the data itself, the handler does. Here the rows are in memory: take the row out and splice it in where `toItemData` (the row at `toIndex`) is. Ctrl+Shift+Up and Down move the active row the same way.

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  priority: string;
  /** Its place in the list, as a server keeps it. */
  order: number;
}
```

## Reorder rows on a server

On a server the order is a field the rows are sorted by. The handler asks the server to move the row to the place of `toItemData` and gives the grid the promise (`e.promise`): the line stays until the answer comes, then `refresh()` loads the rows in their new order. 10,000 rows, the virtual list loading blocks as it scrolls.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Drag rows between grids

Grids with the same `group` take each other's rows: drop a row on the other grid and `onRemove` comes on the grid it left, `onAdd` on the one it went to (pair), with `toIndex` and `toItemData` saying where. Both grids here push their rows aside and reorder too.

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  priority: string;
  /** Its place in the list, as a server keeps it. */
  order: number;
}
```

## Options

| rowDragging | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowReordering` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Rows move within the grid. |
| `allowDropInsideItem` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A row can be dropped onto another (the middle half of a row): `dropInsideItem` in the events, for trees and details. |
| `dropFeedbackMode` | `Bind<'indicate' \| 'push'>` | `'indicate'` | Where a drop would land: a line between the rows, or the rows moving aside to make room for it (not with `allowDropInsideItem`). |
| `showDragIcons` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A column of drag icons, pinned to the start, to drag rows by; off, the whole row is dragged (a click still selects and edits). |
| `handle` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A CSS selector of what a row is dragged by, instead of the icon or the whole row. |
| `group, data` | `Bind<string>`, `Bind<unknown>` | — | Grids of the same group take each other’s rows; `data` is handed to the events as `fromData` / `toData`. |
| `dragDirection` | `Bind<'both' \| 'vertical' \| 'horizontal'>` | `'both'` | Where the copy of the row may go. |
| `boundary, container` | `Bind<string \| HTMLElement>` | none, the grid | The element the dragged row stays inside; the element its copy is shown in. |
| `cursorOffset` | `Bind<{ x, y } \| string>` | where the row was taken | Where the copy sits from the pointer. |
| `dragTemplate` | `({ itemData, itemElement }) => unknown` | a copy of the row | Content of your own under the pointer: a component, an element or a text. |
| `autoScroll, scrollSpeed, scrollSensitivity` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<number>`, `Bind<number>` | `true`, `30`, `60` | The rows scroll while the pointer is near their top or bottom edge: pixels per frame at the edge, and how near it starts. |
| `keyboard, moveUpKeys, moveDownKeys` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<string[]>` | `true`, `['Ctrl+Shift+ArrowUp']`, `['Ctrl+Shift+ArrowDown']` | The active row moves a place up or down with these keys (any chord: `Mod+Alt+Up`…), with the same events as a drop; announced. |
| `columnWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `36` | Width of the drag icon column, in pixels. |
| `settings.dragThreshold, settings.dragGhost` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<boolean>` | `5`, `true` | How far the pointer moves before a drag starts, and whether a copy follows it; the same as for headers. |

| Topic | How dragging does it |
| --- | --- |
| `The data` | The grid moves nothing itself (as in the standard grid): `onReorder` and `onAdd` / `onRemove` move the row in your array or tell the server. The grid reads your rows as they are, plain or reactive: after the move call `e.component.refresh()` (rows in memory and a server alike). |
| `Sorted, filtered, grouped` | Rows can be dragged as they are shown; the indexes are the shown ones. A list the user orders by hand usually turns `sortable` off; while grouped the keys move a row within its group, and only data rows are dragged (not group rows, new rows or rows still loading). |
| `Virtual and paged` | The rows under the pointer are the pooled rows drawn now; near the edges the rows scroll and the new ones take the marks. Paged, a row moves within its page; the indexes count across pages. |
| `Screen readers` | The drag icon cell is named “Drag to move the row” with the keys in `aria-keyshortcuts`; drops and key moves are announced politely. |

## Events and methods

| rowDragging handler | When |
| --- | --- |
| `onDragStart` | A row is about to be dragged (pointer or keys); `cancel` keeps it in place. |
| `onDragMove` | The row moved under the pointer; `cancel` takes no drop there. |
| `onDragChange` | The place it would land changed (another index, another grid, onto a row); `cancel` takes no drop there. |
| `onDragEnd` | The row is about to be dropped (`toIndex` -1 when it is over no grid that takes it); `cancel` drops nothing. |
| `onReorder` | Dropped elsewhere in this grid: move it in the data. `promise`: the grid waits for it, the marks shown. |
| `onRemove / onAdd` | Dropped on another grid of the group: `onRemove` on the grid it left, `onAdd` on the one it went to. |

| Field of the event | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `component, fromComponent, toComponent` | The grid raising it, the grid the row comes from, the grid under the pointer (the same while reordering, `null` over none). |
| `itemData, itemKey, itemElement` | The row dragged, its key, its element. |
| `fromIndex, toIndex` | The grid’s row indexes (as `focusedRowIndex` and `getVisibleRows()` count them, across pages too): where the row is, and where it would be after the drop. |
| `toItemData` | The row at `toIndex` before the drop — splice the row in where it is; `undefined` at the end of the other grid or on a group row. |
| `dropInsideItem, fromData, toData, event` | Dropped onto the row at `toIndex`; the grids’ `rowDragging.data`; the pointer or key event. |
| `cancel / promise` | The four drag events can be cancelled; the three drop events take a promise. |

| Member | Gets or returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rowDragging` | read/write, live | `grid.rowDragging.allowReordering = true`, handlers too; `onOptionChanged` tells `rowDragging.allowReordering`. |
| `moveRow(fromIndex, toIndex)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Moves a row as a drop there would: `onDragStart`, `onDragChange`, `onDragEnd` (any can cancel), then `onReorder`; whether it was raised. |

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Up / Ctrl+Shift+Down on a row (`moveUpKeys`, `moveDownKeys`)` | Moves the active row a place up or down (`allowReordering`); the row stays the active one, and the move is announced (“Row moved to position 3 of 20”). |
| `Escape while dragging` | Cancels the drag; nothing is dropped. |

## Example files

`RowReorder.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

/** Rows in memory reordered by dragging (or Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down): `onReorder` moves the row in the array. */
export default function RowReorder() {
  const s = reactive({ rows: makeTasks(500), push: true, icons: true });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="The rows make room (push)" x-model={() => s.push} />
        <CheckBox label="Drag icons (off: drag the whole row)" x-model={() => s.icons} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-reorder"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={() => s.rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={taskColumns}
        label="Tasks to reorder"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{
          allowReordering: true,
          dropFeedbackMode: () => (s.push ? 'push' : 'indicate'),
          showDragIcons: () => s.icons,
          onReorder: (e) => {
            // The grid does not move the data: take the row out and put it where the row at `toIndex` is.
            const from = s.rows.indexOf(e.itemData);
            const to = s.rows.indexOf(e.toItemData as Task);
            s.rows.splice(from, 1);
            s.rows.splice(to, 0, e.itemData);
            e.component.refresh();
          },
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

`tasks.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';

const TITLES = ['Write the release notes', 'Fix the login page', 'Review the pull request', 'Plan the sprint', 'Update the docs', 'Call the customer', 'Test on mobile', 'Clean up the backlog'];
const OWNERS = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger'];
const PRIORITIES = ['Low', 'Normal', 'High'];

/** `n` made-up tasks from id `from`, in their order. */
export function makeTasks(n: number, from = 1): Task[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: from + i,
    title: `${TITLES[(from + i) % TITLES.length]} #${from + i}`,
    owner: OWNERS[(from + i) % OWNERS.length],
    priority: PRIORITIES[(from + i) % PRIORITIES.length],
    order: i,
  }));
}

export const taskColumns: GridColumn<Task>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 70 },
  { field: 'title', title: 'Task', width: 240, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'owner', title: 'Owner', width: 110 },
  { field: 'priority', title: 'Priority', width: 100 },
];
```

`task.ts`

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {

  title: string;
```

`RowReorderServer.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

const tasks = makeTasks(10_000);
const server = new SlowAdapter<Task, number>({ data: tasks, key: 'id' }, 200);
const source = new data.DataSource<Task, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });

/** What the server does when a task moves to place `order`: the tasks in between move one place. */
async function moveTask(id: number, order: number) {
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 200));
  const task = tasks.find((t) => t.id === id)!;
  const from = task.order;
  for (const t of tasks) {
    if (from < order && t.order > from && t.order <= order) t.order--;
    else if (from > order && t.order >= order && t.order < from) t.order++;
  }
  task.order = order;
}

/** 10,000 tasks on a server, in the order of their `order` field: a drop tells the server and loads again. */
export default function RowReorderServer() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-reorder-server"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        dataSource={source}
        columns={[...taskColumns, { field: 'order', title: 'Order', type: 'number', width: 90 }]}
        sort={[{ field: 'order', dir: 'asc' }]}
        label="Tasks on a server"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{
          allowReordering: true,
          onReorder: (e) => {
            // The row at `toIndex` gives the place; the grid waits for the promise, the line shown.
            const order = (e.toItemData as Task).order;
            e.promise = moveTask(e.itemData.id, order).then(() => {
              s.saved = `Task ${e.itemData.id} moved to order ${order}`;
              return e.component.refresh();
            });
          },
        }}
      />
      <output class="dg-reorder-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`RowDragBetween.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { GridRowDropEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

/** Two grids of one `group`: a row dropped on the other grid leaves this one (`onRemove`) and goes there (`onAdd`). */
export default function RowDragBetween() {
  const s = reactive({ todo: makeTasks(12), done: makeTasks(4, 101) });
  const columns = taskColumns.filter((c) => c.field !== 'priority');
  const grid = (list: 'todo' | 'done', label: string) => {
    const rows = () => s[list];
    const add = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      const at = e.toItemData ? rows().indexOf(e.toItemData) : rows().length;
      rows().splice(at, 0, e.itemData);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    // The grids read the arrays as they are: each loads its own again after the change.
    const remove = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      rows().splice(rows().indexOf(e.itemData), 1);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    const reorder = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      const from = rows().indexOf(e.itemData);
      const to = rows().indexOf(e.toItemData as Task);
      rows().splice(from, 1);
      rows().splice(to, 0, e.itemData);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    return (
      <DataGrid
        class={`dg-board dg-board-${list}`}
        style="block-size: 28rem; flex: 1 1 18rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label={label}
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{ group: 'board', allowReordering: true, dropFeedbackMode: 'push', onAdd: add, onRemove: remove, onReorder: reorder }}
      />
    );
  };
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start">
      {grid('todo', 'To do')}
      {grid('done', 'Done')}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```
