# DataGrid: Selecting by dragging

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Rows

With `selection: 'multiple'`, press on a row and drag over others: the rows between are selected as the pointer goes, with a frame around them while the drag runs. A plain drag replaces the selection, Ctrl (⌘ on Apple) adds the rows to it, Shift goes from the anchor. Over the check boxes the rows passed take the state the first one takes. Near the top or bottom edge the rows scroll, here over 300 rows; grouped, the group rows are passed over. `onSelectionChanged` comes once per row reached, with `e.byDrag`.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Cell ranges

`cellSelection` draws rectangles of cells as in a spreadsheet: press on a cell and drag, Ctrl/⌘ starts another range (`'multiple'`), Shift+click extends the last one from its anchor, a plain click starts over; Shift and the arrows do the same from the keyboard. Ctrl+C copies the ranges as tab-separated text, Ctrl+V pastes into them (one value fills them all), Delete empties them through the normal edit path, and the bar sums the numbers up. The Note column opts out until it is let in.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Over 100,000 rows

Ranges are marks on the cells drawn now: the pooled rows and, with virtual columns, the columns in view. Drawing one over 100,000 rows × 60 columns keeps the frame rate, and a change of a range writes only the marks that changed, never a cell's text. The buttons set ranges by key from code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumnItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

type Reading = { id: number };

const SENSORS = 60;

const columns: GridColumnItem<Reading>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'Hour', type: 'number', width: 90, sticky: 'start' },
  ...Array.from({ length: SENSORS }, (_, n) => ({ field: `s${n}`, title: `S${n + 1}`, type: 'number' as const, width: 90, value: (r: Reading) => ((r.id * (n + 7)) % 1000) / 10 })),
];

const rows: Reading[] = Array.from({ length: 100_000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1 }));

/** 100,000 rows × 60 virtual columns: a range is drawn over pooled rows, only the drawn cells carry its marks. */
export default function CellRangesVirtual() {
  const s = reactive({ told: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Reading> | null = null;
  const show = () => {
    const sum = grid?.cellSelectionSummary;
    s.told = sum ? `${sum.cells.toLocaleString('en')} cells, sum ${sum.sum.toLocaleString('en')}` : '';
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Hours 10–20, S1–S5" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.selectCells({ key: 10, field: 's0' }, { key: 20, field: 's4' }) && show()} />
        <Button text="Add hour 50, S10–S12" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.selectCells({ key: 50, field: 's9' }, { key: 50, field: 's11' }, true) && show()} />
        <Button text="Clear" size="sm" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearCellSelection()} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-range-virtual"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sensor readings as a sheet"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ cellSelection: 'multiple', columnRenderingMode: 'virtual' }}
        onCellSelectionChanged={show}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Reading>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-range-virtual-state">{() => s.told}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Options

| settings | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rowDragSelection` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | With `selection: 'multiple'`, pressing on a row and dragging selects the rows passed. |
| `cellSelection` | `Bind<'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'>` | `'none'` | Rectangles of cells: one at a time, or more with Ctrl/⌘. While it is on, clicks on the cells draw ranges and rows are selected from the check box column. |
| `cellDragSelection` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Ranges are drawn by dragging; off, Shift+click and the keys still draw them. |
| `cellSelectable (column too)` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The column’s cells can be in a range; the column’s own value wins. A range leaves such a column out and a press there draws none. |
| `dragSelectionThreshold` | `Bind<number>` | `5` | Pixels the pointer moves after a press before a drag starts; less is a click (it selects, or starts editing with `startEditAction: 'click'`). |
| `dragSelectionAutoScroll, dragSelectionScrollSpeed, dragSelectionScrollSensitivity` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<number>`, `Bind<number>` | `true`, `30`, `60` | The rows scroll while the pointer is near or past an edge, down and (for ranges) sideways: pixels a frame at the edge, and how near it starts. |
| `dragSelectionTouch, dragSelectionLongPress` | `Bind<'scroll' \| 'longPress'>`, `Bind<number>` | `'scroll'`, `500` | On a touch screen a drag scrolls, or a press held that many milliseconds starts a drag selection. |
| `dragSelectionOnEditableCells` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A drag may start on a cell the user can edit; off, presses there are clicks only. |
| `selectAllCellsKeys, clearCellSelectionKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Mod+A']`, `['Escape']` | Keys that select every cell and clear the ranges (any chord: `Ctrl+Shift+A`…). |
| `extendCellsKeys` | `Bind<GridCellExtendKeys>` | `{ up: ['Shift+ArrowUp'], down, left, right, pageUp, pageDown, home, end` with Shift; `top, bottom, leftmost, rightmost` with `Mod+Shift+Arrow…`; `first: ['Mod+Shift+Home'], last: ['Mod+Shift+End'] }` | The keys that move the last range’s far corner, by where it goes: a cell, a screen of rows, the row’s first or last cell, the first or last row, the leftmost or rightmost cell, the very first or last cell. Each is a list of chords; assign a new object to change some. |
| `toggleRowSelectionKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Shift+Space']` | Keys that select or deselect the active row (Space alone still does on the check box column and on cells that cannot be edited). |
| `extendRowSelectionKeys` | `Bind<GridRowExtendKeys>` | `{ up: ['Shift+ArrowUp'], down: ['Shift+ArrowDown'], pageUp: ['Shift+PageUp'], pageDown: ['Shift+PageDown'] }` | Multiple selection: keys that move the active row and extend the selection from the anchor (while cells are selected: from the check box column). |
| `cellSummary, cellSummaryItems` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<('count' \| 'sum' \| 'average' \| 'min' \| 'max')[]>` | `true`, `['average', 'count', 'sum']` | The summary of the selected cells in the bottom bar, while more than one cell is selected. |

| What changes | What happens to the ranges |
| --- | --- |
| `Sorting, filtering, searching, grouping` | The rows between the corners would be other rows: the ranges go (without asking `onCellSelectionChanging`). Opening or closing a group does the same. |
| `Paging` | A range belongs to the page it was drawn on: another page takes it away. Shift+PageUp / PageDown extend within the page. |
| `Rows added, loaded again, edited` | Corners keep their row by key (a new row by its id): a range follows its rows when new rows open above them, the data reloads or a value changes. A row that was loading when the corner was set is the row at that place once it comes. |
| `Columns` | A range keeps its columns by field: moved, they stay selected where they go; hidden (by the user or the width), they are left out until they show again. Pinned columns, band headers and virtual columns work as any; a column with `cellSelectable: false` breaks the frame. |
| `Virtual and infinite rows` | Ranges and runs are drawn on the pooled rows only, cell by cell, and never draw a cell’s text again. Rows that load while the rows scroll under a drag are taken in as they come; copying needs every row of the ranges loaded (else: use Export). |
| `Group rows, details` | Group rows, group footers, details and adaptive details are never selected. Dragging over a group row selects the rows shown on each side of it; the rows of a closed group stay as they are. |
| `Selected rows and ranges` | Both can be on: over a selected row a range is drawn whole, with its own text color, so the text keeps its contrast. |

| Next to | How they share the pointer |
| --- | --- |
| `Row drag and drop` | The drag icon (or `handle`) moves the row; without icons the whole row moves it and rows are not selected by dragging. |
| `Editors and clicks` | The threshold separates a click from a drag: a click selects, opens a cell with `startEditAction: 'click'`, a double click edits. The click after a drag is swallowed. |
| `Headers, filter row, group panel, totals` | Presses there are theirs: sort, resize, move, filter, group. |
| `Buttons, links, fields, toggles` | Presses on the action buttons, the master-detail and “…” toggles, links, buttons and fields inside cells are theirs. |
| `Text` | While a drag selects, the browser selects no text. Alt+drag is left to the browser, to select text in the cells. |

## Events and methods

| Member | Gets or returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cellRanges` | `GridCellRange[]`, read/write, reactive | `{ from, to, fields }`: the cell the range started on, its far corner (`{ field, key, rowIndex }`) and its columns. Assign by key or grid index; `[]` clears. |
| `selectCells(from, to?, add?)` | `boolean` | A range from cell to cell (one cell without `to`), alone or after the others (`add`, with `'multiple'`); whether it shows. |
| `clearCellSelection()` | `void` | No range. |
| `getSelectedCellValues()` | `GridCellValue<T>[]` | The selected cells of the loaded rows, each once, row by row: `{ rowIndex, key, field, value, row }` (unsaved edits included). |
| `cellSelectionSummary` | `GridCellSummary`, reactive | `{ cells, count, numbers, sum, average, min, max }`, as a spreadsheet’s status bar. |
| `onCellSelectionChanging` | `{ ranges, previous, byDrag, cancel }` | Before every change, by the user or code; `cancel` keeps the ranges (while drawing: the last step). |
| `onCellSelectionChanged` | `{ ranges, byDrag }` | After every change: once per cell the pointer reaches while drawing. |
| `onSelectionChanging / onSelectionChanged` | `{ …, byDrag }` | The row selection’s events, once per row a drag reaches; `byDrag` tells it apart. |
| `onCopying` | `{ text, html, rows, ranges, cancel }` | Before a copy; `ranges` are the ranges copied. |

## Keyboard and screen readers

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Shift+Arrows, Shift+Home / End, Shift+PageUp / PageDown (`extendCellsKeys`)` | Extend the last range from its far corner (no range: from the active cell); focus moves with the corner. Ctrl+Shift (⌘+Shift) with the arrows and Home / End go to the edge. |
| `Ctrl+A (`selectAllCellsKeys`)` | Every cell of the rows the user can reach. |
| `Escape (`clearCellSelectionKeys`)` | Clears the ranges; while drawing, gives the drag up (rows: the selection before it comes back). |
| `Arrows, Home, End, PageUp / PageDown` | Move the active cell and clear the ranges, as in a spreadsheet. |
| `Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Delete` | Copy the ranges; paste into them (one value fills them all, a block starts at the first cell); empty their cells the user can edit, saved as the save mode says. |
| `Shift+Space (`toggleRowSelectionKeys`), Shift+Up / Down and PageUp / PageDown (`extendRowSelectionKeys`)` | Select rows, as before; while cells are selected, from the check box column. |

With `cellSelection` on, the grid is `aria-multiselectable` and every selectable cell carries `aria-selected`. What a drag or a key selected is said politely: “4 rows selected”, “3 × 5 cells selected”, “12 cells selected in 2 ranges” (`gridRowsSelected`, `gridCellsSelected`, `gridCellRangesSelected`, in English and Turkish).

## Tokens

| Token | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `datagrid.range-fill, range-fill-opacity` | The fill of the cells of a range, laid over the row’s own look at that opacity; whole over a selected row. |
| `datagrid.cell (`range-selected`, `range-anchor`)` | The text of a range over a selected row, and of the anchor cell. |
| `datagrid.range-border-color, range-border-width` | The frame around a range. |
| `datagrid.range-anchor-fill` | The cell the last range started on (the language’s surface). |
| `datagrid.row-run-border-color, row-run-border-width` | The frame around the rows a drag selects, while it runs. |

## Example files

`DragSelectRows.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridSelectionChangedEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Rows selected by dragging over them: live, with Ctrl to add, Shift from the anchor, over the check boxes too. */
export default function DragSelectRows() {
  const s = reactive({ drag: true, scroll: true, grouped: false, last: '' });
  const told = (e: GridSelectionChangedEventArgs) => (s.last = `${e.selection.keys.length} keys${e.byDrag ? ', by dragging' : ''}`);

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Select rows by dragging" x-model={() => s.drag} />
        <CheckBox label="Scroll near the edges" x-model={() => s.scroll} />
        <CheckBox label="Group by city" x-model={() => s.grouped} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-drag-rows"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(300)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: () => (s.grouped ? 0 : undefined) } : c))}
        label="Orders to select by dragging"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: 'multiple', rowDragSelection: () => s.drag, dragSelectionAutoScroll: () => s.scroll }}
        onSelectionChanged={told}
      />
      <output class="dg-drag-rows-state">{() => s.last}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },

  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`CellRanges.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridCellSelectionChangedEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const MODES = ['none', 'single', 'multiple'] as const;

/** Ranges of cells as in a spreadsheet: drawn, extended, copied, filled and emptied; the bar sums them up. */
export default function CellRanges() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'multiple' as (typeof MODES)[number], drag: true, summary: true, touch: false, note: false, last: '' });
  const told = (e: GridCellSelectionChangedEventArgs) =>
    (s.last = e.ranges.map((r) => `${r.from.key ?? r.from.rowIndex}.${r.from.field} → ${r.to.key ?? r.to.rowIndex}.${r.to.field}`).join(', ') + (e.byDrag ? ' (drawing)' : ''));

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Cell selection">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Draw by dragging" x-model={() => s.drag} />
        <CheckBox label="Summary in the bar" x-model={() => s.summary} />
        <CheckBox label="Long press on touch" x-model={() => s.touch} />
        <CheckBox label="Note can be selected" x-model={() => s.note} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-cell-ranges"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'note' ? { ...c, cellSelectable: () => s.note } : c))}
        label="Orders as a sheet"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          editable: true,
          cellSelection: () => s.mode,
          cellDragSelection: () => s.drag,
          cellSummary: () => s.summary,
          dragSelectionTouch: () => (s.touch ? 'longPress' : 'scroll'),
        }}
        onCellSelectionChanged={told}
      />
      <output class="dg-cell-ranges-state">{() => s.last}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Scrolling

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Scrolling modes

The `mode` prop picks how the rows are reached. Every mode draws only the rows in view from a small pool of rows, so the page never holds one element per row.

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `'virtual' (default)` | One long list: the scroll bar is as long as every row, blocks load where the view is (a source with `loadMode: 'blocks'`), the rows between are never asked for. |
| `'paged'` | Pages with a pager; a source that loads by page is always paged. |
| `'infinite'` | The rows show part by part, `pageSize` each; the next part loads as the view nears the end and the scroll bar grows with the rows that came. No total is needed. Rows in memory, groups and summaries are shown part by part the same way. |

## Infinite scrolling

With `mode: 'infinite'` the grid shows 50 orders, and as the last of them comes into view it asks the server for the next 50, with “Loading more rows…” over the bottom while they come. This server cannot count (`count: false`): the grid finds the end when a part comes back short. Turn on “The next part fails” and scroll down: the mark offers Retry. Sort, filter or search: it starts again from the first part.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `Bind<'virtual' \| 'paged' \| 'infinite'>` | `'virtual'` | How the rows are shown; another mode starts the data again. |
| `pageSize` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | Rows of a part for rows in memory (0: every row at once). A source that loads by blocks uses its own block size. |
| `settings.loadMoreDistance` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | Rows left below the view when the next part starts to load; 0 waits for the last row to come into view. |
| `settings.preloadEnabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The next part loads one part earlier (in virtual mode: a part on each side of the view), so scrolling seldom waits. |
| `settings.loadMoreIndicator` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The “Loading more rows…” mark over the last rows while a part loads, with Retry when it failed. |
| `DataSource count` | `boolean` | `true` | Off, no part asks the server for a total: a part shorter than the block size ends the rows (an empty one after a full one too). |

| Member | Gets or returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onMoreRowsLoading` | `{ skip, take, cancel }` | The next part is about to load (the view near the end, `loadMore()`, Ctrl+End); `cancel` keeps the rows as they are. |
| `onMoreRowsLoaded` | `{ skip, count, ended }` | A part came: `count` rows from `skip`; `ended` once every row shows. |
| `loadMore()` | `boolean` | Loads the next part, after `onMoreRowsLoading`; `false` while the rows load, a part is loading or failed, or every row shows. |
| `loadingMore, endReached` | `boolean`, reactive | A part is loading; every row shows (always outside infinite mode). |
| `retry()` | — | Loads a part that failed again (the mark’s Retry does the same). |
| `pageIndex(), pageIndex(n), page` | `number` | The last part shown; with a number, loads the parts up to that one and scrolls to its first row. |
| `pageCount` | `number`, reactive | The parts of every row once their count is known, else the parts shown. |
| `total, totalCount()` | `number` | `total`: the rows shown so far. `totalCount()`: every matching row once known (counted, or the last part came), −1 until then. |
| `refresh()` | — | Loads the rows shown again, keeping the position. |

| Topic | How infinite mode does it |
| --- | --- |
| `The end` | With a count the end is known from the first part; without one (`count: false`) a part that comes back short is the last one. Scrolling at the end asks for nothing more. |
| `Failing parts` | A part that fails shows Retry in the mark (in the bottom bar with `loadMoreIndicator` off); scrolling does not ask for it again until Retry. The rows shown stay; the first part failing shows the grid’s own error. |
| `Sort, filter, search` | Start again from the first part, at the top. |
| `Grouping` | Group rows and rows show part by part together. Groups from a server load only the rows of the part shown; in memory every row is already there. |
| `Selection, export` | “Select all” and Ctrl+A select every matching row, loaded or not; the export writes every row, the parts not loaded too. |
| `Editing, details` | The row in edit, the focused row, its details and the selection stay as parts come; new rows open after the rows shown. |
| `Pager` | Hidden: the rows are reached by scrolling. |
| `Assistive technology` | `aria-rowcount` is −1 until the last part came; each row keeps its `aria-rowindex`. |

## Rows in memory, grouped

Rows in memory are shown part by part too, here 100 places at a time grouped by city: group rows and rows count alike, so the next city's group shows once its part does. Details, selection and the group summaries work as in the other modes.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Virtual columns

With `settings.columnRenderingMode: 'virtual'` (`columnRenderingMode`) only the scrolling columns in view, and `extraColumns` on each side, get cells; the others keep their place in the layout and get cells as they come into view. Here 100,000 hours of 200 sensors, in bands of 20, with the hour and the sum pinned. Turn “Virtual columns” off to see the same grid with every column drawn.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, NumberBox, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { GridColumnItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

type Reading = { id: number };

const SENSORS = 200;

/** 200 sensors in bands of 20, each reading worked out from the row: no row holds 200 values. */
const columns: GridColumnItem<Reading>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'Hour', type: 'number', width: 90, sticky: 'start' },
  ...Array.from({ length: SENSORS / 20 }, (_, b) => ({
    title: `Sensors ${b * 20 + 1}–${b * 20 + 20}`,
    columns: Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, k) => {
      const n = b * 20 + k;
      return { field: `s${n}`, title: `S${n + 1}`, type: 'number' as const, width: 90, value: (r: Reading) => ((r.id * (n + 7)) % 1000) / 10 };
    }),
  })),
  { field: 'total', title: 'Sum', type: 'number', width: 100, sticky: 'end', value: (r: Reading) => (r.id * 31) % 100_000 },
];

const rows: Reading[] = Array.from({ length: 100_000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1 }));

/** 100,000 rows × 200 columns: only the columns in view (and two on each side) get cells. */
export default function VirtualColumns() {
  const s = reactive({ virtual: true, extra: 2 });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Virtual columns" x-model={() => s.virtual} />
        <NumberBox label="Extra columns" labelMode="side" min={0} max={20} x-model={() => s.extra} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-columns"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sensor readings"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ columnRenderingMode: () => (s.virtual ? 'virtual' : 'standard'), extraColumns: () => s.extra ?? 0, filterRow: true }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.columnRenderingMode` | `Bind<'standard' \| 'virtual'>` | `'standard'` | `'virtual'`: only the scrolling columns in view and `extraColumns` on each side get cells; pinned columns always do. |
| `column.columnRenderingMode` | `Bind<'standard' \| 'virtual'>` | the grid’s | One column’s own: `'standard'` keeps its cells while it is out of view (a cell content with a state of its own), `'virtual'` lets only it go. |
| `settings.extraColumns` | `Bind<number>` | `2` | Columns drawn beyond the ones in view on each side, so a quick sideways scroll shows no gap. |
| `settings.renderAsync` | `Bind<boolean \| 'auto'>` | `'auto'` | The columns coming into view are drawn as the rows scroll (`false`), once the scrolling stops (`true`), or once it stops while drawing them takes longer than the threshold. |
| `settings.columnRenderingThreshold` | `Bind<number>` | `300` | Milliseconds drawing the new columns may take before they wait for the scrolling to stop (`renderAsync: 'auto'`). |
| `settings.columnRenderingDelay` | `Bind<number>` | `300` | Milliseconds without sideways scrolling before the columns that waited are drawn. |

| Topic | How virtual columns do it |
| --- | --- |
| `Rows of every kind` | The header, the filter row, the rows, the group rows’ items under their columns, the group footers and the totals all follow; the row in edit keeps its editor’s column. |
| `Pinned columns and bands` | Pinned columns are always drawn. A band header spans only its columns drawn and goes with the last of them; its `aria-colindex` and `aria-colspan` stay those of all its columns. |
| `Keyboard` | The active column is always drawn: Tab, the arrow keys, Home and End move into a column without cells, which gets them and scrolls into view. |
| `Layout` | Resizing, moving (dragging a header past columns without cells too), pinning and hiding work as before; “Fit all columns” draws every column while it measures them. |
| `Assistive technology` | Cells keep their `aria-colindex` and the grid its `aria-colcount`, so a screen reader still names column 120 of 202. |
| `Export, copy` | CSV, Excel and PDF write every column, the ones without cells too; copying reads the values, not the cells. |
| `Events` | `onCellPrepared` and `onRowPrepared` run as cells are made, so again after a sideways scroll. |

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+End` | Infinite: the last row shown, and the next part loads. |
| `Down, Page Down on the last rows` | Infinite: the view nears the end and the next part loads. |
| `Home, End, Tab, Left / Right` | Virtual columns: into a column without cells; it is drawn and scrolled into view. |

## Example files

`InfiniteScroll.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** A server that cannot count, and fails on purpose while `failing` is on. */
class OrderServer extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  failing = false;

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<Order>> {
    const result = await super.load(options);
    if (this.failing && (options.skip ?? 0) > 0) throw new Error('The server did not answer.');
    return result;
  }
}

/** 1,030 orders from a slow server without a count, loaded 50 at a time as the list nears its end. */
export default function InfiniteScroll() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0, parts: 0, preload: false, failing: false });
  // Stands in for a server: new data.RestAdapter({ url: '/api/orders', key: 'id' }) goes in its place.
  const server = new OrderServer({ data: makeOrders(1_030), key: 'id', capabilities: { count: false } }, 600);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  // `count: false`: no part asks for a total; a part shorter than 50 rows is the last one.
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 50, count: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Load a part ahead" x-model={() => s.preload} />
        <CheckBox label="The next part fails" x-model={() => s.failing} onValueChanged={(e) => (server.failing = !!e.value)} />
        <Button text="Load more" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.loadMore()} />
        <Button text="To the last row" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(grid.total - 1, 'end')} />
        <output class="dg-infinite-state">{() => `${s.loads} loads, ${s.parts} parts came${grid?.endReached ? ', every row is here' : ''}`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-infinite"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        mode="infinite"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders, part by part"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ preloadEnabled: () => s.preload, selection: 'multiple', filterRow: true }}
        onMoreRowsLoaded={() => s.parts++}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

```tsx
import { DataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 2,000 orders in memory, grouped by city: the group rows and the rows show 100 places at a time. */
export default function InfiniteGroups() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-infinite-groups"
      style="block-size: 28rem"
      mode="infinite"
      pageSize={100}
      rows={makeOrders(2_000)}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0 } : c))}
      label="Orders by city, part by part"
      locale="en"
      settings={{ groupPanel: true, selection: 'multiple' }}
      summary={{ groupItems: [{ column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: true }] }}
      masterDetail={{ enabled: true, template: (ctx) => <p class="dg-infinite-detail">{() => `${(ctx.row as Order).customer} · ${(ctx.row as Order).note || 'no note'}`}</p> }}
    />
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Layout and events

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.2

## Toolbar

The bar above the rows holds the grid's own items whose features are on, at the end, in this order: “New row” (`addRows`, `newRowButton`), “Save changes” and “Discard” (batch mode, `saveButtons`), “Export” (`exportButton`), the column list (`columnChooserButton`) and the search box (`searchPanel`); with none of them it does not show. `toolbar.items` lists exactly what it holds: the grid's items by name, an object with a `name` to change one of them, and items of your own — a button with `text`, `icon`, `hint` and `click`, or any component with `content` — at the start (`location: 'before'`) or at the end. Buttons that do not fit go into its “more” menu (`overflow`); the grid's own show only their icons there (`showText`), and their texts in the menu.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Item field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | One of the grid’s items (`groupPanel`, `rowActions`, `searchPanel`, `addRowButton`, `saveButton`, `revertButton`, `exportButton`, `columnChooserButton`) to change, or a name of your own. A grid item whose feature is off stays out. |
| `location` | `'before'` or `'after'` (default; the group panel and `rowActions` `'before'`): which end of the bar. |
| `text, icon, hint` | The button’s text, icon and tooltip (default: the text when only the icon shows). |
| `showText` | `'always'` (default) or `'inMenu'`: only the icon in the bar, the text in the “more” menu (the grid’s own buttons). |
| `visible, enabled` | Leave the item out; dim it. |
| `overflow` | `'never'` (default; the grid’s buttons `'auto'`), `'auto'` or `'always'`: whether it may go into the “more” menu. |
| `content` | `() => component`: your own component in place of a button, made once. |
| `click` | `(e) => void` with `{ item, grid, event }`; on a grid item it replaces what the item does. |

## Columns at run time

`addColumn(column, index?)` adds a column at a place among the data columns, with its own width, visibility and sticky side (or what the kept layout says of it); `deleteColumn(field)` takes one out, and its sort, grouping and filter go with it. `columnOption(field, name, value)` changes one option of a column while it shows — its layout (`width`, `visible`, `sticky`, `visibleIndex`), sort, grouping, header filter values, a feature switch, or any field of its definition (`title`, `format`, `lookup`, `cell`, `type` …), the column drawn again with it — and `columnOption(field, { … })` several at once. The layout, `layoutKey` and `onLayoutChange` follow; `onOptionChanged` tells each change (`name: 'columns'` for a column added or taken out). `columnCount()` and `getVisibleColumns()` read them.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Keeping the layout

With `layoutKey` the grid keeps the column widths, order, hidden and pinned columns, the sort, the filters and the search text in the browser's `localStorage`, and a grid made again with the same name — after a reload too — gets them back. Storage that is full or blocked is skipped quietly. `resetLayout()` (also in the column menu) goes back to the column definitions. To keep the layout elsewhere, a server for instance, read `layout` and `filters`, listen to `onLayoutChange`, and give them back through the props of the same names.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Turning features off

Every feature has a switch in `settings`, each a value or a function; a column can turn one on or off for itself, and its value wins. `grid.settings` and `grid.columnSettings(field)` change them while the grid shows.

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editable` | `false` | Edit cells in place. A column can decide itself, also per row with `(row) => boolean`. |
| `creatable` | `true` | Fill the cells of new rows. A column with its own `editable` and no `creatable` uses the same; `editable: false, creatable: true` is entered only when the row is created. |
| `addRows, newRowButton, tabChain` | `false`, `true`, `true` | The user adds rows; the toolbar’s “New row” button; Tab on a new row’s last cell opens the next one. |
| `enterMoves` | `'none'` | Enter in an editor keeps the value and stays, goes `down`, or goes on like Tab (`next`). |
| `rowStatus` | `true` | The narrow column that marks new, changed, deleted, saving and failed rows. |
| `saveButtons, errorSummary` | `true` | “Save changes” and “Discard” in the toolbar in batch mode (dimmed while there is nothing to save); “N rows with errors” and “Next error” in the bar under the rows. |
| `sortable, multiSort` | `true` | Sort from the header; Shift adds a column to the sort. |
| `resizable, movable, hideable, pinnable, menu` | `true` | What the user may do with the columns; a column can say otherwise for itself. |
| `resizeMode` | `'widget'` | Dragging a column edge: `widget` changes that column and the columns after it shift; `nextColumn` moves only the edge between it and the next column, which gives or takes the difference. A column can set its own. |
| `headerButtons` | `'hover'` | The menu button shows on hover and focus (always on touch screens), or `always`. |
| `columnChooser, layoutReset` | `true` | The column list and “Reset layout” in the column menu. |
| `columnChooserButton` | `false` | A toolbar button that opens the column list (while `columnChooser` is on). |
| `tooltips, striped, rowCount` | `true`, `false`, `true` | Full text of a clipped cell; stripes; the row count. |
| `pager` | `true` | The pager in paged mode; `auto` only while there is more than one page. |
| `actionsColumn, actionsPosition, actionsSticky, actionsWidth` | `true`, `'end'`, `true`, `140` | The actions column, at the start or the end, pinned to its edge or scrolling with the rows, and its width. |
| `actionsLocation, actionsTarget, actionsDisplay` | `'row'`, `'auto'`, `'auto'` | Where the actions show (the row, the toolbar, the bottom bar), which rows the bars act on, and buttons or a menu only: see [Row actions](datagrid-editing.md#actions). |
| `actionsMultipleEnabled, actionsShowCount, actionsStopOnError` | `'all'`, `true`, `false` | Actions on several rows: enabled for all or any, the count after the text, a failed row stops the rest. |
| `actionsProgress, actionsStopButton, actionsContextMenu` | `true`, `true`, `true` | The progress panel and its Stop button while an action works on several rows; the actions in the row’s context menu. |
| `selection, selectionColumn, selectAll, selectedCount` | `'none'`, `true`, `true`, `true` | `single` or `multiple`; the check box column; the header check box and Ctrl+A; “N selected” in the bar. |
| `filterRow, headerFilter` | `false` | The filter row and the header filter; a column can turn them on or off for itself. |
| `syncLookupFilterValues` | `true` | A lookup column’s filter row and header filter list only the keys of the rows the other filters leave; off, they list the lookup source. A column can say otherwise for itself. |
| `filterDelay` | `300` | Milliseconds from the last key typed in the filter row to the filter. |
| `copyable, exportable` | `true` | Columns that go into what Ctrl+C copies and into an export; a column can say otherwise for itself. |
| `copyValues, copyHeaders` | `'shown'`, `false` | Ctrl+C copies the text the cells show or their `raw` values; copied rows start with the column titles. |
| `paste, pasteNewRows` | `true`, `false` | Ctrl+V writes into the editable cells; pasted lines past the last row open new rows (with `addRows`). |
| `exportButton` | `false` | An “Export” button in the toolbar: the formats of the `export` prop (CSV by default), as a menu when it offers more than one command. |
| `saveLayout` | `true` | With `layoutKey`, the layout, the filters and the search text are kept and come back. |
| `searchPanel` | `false` | The search box in the toolbar. `searchText` and `searchByText()` search without it too. |
| `filterPanel, filterSyncEnabled` | `false`, `'auto'` | The filter panel under the rows, and the filter row and header filters kept in the filter value (`'auto'`: while the panel shows). See [Filter panel and builder](datagrid-filtering.md#filter-panel). |
| `searchPanelWidth, searchPlaceholder` | `160`, `uiLocale` “Search…” | The box’s width (pixels or a CSS length) and its placeholder. |
| `searchDelay` | `700` | Milliseconds from the last key typed in the search box to the search; Enter searches at once. |
| `highlightSearchText, highlightCaseSensitive` | `true`, `false` | Mark what the search found in the cells; mark only text in the same case (the search itself ignores case). |
| `searchVisibleColumnsOnly` | `false` | Search only the visible columns; by default hidden ones too. |
| `searchable` | `true` | The columns the search looks in; a column can say otherwise for itself (one that turns its own filters off is left out). |
| `groupPanel` | `false` | The group panel at the start of the toolbar: a chip per grouped column, and where headers are dropped to group by them. |
| `groupPanelDragging, groupPanelEmptyText` | `true`, `uiLocale` “Drag a column header here…” | Headers drag to the panel and chips back (off: the panel only shows the grouping); what the empty panel says. |
| `groupMenu` | unset | “Group by this column”, “Ungroup” and “Ungroup all” in the column menu. Left unset (grid and column), they show while the panel takes headers, as the keyboard’s way to do the same. |
| `groupable, showWhenGrouped` | `true`, `false` | The columns the user can group by; a grouped column still shows among the columns. A column can say otherwise for itself. |
| `autoExpandAll, allowCollapsing` | `true`, `true` | Groups start open (a column’s `autoExpandGroup` decides for its level); the user can open and close them (code always can; a column can say otherwise). |
| `groupExpandMode` | `'button'` | A group opens from its arrow and the keyboard, or with `rowClick` from a click anywhere on its row. A column can set its own. |
| `groupCount` | `true` | Group rows show their row count; a column can say otherwise for itself. |
| `groupToggleKeys, groupArrowKeys` | `['Enter', ' ']`, `true` | The keys that open and close a group row; Right and Left open, close and go in and out. |
| `remoteGrouping` | `'auto'` | Who groups a data source’s rows: `auto` its adapter when it groups (blocks), `true` the adapter whenever the source loads by blocks, `false` always the browser, from every matching row. |
| `groupLoadPageSize` | `0` | Grouping or summaries in the browser over a source that loads pages or blocks: rows per request while every matching row loads (0: one request). |
| `totalSummary, groupSummary` | `true` | The row of totals with the items of `summary.totalItems`; the items of `summary.groupItems` in group rows and footers. An item’s `visible` wins. |
| `totalSummaryTabStop` | `true` | The row of totals is a Tab stop of its own after the rows. |
| `remoteSummary` | `'auto'` | Who works out the summaries of a source that loads pages or blocks: `auto` its adapter when it has the `summary` capability, `true` the adapter always, `false` the browser, from every matching row. `custom` items and columns with a `value` reader are always worked out in the browser. |
| `dragThreshold` | `5` | Pixels a pressed header or chip moves before it is dragged. |
| `dragGhost` | `true` | A dragged header or chip shows its title next to the pointer, marked with what a drop would do: group, move, ungroup. While a header is dragged the whole toolbar takes drops for the group panel and is marked. |
| `emptyRows` | `3` | Rows of room the body keeps while it has no rows to show (empty, loading, failed), so the message shows in a grid without a height. |
| `columnWidth, columnMinWidth` | `140`, `48` | The width of a column that gives none, and the smallest width the user can resize one to; a column’s `width` and `minWidth` win. |
| `rowStatusWidth, selectionColumnWidth` | `28`, `36` | Widths of the row status column and the check box column. |
| `resizeStep, resizeFineStep` | `10`, `1` | Pixels one arrow key resizes a column by (“Width” in the column menu), and with Shift. |
| `tooltipDelay` | `500` | Milliseconds the pointer rests on a cell before its tooltip shows (keyboard focus shows it at once). |
| `extraRows` | `4` | Rows drawn above and below the visible ones, so a quick scroll shows no gap; more costs more per scroll. |
| `loadMoreDistance, preloadEnabled, loadMoreIndicator` | `0`, `false`, `true` | Infinite mode: rows left below the view when the next part loads; a part loaded ahead (in virtual mode a part on each side); the “Loading more rows…” mark with Retry. See [Infinite scrolling](datagrid-scrolling.md#infinite). |
| `columnRenderingMode, extraColumns` | `'standard'`, `2` | `virtual`: only the scrolling columns in view and `extraColumns` on each side get cells; a column’s own `columnRenderingMode` wins. See [Virtual columns](datagrid-scrolling.md#virtual-columns). |
| `renderAsync, columnRenderingThreshold, columnRenderingDelay` | `'auto'`, `300`, `300` | Virtual columns coming into view are drawn as the rows scroll, once the scrolling stops, or once it stops while drawing them took longer than the threshold (ms); the quiet time before they are drawn (ms). |
| `pagerNeighbors, pagerNavigation, pagerInfo` | `1`, `true`, `true` | Page buttons on each side of the current page; the first, previous, next and last buttons; “Page 3 of 12 (250 items)”. |
| `pagerInfoText, pagerLabel` | `uiLocale` texts | The pager’s text (`{0}` or `{page}`, `{1}` or `{count}`, `{2}` or `{total}`) and its accessible name. |
| `pagerDisplayMode` | `'adaptive'` | `full`: page buttons, and the page sizes as buttons; `compact`: a page number box and a drop-down of the sizes; `adaptive`: full while it fits in the bar. |
| `pageSizeSelector, allowedPageSizes` | `false`, `'auto'` | The page sizes in the pager; the sizes it offers (numbers and `all`; `auto` is half, once and twice the page size). |
| `pageKeys` | `'page'` | In paged mode PageUp and PageDown go to the previous and next page, or move a screen of rows (`rows`). |
| `headerFilterPageSize, headerFilterRows` | `100`, `8` | Values the header filter loads per request; the height of its list (or tree) in rows. |
| `headerFilterDateInterval` | `'day'` | The deepest part of the year → month → day tree a date column’s header filter lists; `null` lists every date. A column’s `headerFilterInterval` wins. |
| `exportPageSize` | `1000` | Rows an export asks a server for per request; `exportCsv({ pageSize })` wins. |
| `trueTexts, falseTexts` | `['true', '1', 'x', '✓', '✔']`, `['false', '0', '']` | Pasted texts read as yes and as no in a yes/no column, besides the `yes` and `no` texts; a column can give its own. |
| `editKeys, clearKeys` | `['Enter', 'F2']`, `['Delete']` | Keys that open the active cell’s editor, and that empty it (`KeyboardEvent.key` values). |
| `editOnKeyPress` | `true` | Typing a character on a cell opens its editor with it. A column can set its own. |
| `startEditAction` | `'dblClick'` | A double-click, or one `click` on the active cell, opens its editor. A column can set its own. |
| `columnHidingEnabled, bandAlign` | `false`, `'center'` | Columns hide while the grid is narrower than they are, and a “…” column opens their values; where band captions sit. See [Bands and adaptive columns](datagrid-bands.md#adaptive). |
| `editMode, confirmDelete, selectTextOnEditStart` | `'row'`, `true`, `true` | How rows are edited: in the cells (`row`, `cell`, `batch`) or in a form (`form`, `popup`); deleting asks first; an editor opens with its text selected. See [Edit forms and popups](datagrid-forms.md#forms). |

## Events

Every action of the user has an event, given as a prop or listened to with `grid.onX((e) => …)`; one that is about to happen (`…ing`) can be stopped with `e.cancel = true`, and most can change what happens (the values sent, the items of a menu, the text copied). Here amounts over 900 are drawn in bold, the rows get a menu of their own (right click, or Shift + F10), a change to “Cancelled” is not saved, and the list tells what happened. Methods do the same from code: `editCell`, `cellValue`, `navigateToRow`, `columnOption`, `state()` and the others in the [API reference](datagrid-api.md#api).

```tsx
/** An order, as the examples' made-up server keeps it. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Event | Gets | Cancel | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onCellClick / onCellDblClick` | `{ field, row, rowIndex, rowType, groupKey?, element, event }` | yes | A cell was clicked or double-clicked (also in a group footer, `rowType: 'groupFooter'`, and in the row of totals, `'totalFooter'`); cancel: no selection, no group toggle, no editor. |
| `onRowClick / onRowDblClick` | `{ row, rowIndex, rowType, groupKey?, element, event }` | yes | The same for the row, after its cell’s event. |
| `onCellPrepared` | `{ field, row, rowIndex, value, isNew, element }` |  | A cell was drawn for a row: style it. Cells are reused while scrolling, so set and clear what you change. Costs nothing while nobody listens. |
| `onRowPrepared` | `{ row, rowIndex, rowType, groupKey?, isSelected, element }` |  | A data row, group row, group footer (`groupFooter`) or the row of totals (`totalFooter`) was drawn; the same rule. |
| `onContentReady` | `{ total }` |  | Rows arrived and are laid out (after a load, a filter, a sort, a page, a resize). |
| `onDataErrorOccurred` | `{ error, operation, row? }` |  | A load (`operation: 'load'`) or the save of a row (`'save'`, with `row`) failed. |
| `onEditingStart` | `{ field, row, rowIndex, isNew }` | yes | A cell editor, or a row’s edit form (`field` `''`), is about to open. |
| `onEditorPreparing / onEditorPrepared` | `{ field, row, isNew, options }` / `{ field, row, isNew, editor, element, place }` | yes / — | An editor of a cell or of a form field is about to be made (change its props in `options`); it was made. |
| `onRowValidating` | `{ key, row, isNew, changed, errors, isValid, errorText }` | yes | A row is checked before it is saved, after its cells: add messages to `errors`, or `isValid = false` (or cancel) with `errorText`. |
| `onInitNewRow` | `{ data, values }` | yes | A new row is about to open: `data` is what it starts with, `values` what counts as entered; cancel opens no row. |
| `onSaving / onSaved` | `{ changes }` / `{ changes, saved, failed }` | yes / — | Changes are about to be sent (leaving a row, the background queue, “Save changes”); the answer came. |
| `onRowInserting / onRowInserted` | `{ row, data }` / `{ row, key }` | yes / — | Per new row: change `data` (what is sent) or keep it unsent; it was saved. |
| `onRowUpdating / onRowUpdated` | `{ key, row, changes }` / `{ key, row, changes }` | yes / — | Per changed row: change `changes` or keep them unsent; they were saved. |
| `onRowRemoving / onRowRemoved` | `{ key, row }` | yes / — | Per deleted row, when the deletion is sent (batch: on “Save changes”); it was deleted. |
| `onEditCanceling / onEditCanceled` | `{ rows }` | yes / — | Unsaved changes are about to be dropped: Escape on a row, the “Cancel” action, `discardChanges()`. |
| `onFocusedCellChanging / onFocusedCellChanged` | `{ rowIndex, field, previousRowIndex, previousField, row }` | yes / — | The active cell moves (keys, a click, code); -1 is the header, -2 the filter row. |
| `onFocusedRowChanging / onFocusedRowChanged` | `{ rowIndex, previousRowIndex, row }` / `{ rowIndex, row, key }` | yes / — | The active row changes. |
| `onKeyHandling` | `{ event, rowIndex, field }` | yes | A key went down in the rows, an editor, the filter row or a group chip, before the grid handles it; cancel and handle it yourself. the standard calls it `onKeyDown`, a DOM event name in JSX. |
| `onOptionChanged` | `{ name, field?, value, previous }` |  | A setting was assigned: `grid.settings`, `columnSettings(field)` (with `field`), `toolbar` (`toolbar.visible`, `toolbar.items`), `columnOption` (with `field`); a column was added or taken out (`name: 'columns'`, the fields). |
| `onSortChanging / onSortChanged` | `{ sort, previous, byUser }` | yes / — | The sort is about to change, by the user or from code. |
| `onFilterChanging / onFilterChanged` | `{ filters, previous }` / `{ filters, filter }` | yes / — | The filter row and header filters are about to apply; cancel puts the ones before back in the cells. |
| `onSearchTextChanging / onSearchTextChanged` | `{ text, previous }` / `{ text }` | yes / — | The search text is about to change; cancel keeps the one before in the box. |
| `onPageChanging / onPageChanged` | `{ page, previous }` | yes / — | Another page is about to show. |
| `onPageSizeChanging / onPageSizeChanged` | `{ pageSize, previous }` | yes / — | The rows per page are about to change (0: all); the grid goes back to the first page. |
| `onMoreRowsLoading / onMoreRowsLoaded` | `{ skip, take }` / `{ skip, count, ended }` | yes / — | Infinite mode: the next part of the rows is about to load; it came. |
| `onSelectionChanging / onSelectionChanged` | `{ selection, previous }` / `{ selection }` | yes / — | The selection is about to change, by the user or from code. |
| `onLayoutChanging / onLayoutChange` | `{ layout, previous }` / `layout` | yes / — | The user resized, moved, hid, pinned, sorted or reset; cancel puts the layout before back. |
| `onGroupingChanging / onGroupingChanged, onGroupDropping` | see [Grouping](datagrid-grouping.md#grouping) | yes | The grouping; a dropped header or chip. |
| `onRowExpanding / onRowExpanded, onRowCollapsing / onRowCollapsed` | `{ kind, key, row }` | yes / — | A group (`kind: 'group'`) or a row's details (`kind: 'detail'`) open or close. |
| `onCopying / onPasting` | `{ text, html, rows }` / `{ text, rowIndex, field }` | yes | Ctrl+C, `copy()`; Ctrl+V, `paste()`: change the text, or stop it. |
| `onSummaryChanged` | `{ total, editing }` |  | The summary values were worked out again: new rows, a new filter or search, a save, or (with `recalculateWhileEditing`) an unsaved change. |
| `onExporting / onExported` | `{ format, component, selectedRowsOnly, options }` / `{ format, rows, text? }` | yes / — | An export is about to start (change its options); for a format the grid does not write (`xlsx`) the handler writes it with `exportDataGrid`. It finished (`exportDataGrid` tells it with `format: 'xlsx'`). |
| `onContextMenuPreparing` | `{ target, field, row?, rowIndex, items }` | yes | A header’s column menu (`header`) or a row’s menu (`row`: a right click or the context menu key; `items` hold the row’s actions, and it opens only when it has items) is about to open: change `items`. |
| `onActionRunning / onActionRan` | `{ action, rows, selection, location }` / `{ action, rows, location, done, failed, canceled, errors }` | yes / — | An action is about to run; it ran. See [Row actions](datagrid-editing.md#actions). |
| `onToolbarPreparing` | `{ items }` |  | The toolbar is laid out: change the list of items it takes. |

## Example files

`Toolbar.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, type GridToolbarItem, type GridToolbarItemName } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

/** The toolbar: the grid's own items with items of the page's own, at the start and at the end. */
export default function Toolbar() {
  const s = reactive({ striped: true, exportText: false, refreshed: 0 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const items: (GridToolbarItem | GridToolbarItemName)[] = [
    { name: 'refresh', text: 'Refresh', hint: () => `Refreshed ${s.refreshed} times`, location: 'before', click: () => (grid?.refresh(), s.refreshed++) },
    { name: 'striped', location: 'before', content: () => <CheckBox label="Striped" x-model={() => s.striped} /> },
    { name: 'exportText', location: 'before', content: () => <CheckBox label="“Export” with its text" x-model={() => s.exportText} /> },
    'addRowButton',
    { name: 'exportButton', showText: () => (s.exportText ? 'always' : 'inMenu') },
    'columnChooserButton',
    'searchPanel',
  ];

  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-toolbar"
      style="block-size: 30rem"
      rows={makeOrders(120)}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={columns}
      label="Orders with a toolbar"
      locale="en"
      newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
      settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, exportButton: true, columnChooserButton: true, searchPanel: true, striped: () => s.striped }}
      toolbar={{ items }}
      ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
    />
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` made-up orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`order.ts`

`RuntimeColumns.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

/** Columns added, taken out and changed while the grid shows; the layout, the sort and the filters follow. */
export default function RuntimeColumns() {
  const s = reactive({ paid: false, city: true, fields: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  const show = () => (s.fields = grid ? `${grid.columnCount()} columns, shown: ${grid.getVisibleColumns().map((c) => c.field).join(', ')}` : '');

  const togglePaid = () => {
    if (!grid) return;
    if (s.paid) grid.deleteColumn('paid');
    else grid.addColumn({ field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80, headerFilter: true }, 2);
    s.paid = !s.paid;
  };
  const toggleCity = () => {
    if (!grid) return;
    if (s.city) grid.deleteColumn('city');
    else grid.addColumn(filterColumns.find((c) => c.field === 'city')!, 2);
    s.city = !s.city;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text={() => (s.paid ? 'Take “Paid” out' : 'Add “Paid” after Customer')} variant="outline" onclick={togglePaid} />
        <Button text={() => (s.city ? 'Take “City” out' : 'Put “City” back')} variant="outline" onclick={toggleCity} />
        <Button text="Amount in euros" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('amount', { title: 'Amount (€)', format: (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'number' ? euros.format(v) : '') })} />
        <Button text="Hide or show “Note”" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('note', 'visible', !grid.columnOption('note', 'visible'))} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-runtime-columns"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns.filter((c) => c.field !== 'paid')}
        label="Orders with columns that change"
        locale="en"
        onOptionChanged={() => show()}
        onContentReady={() => show()}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-runtime-fields">{() => s.fields}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`KeepLayout.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Widths, order, sort and filters kept under `layoutKey`; a grid made again gets them back. */
export default function KeepLayout() {
  const s = reactive({ keep: true, shown: true });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const makeAgain = () => {
    s.shown = false;
    setTimeout(() => (s.shown = true), 0);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Keep the layout" x-model={() => s.keep} />
        <Button text="Make the grid again" variant="outline" onclick={makeAgain} />
        <Button text="Reset the layout" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.resetLayout()} />
      </Stack>
      {s.shown && (
        <DataGrid
          class="dg-layout"
          style="block-size: 28rem"
          rows={makeOrders(40)}
          rowKey="id"
          columns={filterColumns}
          label="Orders that keep their layout"
          locale="en"
          layoutKey="docs-orders"
          settings={{ saveLayout: () => s.keep }}
          ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';

          resizable: () => s.resizable,
          resizeMode: () => (s.nextColumn ? 'nextColumn' : 'widget'),
          movable: () => s.movable,
          pinnable: () => s.pinnable,
          menu: () => s.menu,
          tooltips: () => s.tooltips,
          rowCount: () => s.rowCount,
```

`Events.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The grid's events: amounts over 900 in bold, a row menu of the page's own, no "Cancelled" saved, and a log of what happened. */
export default function Events() {
  const s = reactive({ log: [] as { id: number; text: string }[] });
  let next = 0;
  const log = (text: string) => {
    s.log.unshift({ id: ++next, text });
    if (s.log.length > 5) s.log.pop();
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-events"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders with events"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true }}
        onCellPrepared={(e) => {
          // The cell is reused for other rows: set and clear.
          if (e.field === 'amount') e.element.style.fontWeight = (e.value as number) > 900 ? 'bold' : '';
        }}
        onContextMenuPreparing={(e) => {
          if (e.target === 'row' && e.row) e.items.push({ text: `Log order ${e.row.id}`, click: () => log(`Order ${e.row!.id} from the row menu`) });
        }}
        onRowUpdating={(e) => {
          if (e.changes.status === 'Cancelled') {
            e.cancel = true;
            log(`Order ${e.key}: cancelling is not saved here`);
          }
        }}
        onRowUpdated={(e) => log(`Order ${e.key} saved: ${Object.keys(e.changes).join(', ')}`)}
        onFocusedRowChanged={(e) => e.key !== undefined && log(`Row ${e.key}`)}
        onSortChanged={(e) => log(`Sorted: ${e.sort.map((x) => `${x.field} ${x.dir}`).join(', ') || 'none'}`)}
      />
      <ol class="dg-events-log" aria-label="What happened" aria-live="polite">
        {s.log.map((entry) => (
          <li key={entry.id}>{entry.text}</li>
        ))}
      </ol>
    </>
  );
}
```
